title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
It’s a hot summer. The mother duck is looking at her {{1}} . She is very happy, and she is waiting.
“Quack! Quack!” the baby ducklings (鸭子) come out one by one. But the biggest egg is still there. At last, the duckling comes out. This duckling is very {{2}} and ugly (丑的), so they all call him “the ugly duckling”.
The ugly duckling is lonely (孤独的). No one {{3}} him. His brothers and sisters don’t want to play with him. The other ducklings say to their mother, “He is so ugly. He is not your child.” The mother duck is very {{4}} . The ugly duckling cries, then he goes away (离开).
He walks and walks. Then he sees a small house. In the house, there is an old woman and a dog.
The ugly duckling asks “Can {{5}} stay here?” The old woman says, “OK. Come in.” But the dog doesn’t like him. So he goes away again.
Autumn comes, and the leaves (树叶) turn yellow. One evening, the ugly duckling sees a lot of beautiful birds. “Swans (天鹅)!” he {{6}} , “How beautiful! ” He looks at himself and cries, “I’m so ugly.”
Winter comes, the ugly duckling is very cold and hungry. A farmer sees him and takes him home. {{7}} the farmer’s son and wife don’t like him. They drive (驱赶) him away. The ugly duckling is very sad. He goes away again.
Spring comes, and it’s sunny and warm. One day, the ugly duckling {{8}} many beautiful swans. He says, “Nice to meet you.” The swan says, “Nice to meet you, beautiful swan.” He looks at the water.
He sees a beautiful swan. He is very happy. He shouts (喊), “I am a swan!”

blanks.mean: 鸭妈妈正在看她孵的蛋。
blanks.why: 根据下文“But the biggest egg is still there.”可知, 最大蛋里的小鸭子还没有出来, 所以此处是指鸭妈妈看着她孵的蛋。故选B。

blanks.mean: 这只小鸭子又大又丑, 所以他们都叫他“丑小鸭”。
blanks.why: 根据上文“But the biggest egg is still there. At last, the duckling comes out.”可知, 从最大的鸭蛋里出来的小鸭子当然是个子大。故选D。

blanks.mean: 没有人爱他。
blanks.why: 根据下文“His brothers and sisters don’t want to play with him.”可知, 他的兄弟姐妹都不想与他一起玩, 说明他们不爱他。故选A。

blanks.mean: 鸭妈妈很伤心。
blanks.gloss: sad伤心的；kind友好的；clever聪明的；cute可爱的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“The other ducklings say to their mother, ‘He is so ugly. He is not your child.’”可知, 其他鸭子对鸭妈妈说他很丑, 不是她的孩子, 这些话让鸭妈妈感到很伤心。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我可以住在这里吗? he他；you你；they他们；I我。
blanks.why: 根据“The ugly duckling asks,”可知, 丑小鸭在询问他是否可住在这里。故选D。

blanks.mean: “天鹅！
blanks.gloss: ”他说, “多美啊！” tells告诉；talks交谈；says“说”, 后接具体内容；speaks“说”, 后常接语言。
blanks.why: 根据“How beautiful!”可知, “多美啊！”是说的内容, 用says。故选C。

blanks.mean: 但是农夫的儿子和妻子不喜欢他。
blanks.gloss: And和, 又；But但是；Or或者；So所以。
blanks.why: 上文“A farmer sees him and takes him home.（一个农民看到了他, 把他带回家。）”和下文“the farmer’s son and wife don’t like him.（农夫的儿子和妻子不喜欢他。）”是转折关系, 应用but来连接两句。故选B。

blanks.mean: 一天, 丑小鸭遇到了许多美丽的天鹅。
blanks.why: 根据下文“He says, ‘Nice to meet you.’ The swan says, ‘Nice to meet you, beautiful swan.’”可知, 丑小鸭与天鹅打招呼问候, 说明他们相遇了。故选C。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

One afternoon, our teacher, Mrs. Hughes, told us that The Wizard of Oz would be our class’s next play. It’s my favorite story. In the past, I was too shy (腼腆的) to try out for school {{1}} . But I love the Cowardly Lion so much that I signed up (报名) for tryouts.
The next day, I brought home a short script (剧本) to {{2}} . As the Lion, I must jump out and roar (吼叫) at Dorothy. My older brother, Michael, heard me and laughed.
“Annie, you sound more like a cute cat than a strong lion,” he said. He let out a big roar. We practiced (练习) being lions until dinner.
For the next few days, I came home and practiced until I no longer needed the script. I was ready for it.
Tryout day arrived. I was {{3}} before I saw how well my classmates did. But when I stood up in front of the class, my shyness returned, and I went wrong with my lines. {{4}} , another student got the part, and I had to play Auntie Em.
I came home in tears. “I wanted to be the Lion and now I have to be Auntie Em,” I told Mom. “I want to {{5}} playing.”
“Annie, sometimes we have to do things we don’t {{6}} to do,” Mom said. “You can’t be the Lion, but you can still try to be the best Auntie Em.”
I decided to listen to Mom. I asked Michael for help, and we practiced every day after school until the play night. When I entered the hall, I was still {{7}} , but I remembered Mom’s words. My voice was clear and strong. When all of us finished, people {{8}} .
Mrs. Hughes walked over and said, “Annie, you were a great Auntie Em. I know you didn’t want that part, but you really made the best of it.”
I can’t wait to try out for next year’s play!

blanks.mean: 过去, 我太腼腆了, 不敢参加学校的戏剧表演。
blanks.why: 根据上文“One afternoon, our teacher, Mrs. Hughes, told us that The Wizard of Oz would be our class’s next play.”可知, 此处指戏剧。故选C。

blanks.mean: 第二天, 我带回家一个简短的剧本来记忆。
blanks.why: 根据下文“For the next few days, I came home and practiced until I no longer needed the script.”可知, 此处指记剧本。故选D。

blanks.mean: 在我看到我的同学们做得这么好之前, 我很放松。
blanks.gloss: relaxed放松的；careful仔细的；worried担心的；unhappy不高兴的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“But when I stood up in front of the class, my shyness returned, and I went wrong with my lines.”可知, 此处句意发生了转折, 表示作者感觉轻松。故选A。

blanks.mean: 不幸的是, 另一个学生得到了这个角色, 我不得不扮演埃姆婶婶。
blanks.gloss: Successfully成功地；Hopefully有希望地；Unluckily不幸的是；Uncomfortably不舒服地。
blanks.why: 根据“another student got the part, and I had to play Auntie Em”可知, 作者没有得到自己想要出演的角色, 所以此处表示的是不幸的事情。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我想停止表演。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Annie, sometimes we have to do things we don’t…to do”可知, 此处表示作者不想参加表演。故选D。

blanks.mean: “安妮, 有时候我们不得不做我们不喜欢做的事情, ”妈妈说。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I wanted to be the Lion, and now I have to be Auntie Em”可知, 此处指有时候我们不得不做我们不喜欢做的事情。故选B。

blanks.mean: 当我走进大厅时, 我仍然很害怕, 但我想起了妈妈的话。
blanks.gloss: afraid害怕的；bored无聊的；sad伤心的；angry愤怒的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“my shyness returned”可知, 作者感到害怕。故选A。

blanks.mean: 当我们所有人都结束时, 人们欢呼起来。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Annie, you were a great Auntie Em. I know you didn’t want that part, but you really made the best of it.”可知, 演出非常成功, 所以此处表示人们欢呼起来。故选D。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

Sally is good at making things. In the new term, she wants to make a {{1}} for the school’s race (车赛). So she asks her dad for help. “Well,” her father says, “You can read some books and do some research (研究) first and then come back to {{2}} with a picture of go-kart.”
It takes Sally a week to design (设计) her go-kart. Then she brings her notes and picture to her dad. She names it “Blue Lightning”. Her dad looks over her work. “Well, that’s {{3}} !” he says, “Have a try. Just let the Blue Lightning walk out of your design.”
Over three weekends of hard work, Sally turns her picture into a real, working go-kart and paints it light blue. Her dad asks her to {{4}} it for a test. Sally is very happy to sit in the go-kart.
Then she drives it back to her dad. “Well,” she says, “Now I know why you want me to have a test drive.”
“Oh, do you know?” he says, “Please {{5}} the problems (问题) with me.”
“In the test, I drive my go-kart fast on the road, but it is difficult to speed up (加速),” she says, “There is something wrong with its shape (形状).”
“Very good!” her dad says. Sally looks a little {{6}} with her dad. She asks, “Why not tell me about it before the test drive?”
Her dad says, “Because I want you to {{7}} out the problems by yourself. We need to keep doing the same tings many times and solving (解决) the problems along the way.”
With her dad’s help, Sally {{8}} on the go-kart even harder (更努力). She has the test drives again and again. Finally she goes to the race with her go-kart and wins the first place.

blanks.mean: 在新学期, 她想为学校的比赛制作一辆卡丁车。
blanks.why: 根据下文“for the school’s race (车赛)”可知, 需要有一台卡丁车才能参加车赛。故选B。

blanks.mean: 你可以先阅读一些书籍, 研究一下, 然后带着一张卡丁车的图片回来找我。
blanks.why: 根据上文“So she asks her dad for help”可知, Sally向父亲求助, 父亲让她自己先做研究, 设计好赛车之后再去找他, 此处为父亲第一人称口吻, 故应用人称代词宾格me。故选D。

blanks.mean: 嗯, 太棒了! great棒极了；free空闲的；right正确的；late迟的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Have a try. Just let the Blue Lightning walk out of your design”可知, 父亲认可了Sally的设计, 并决定将其设计实现。故选A。

blanks.mean: 她父亲让她开着卡丁车去做测试。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Now I know why you want me to have a test drive”可知, Sally的父亲让她驾驶着卡丁车去做测试。故选A。

blanks.mean: 请和我分享一下你发现的这些问题。
blanks.why: 根据下文“There is something wrong with its shape (形状)”可知, 父亲让Sally分享一下自己测试卡丁车过程中发现的问题。故选D。

blanks.mean: Sally看起来有点生她爸爸的气。
blanks.gloss: happy快乐的；lovely可爱的；angry生气的；kind好心的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Why not tell me about it before the test drive?”可知, Sally有些生气父亲在测试之前没有给她指出卡丁车存在的问题。故选C。

blanks.mean: 因为我想让你自己发现问题。
blanks.why: find out the problems为固定搭配, 意为“发现问题”, 符合句意, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 在爸爸的帮助下, Sally更加努力地钻研这台卡丁车。
blanks.why: 根据下文“She has the test drives again and again”可知, 在爸爸的帮助下, Sally更加努力地钻研这台卡丁车。work on意为“从事……工作”, 符合句意, 故选C。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
Emma is not happy today. It’s her birthday but no one in her {{1}} says happy birthday to her. They are all busy with the surprise party for Mr. Stinton, their Chinese teacher.
Mr. Stinton is very nice. He knows every student’s {{2}} and often makes cards and cookies for them on their birthdays. He doesn’t like his students to {{3}} presents for him, so Emma and her classmates make a big card and some cookies for him. It takes them a long time to {{4}} the party. They want Mr. Stinton to be happy.
It’s 7:30 pm. Mrs. Bowman, the music teacher, is in the classroom with these students. “I’ll call Mr. Stinton,” she says. “Emma, can you turn off the lights?”
Mrs. Bowman {{5}} Mr. Stinton and says the lights in the classroom don’t work.
When Mr. Stinton gets to the {{6}} , Emma turns on the lights. Everyone says, “Surprise!”
“A party for me?” Mr. Stinton asks. He sees the big card and says, “This card is cool! I like it.”
Then he goes to Emma and says, “I have a birthday card for you, but it looks {{7}} now.” And he also gives Emma some cookies. “Happy Birthday, Emma. I’m happy we have the {{8}} birthday,” he says.
“Happy Birthday, Emma,” her classmates say.
Emma is really happy.

blanks.mean: 今天是她的生日, 但班上没有人对她说生日快乐。
blanks.why: 根据下文“They are all busy with the surprise party for Mr. Stinton, their Chinese teacher.”可知, 此处指班上没有人对她说生日快乐, 他们都为给老师准备惊喜派对忙碌着。故选D。

blanks.mean: 他知道每个学生的生日, 经常在他们生日时给他们做卡片和饼干。
blanks.gloss: number数字；birthday生日；hobby 爱好；name名字。
blanks.why: 根据“often makes cards and cookies for them on their birthdays”可知, 此处指生日。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他不喜欢他的学生给他买礼物, 所以Emma和她的同学给他做了一张大卡片和一些饼干。
blanks.why: 根据“so Emma and her classmates make a big card and some cookies for him”并结合选项可知, 此处指Stinton老师不喜欢他的学生给他买礼物。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他们花了很长时间来计划派对。
blanks.why: 根据下文“They want Mr. Stinton to be happy.”可知, 此处指计划派对。故选A。

blanks.mean: Bowman夫人打电话给Stinton老师, 说教室里的灯坏了。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I’ll call Mr. Stinton”可知, 此处指打电话。故选C。 18题详解】 句意：当Stinton老师到达教室时, Emma打开了灯。 garden花园；classroom教室；library图书馆；playground操场。根据上文“Mrs. Bowman…Mr. Stinton and says the lights in the classroom don’t work.”可知, 此处指Stinton老师到达教室。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我有一张生日卡给你, 但现在看起来很小。
blanks.gloss: clean干净的；useful有用的；special特殊的；small小的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“so Emma and her classmates make a big card and some cookies for him”以及空前的“but”可知, 此处句意发生了转折, 表示给Emma的生日卡现在看起来很小。故选D。

blanks.mean: “生日快乐, Emma。
blanks.why: 根据上文“It’s her birthday”以及“They are all busy with the surprise party for Mr. Stinton, their Chinese teacher.”可知, Stinton老师和Emma的生日是同一天。故选C。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Pedro is walking in a park. He {{1}} a watch under a big tree. It goes well and looks nice. “Whose watch is it?” Pedro says to himself.
He looks around the {{2}} . A girl and her father are taking photos at the lake. A woman is sitting on the grass. Nobody finds that Pedro picks up the watch.
“The watch looks so {{3}} .” Pedro thinks. “I really {{4}} this nice watch. I don’t need to ask Jack about {{5}} if I have one.” Again, he looks around carefully. “No one {{6}} me...” Pedro doesn’t do anything, but his face turns red.
“Don’t {{7}} other people’s things.” Pedro thinks of his mother’s words. “I will not be {{8}} if I take this watch,” Pedro says to himself.
At last, he thinks he should find the owner (主人) of the watch.

blanks.mean: 他在一棵大树下发现一块手表。
blanks.why: 根据“Whose watch is it?”可知, 他在一棵大树下发现一块手表。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他在公园四处看。
blanks.why: 根据“Pedro is walking in a park.”可知, Pedro在公园里四处看。故选A。

blanks.mean: 手表看起来很漂亮。
blanks.why: 根据“nice watch”可知, 手表很漂亮。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我真的很喜欢这块表。
blanks.why: 根据“nice watch”和“I take this watch”可知, Pedro很喜欢这块表。故选A。

blanks.mean: 如果我拥有它的话, 我就不需要问Jack时间了。
blanks.why: 根据“I don’t need to ask Jack about”和常识可知, 手表是用来看时间的。故选D。

blanks.mean: 没有人看见我…… loves爱；teaches教导；calls打电话；sees看见。
blanks.why: 根据“Again, he looks around carefully.”可知, 此处指没人看见Pedro在做什么。故选D。

blanks.mean: 不要拿其他人的东西。
blanks.why: 根据“if I take this watch”可知, 此处指“拿别人的东西”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 如果我拿了这块手表, 我不会快乐的。
blanks.gloss: worried担忧的；angry生气的；happy快乐的；sorry遗憾的。
blanks.why: 根据“At last, he thinks he should find the owner of the watch.”可知, Pedro认为拿这块表是不对的。故选C。

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:
The teacher stood before his class and was ready to give the final test paper to students. “I know how hard you worked to {{1}} for this test,” he said. “But if you choose not to take the test, you can still get a B.”
Many students jumped up {{2}} to thank the teacher and left the classroom. The teacher looked at the other students and said, “Does anybody else want to get a B? This is the last {{3}} I ask this question.” Two more students decided to go.
Finally, seven students {{4}} at their seats. The teacher then handed out the paper to them. There were only three sentences on the paper: Congratulations (祝贺)! You got an A in this class. Keep believing in yourself.
I never had a teacher like that but I think it is a {{5}} that any teacher could and should give. Students who do not have confidence (自信) are B students at most.
The same is {{6}} for students in real life. The A students usually believe in themselves. They learn life’s lessons, from study or from everyday life, and {{7}} better people.
We should know that we have some limits (局限性). However, we should also know that doesn’t mean we can’t do anything or learn to be anyone. Sir Edmund Hillary, the first person to reach the top of Mount Everest said, “It’s not the mountain we {{8}} over but ourselves.”

blanks.mean: “我知道你为准备这次考试付出了多大的努力, ”他说。
blanks.why: 结合空后“for this test”和备选词汇可知, 此处是指准备考试, 考查prepare for“为……做准备”, 动词短语。故选A。

blanks.mean: 许多学生迅速地跳起来感谢老师, 然后离开了教室。
blanks.gloss: unhappily不开心地；carefully细心地；quickly迅速地；rudely无礼地。
blanks.why: 结合“left the classroom”和备选词汇可知, 此处是指一些学生迅速地跳起来, 然后离开了教室。故选C。

blanks.mean: 这是我最后一次问这个问题。
blanks.why: 结合语境和备选词汇可知, 此处是指老师最后一次询问这个问题。故选B。

blanks.mean: 最后, 7名学生留在了座位上。
blanks.why: 结合下文“The teacher then handed out the paper to them.”和备选词汇可知, 此处是指7个学生留在了座位上。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我从来没有遇到过这样的老师, 但我认为这是任何老师都可以而且应该进行的测试。
blanks.why: 根据上文“The teacher stood before his class and was ready to give the final test paper to students.”可知, 此处是指一次测试。故选C。

blanks.mean: 现实生活中学生也是如此。
blanks.gloss: true真实的, 确实的；wrong错误的；new新的；strange奇怪的。
blanks.why: 结合下文“The A students usually believe in themselves. They learn life’s lessons, from study or from everyday life,”和备选词汇可知, 此处是指现实生活中的学生也确实是这样的。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他们从学习或日常生活中吸取教训, 成为更好的人。
blanks.why: 根据上文“They learn life’s lessons, from study or from everyday life,”可知, 此处是指他们成为更好的人。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我们要翻越的不是高山, 而是我们自己。
blanks.why: 结合空前“the mountain”和备选词汇可知, 此处是指翻越这座山, 考查climb over“翻越”, 动词短语。故选B。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
After school, Carol and her younger sister Amy went to see the new seat arrangements (安排) for the school band on the wall. Almost right away Carol {{1}} Amy’s name. Amy, Concert Mistress, leader of the whole band? No way!
Carol kept reading. What? She wasn’t even in the first violin section?
“I can’t believe I’m the Concert Mistress!” Amy shouted excitedly. “I can’t, either!” Carol said unhappily. “Mr Benson must have made a {{2}} . I should be in the first violins this summer, not you!”
Amy’s face hardened. “No, he didn’t. Carol, I practiced more!” Then she turned and walked away. Carol didn’t mean to hurt Amy. But what would her friends say if her younger sister had a better {{3}} than she did?
The next morning, Carol went straight to the music room. “Mr Benson, I want to talk to you about the band seats.”
“Carol, congratulations to both you and Amy. I believe you must be {{4}} of your sister.” Mr Benson smiled, “If she keeps working hard like this, I think she will become a great musician! Carol froze. She realized there wasn’t any mistake.
Carol went down the hall with {{5}} steps. She thought of her life full of softball, classes, and friends, so full that she didn’t always practice her violin. But Amy played every day.
When school was over, Carol waited for Amy at the school gate.
“Hey,” Carol greeted when she saw Amy. “It’s great you’re Concert Mistress.”
“Do you really {{6}} that?”
“Yeah,” Carol paused. “I’m sorry. I guess I was kind of jealous (嫉妒).”
“Jealous?” Amy was {{7}} . “But you’re popular, Carol. You get better grades. You’re better at sports. You can do everything.”
Carol shook her head. “I can’t play the violin as beautifully as you can.”
“I can help you.” Amy smiled. “But you have to help me with my math.”
Carol’s eyes lit up, “By the time we’re through, you’ll be a math queen.”
Amy {{8}} , “And you’ll be the next Concert Mistress!”
They hugged each other and the bond between them grew even stronger.

blanks.mean: 卡罗尔几乎立刻就注意到了艾米的名字。
blanks.why: 根据“Amy, Concert Mistress, leader of the whole band?”可知, 此处表示她看到了艾米的名字, 故选B。 24题详解】 句意：班森先生一定弄错了。 difference差异；wish希望；plan计划；mistake错误。根据“I should be in the first violins this summer, not you!”可知, 卡罗尔认为班森先生弄错了, make a mistake“出错, 弄错”, 故选D。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
Christopher Nguyen is a talented (有天赋的) piano player from Alameda, California, US.
He enjoys playing the piano and is very {{1}} at it. Christopher likes to share his music. Every week after school on Friday afternoons, Christopher {{2}} the old people’s home, a place for the elders to spend time together.
At the old people’s home, the elders usually like to read newspapers and watch TV after {{3}} . When Christopher comes to play the piano for them, they all {{4}} what they are doing to listen. Christopher likes making people happy. He looks at people’s faces to see how they are feeling, and then he plays a song and he thinks it will make them feel good.
Christopher can play all kinds of music, so he can always {{5}} something that everyone likes. When he plays, the elders usually smile, and sometimes they cry. Mary Kelly, an elder from the old people’s home says, “We all know him and we all look forward to him playing every Friday.”
Christopher is usually a very shy (害羞的) person. He doesn’t like to {{6}} in front of his classmates at school. But he doesn’t feel shy when he plays the piano. He feels {{7}} to share his talent with others. Christopher knows that his {{8}} makes them happy, and that makes him happy too. “I enjoy putting a smile on people’s faces.” Christopher said.

blanks.mean: 他喜欢弹钢琴而且非常擅长弹钢琴。

blanks.why: 根据并列部分“He enjoys playing the piano”可知此处指他擅长弹钢琴, 故选B。

blanks.why: 根据上文“Christopher is usually a very shy person”可知, 他不喜欢同学面前讲话, 故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“But he doesn’t feel shy when he plays the piano”可以推测, 在和他人分享音乐才华时他感到兴奋, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 克里斯托弗知道他的音乐让他们开心, 这也让他开心。

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
Luis’s whole family met every June to celebrate Grandpa’s birthday. Before everyone sat down to eat, each person had to tell a personal story they had about {{1}} . Some family members told the same story year after year. Luis, for example, had his usual story about the time Grandpa taught him how to take care of a vegetable garden.
The stories were a {{2}} . And now that most of the grandchildren were old enough to {{3}} , the tradition could go on for quite a while. Last year, it took three hours. Luis tried hard not to yawn(打哈欠) as he listened to all the same old stories.
This year, Uncle Frank and Aunt Teresa had dinner ready early and called everyone to eat.
“What about the {{4}} ?” Luis asked.
“There’s just not enough time this year, with so many people,” Uncle Frank said.
After hearing this, Luis felt relieved(如释重负). But he also felt a little {{5}} as he sat down at the long dining table. Without the tradition, Grandpa’s birthday felt like any other holiday the family shared.
Luis eyed the plate of vegetable salad. “You know, I wouldn’t know how to pick a tomato right if it wasn’t for Grandpa,” he said softly.
“I wouldn’t know {{6}} to drive a car,” said Aunt Teresa.
“I wouldn’t know how to turn a paperclip into a safety pin,” added Uncle Felix. “That sure saved the day at Edna’s wedding(婚礼)!” Everyone laughed and smiled at each other at the reminder of that well-known family story.
It was a {{7}} birthday. Conversations flowed like water, and the food was wonderful. But something told Luis that next year, the tradition of telling stories would {{8}} .

blanks.why: 根据“Luis, for example, had his usual story about the time Grandpa taught him how to take care of a vegetable garden. 例如, 路易斯经常讲爷爷教他如何照料菜园的故事。”可知是讲关于爷爷的故事, 故选B。
根据：“the tradition could go on for quite a while这一传统可能会延续很长一段时间。”, 故选A。
结合前文是指讲故事, 那么孙女孙儿长大应该是参加这一传统, 故选C。
结合上文这里是指“上文讲故事”, 故选D。
根据“Without the tradition, Grandpa’s birthday felt like any other holiday the family shared. 没有这个传统, 爷爷的生日感觉就像家人共享的其他节日一样。”, 又注意到“but”表转折, A. thankful 感恩的；B. excited激动的；C. afraid害怕的；D. sad伤心的, 故选D。
结合句意, 故选A.
根据：“Conversations flowed like water, and the food was wonderful谈话像流水一样流动, 食物也很美味。”, 可知生日是美好的, A. bad坏的；B. boring无聊的；C. great很好的；D. small气味, 问。故选C。
考查动词辨析。句意：“但有些事情路易斯说的那样, 明年讲故事的传统将会回归。”, A. stop停止；B. return回, 返回, 归还；C. help帮助；D. lose丢失, 故选B。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship

Jimmy was good at everything. He was a good athlete. He was good at music. He did well in school. I couldn’t {{1}} the fact that he was always first in everything he did.
So when I heard that there was going to be a soapbox race, I thought, “This is my chance to {{2}} him to be more humble.”
Everyone worked hard all week to build the best race car. The day of the race, I saw his racer. Of course, it was beautiful. It was red and had a big flame on the side. It was smooth and had wheels that looked very expensive.
I was so upset and {{3}} that I did something I should not have. When he wasn’t looking I kicked one of his expensive {{4}} . “Now let’s see who wins!” I thought.
I got back in my racer and waited for the race to start.
BANG!
We were off slowly at first, and then faster as we picked up {{5}} going down the hill.
Jimmy and I were both pulling away from the pack
Suddenly, his wheel started to wobble badly, and then it came off! He started to swerve! I realized I had made his racer dangerous. He couldn’t steer it as we approached the big turn at the bottom of the hill!
The race was {{6}} to win, but I realized that I could not win this way, no matter how much I disliked Jimmy. I hit the brake and grabbed his cart to keep it beside me.
I had to steer and brake for both of us. We stopped just before the edge of the road, and the other racers {{7}} past us.
“Jimmy,” I said, “I kicked your wheel because I could not stand to see you win again. I’m sorry.”
It was {{8}} to admit what I had done, but Jimmy forgave me and we eventually became good friends. I realized that winning isn’t everything, and so did Jimmy.

blanks.mean: 我不能接受这样的事实, 他做任何事都是第一。
blanks.why: 根据倒数第二段“because I could not stand to see you win again. I’m sorry.”可知, 这里说的是不能接受这样的事实。故选A。

blanks.mean: 这是我教他更谦虚的机会。
blanks.why: 上文说不能接受吉米任何事都是第一, 所以此处想表达的是教他该怎样谦虚。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我非常沮丧和生气, 我做了一些我不应该做的事情。
blanks.gloss: angry生气的；tired疲倦的；sad难过的；nervous紧张不安的。
blanks.why: 根据“that I did something I should not have.”可知, 是在生气的情况下做了不该做的事情。故选A。

blanks.mean: 当他不注意的时候, 我踢了他的一个昂贵的轮子。
blanks.why: 根据上文“It was smooth and had wheels that looked very expensive.”可知, 是昂贵的轮子。故选D。

blanks.mean: 开始我们走得很慢, 然后随着下山速度的加快, 速度越来越快。
blanks.gloss: race竞赛；power力量；speed速度；time时间pick up speed“加快速度”, 固定搭配。
blanks.why: 故选C。

blanks.mean: 这场比赛本该是我赢的, 但我意识到我不可能以这种方式赢, 不管我有多不喜欢吉米。
blanks.why: 根据“but I realized that I could not win this way”可知, 表示比赛本该是我赢的。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我们在路边停了下来, 其他选手从我们身边飞驰而过。
blanks.why: 根据“and the other racers...past us.”可知, fly past“掠过”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 承认我的所作所为很难, 但吉米原谅了我, 我们最终成为了好朋友。
blanks.gloss: easy容易的；relaxing令人放松的；difficult困难的；boring无聊的。
blanks.why: 根据“It was...to admit what I had done”可知, 这里表示承认自己的错误很难。故选C。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
There are two children in my family. I am three years younger than my {{1}} , Emily. I think she is great. I like to play with her and her friends. But they don’t like that. Over time, there is a distance (距离) between us although (虽然) we live in the same {{2}} .
When she says she’s going to China, I’m not so sad. But after she leaves, I feel that my life is so different. I cry sadly. But as the night falls, my tears (眼泪) turn into tears of calm (冷静), tears of {{3}} beginnings—I start to do something.
I pick up the phone. “Hello?”
“Hey, Emily. It’s me. Sara. I’m just calling to tell you I love you.” My words come out quickly. I know that if I stop in the middle, I won’t {{4}} them. “I know we aren’t as close as some sisters, {{5}} that doesn’t mean I don’t love you.”
After a long time, she says, “Your words make me feel you are by my side. I love you, too.”
I never feel so great to have Emily as my sister. I’m hoping to see {{6}} back home this December.

blanks.mean: 我不会说的。

title: A Family Lesson
text:

When she gets {{6}} , she says, “Who can help to make fruit salad?” Her daughters all say, “Sorry, Mom, we are not {{7}} .” {{8}} she makes the salad, she says to them, “Who wants to eat the salad?” “I will, Mom!” They all say. “No, you can’t {{9}} you don’t do anything before I make the salad. You must {{10}} ‘No pains, no gains(不劳无获)’ . ” Then she eats the salad herself.

title: An Important Lesson at School

On weekends, I have to clean my room and wash my clothes in the morning. Then I have to {{4}} English books. Later in the afternoon I have to go to the Children’s Palace to {{5}} how to play the piano. In the {{6}} , I have to play the piano for one hour. After that, I can go to bed. Yours,
Susan

Every time Mary picks it up and says to her. “Grandma, let me {{3}} you put it back on your foot.” “Thank you, my girl. You are so beautiful.” the old woman says to her when Mary helps her. The old woman feels warm in her heart and smiles.
In the old people’s home, Mary meets an old man, too. He has no legs. He often says “Hi” to Mary. Every time Mary stops to talk with him happily. And she listens to him tell his {{4}} . Mary doesn’t think the stories are funny, but she smiles all the time and listens carefully. “Thanks for your listening, my girl. You are so beautiful.” he says to Mary after telling.
The old woman and old man say Mary is a beautiful girl to her. This makes Mary very {{5}} . She thinks she doesn’t do any special things in that old people’s home, but she feels she gets something special. She thinks her looks are not important.
Give your {{6}} to others, and you will feel you are sparkling (闪闪发光的).

Finding the class having a heated discussion, Mrs. Klein was in {{6}} . She almost forgot Douglas. When she had the others at work on another project, she bent over Douglas’s desk and asked him whose hand it was.
Douglas said in a low voice, “It’s yours, Mrs. Klein.”

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
I’m good in school. I do my work and study a lot, but I have a bad habit (习惯) of {{1}} things.
Last summer, I was on holiday with my family at the beach. On the first day, my father gave me a watch because I had lost one the year before. “You need a watch, so {{2}} this one,” he said.
The next day, I went swimming. The sun was shining on the water. The water was warm and beautiful. I really enjoyed being in the water.
When I returned to the {{3}} I was very tired so I lay down. At that moment, I wanted to see what time it was and I {{4}} my watch. But it was gone! I searched all afternoon, but I couldn’t find it.
The night at dinner, I arrived with my sleeves (袖子) pulled down, hoping {{5}} would notice that I didn’t have my watch.
My sister asked, “What time is it?”
“Ask Tom,” my mother said. “He has a good watch.”
Dad looked at me and said, “Don’t tell me that you lost your watch again!”
“No!” I said. I was very {{6}} . I knew that they would find out that I told a terrible lie. Just then, there was an announcement (广播通知): “Ladies and gentlemen, a very nice watch was found on the beach today. If you lost one and can identify (认出) it, please come to the front desk.”
I knew what I had to do. I ran to the desk {{7}} . There it was. The watch was all right. It was still working.
I walked back to the table and sat down. Everyone looked worried, but then my dad {{8}} . He knew that I finally learned my lesson.

blanks.why: 根据空前“a bad habit”可知, 应是丢东西的坏习惯。故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
The Read family come to a new big city. Mrs. Read’s son, Bob, is not happy. He doesn’t have anyone to play with. “Don’t worry!” says his mother. “You will soon make {{1}} here.”
One morning, there is a knock at the door. Bob’s mother, Mrs. Read, {{2}} it. There stands a woman with round glasses. It is Mrs. Miller. She comes to borrow some eggs. She wants to make cakes. Mrs. Read gives her two. In the afternoon, there is another knock at the door. Mrs. Read opens it and she sees a {{3}} standing there. “My name is Jack Miller,” he says. “My mother sends you this {{4}} and two eggs.” “Well, thank you, Jack,” says Mrs. Read. “ {{5}} and meet my son, Bob.”
Look! Bob and Jack are having the cake. They are talking {{6}} . Now they are friends! Jack says, “I’m glad you live next door.” Bob says, “I must thank your mother for coming to borrow eggs.” Jack laughs and tells Bob, “My mother doesn’t want the two eggs, but she wants to make friends with your mother!” Bob says, “That’s a {{7}} way to make friends. It’s an easy way, too. It can work!”
So if you want to make friends, you can always {{8}} some ways!

blanks.why: 根据“He doesn’t have anyone to play with.”可知, Bob在新城市没有人跟他玩, 妈妈在安慰他很快会交到朋友。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我妈妈送你这个蛋糕和两个鸡蛋。
blanks.why: 根据“She comes to borrow some eggs. She wants to make cakes.”可知, 因Miller夫人曾来借过鸡蛋做蛋糕 , 现在是Jack来归还鸡蛋, 并送了蛋糕。故选C。

blanks.mean: 进来见见我的儿子Bob吧。

blanks.mean: 这是一种有趣的交友方式。
blanks.gloss: difficult困难的；quiet安静的；cheap便宜的；funny有趣的。
blanks.why: 根据“My mother doesn’t want the two eggs, but she wants to make friends with your mother!”可知, Jack的妈妈想用借鸡蛋的方式来和Bob妈妈交朋友, 这是一种有趣的交友方式。故选D。

blanks.mean: 所以, 如果你想交朋友, 你总能找到一些方法！

text:

Many years ago, when I was 5 years old, my mother grew some plants on the balcony (阳台). As {{1}} came, some flowers came out. I enjoyed looking at them very much. They were so {{2}} . But they didn’t give out any sweet smells (气味). How can I {{3}} them to smell as good as they look? After {{4}} about the problem for a few days, I had a good idea.
One day, when my parents were not at home, I picked a bottle of perfume (香水) from my mother’s dressing table. Then I {{5}} the bottle cap and poured (倾倒) some perfume onto the plants. I was very {{6}} that I helped to make my lovely flowers become better. But to my surprise (惊讶), a few days later, I noticed the flowers fell (凋落), before summer arrived, the plants lost their lives. I cried and I knew I did something wrong.
Later, my mother told me the {{7}} . She said the perfume was really bad for plants. Some beautiful flowers have no smells at all. We can’t change it as we like. Everything in life follows the ways of nature (自然). We must not put our ideas into {{8}} before we learn about the ways of nature.
What a lesson!

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
It was my 13th birthday. I had to spend it without my dad again another year. He always has to be on a work trip somewhere making money for us. It is great that he does this, but on my special day, I {{1}} him a little more.
He often sends cards through the mail for my birthdays and I usually get them when I get up. It is {{2}} not seeing my dad much all the time, so I do expect (期盼) my birthday cards every year. Other kids may never want the birthday cards so much like me because they {{3}} their dads every day.
I went to the mailbox to get the card out this morning, but it wasn’t there. Didn’t my dad send one? Maybe it got lost along the way. I went back inside to the kitchen. Mum looked at me and {{4}} my thoughts in some way.
She thought for a second and said, “It may be running {{5}} today. Don’t worry.” It should be always there on time. I checked it many times, still nothing. Later, it was time for dinner with my mum and my grandparents. I just ate little because I really wanted to know where the {{6}} was. I thought everyone else here was having a better time than me on my own birthday.
“What a birthday like this...” I said to myself sadly. Suddenly, the doorbell rang. My mum told me to answer the door. I walked to the door slowly, looked through the glass and saw a man holding a cake. To my surprise, it was my {{7}} ! I opened the door and he gave me a big hug.
“Happy birthday!” he said, “I don’t have to go on another work trip for at least another year.” “Dad, I have you back again! Thank you for {{8}} my favourite cake,” I said excitedly.

blanks.why: 根据“on my special day”可推知, 此处指作者在生日这天会更想念爸爸。故选C。

blanks.why: 根据“It may be running...today. Don’t worry.”可知, 作者的妈妈看出了作者的心思, 所以才安慰他。read sb’s thoughts意为“读懂/看透某人的想法”。故选C。

blanks.gloss: late晚, 迟；around周围；freely自由地；carefully仔细地。
blanks.why: 根据“I went to the mailbox to get the card out this morning, but it wasn’t there.”可知, 作者生日那天的早晨没收到爸爸的贺卡, 所以妈妈安慰他可能晚点就会收到。故选A。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
When I was nine years old, I loved to go fishing with my dad. But the only thing that wasn’t very fun was that he could catch many fish but I couldn’t. I was usually {{1}} and kept asking him why. He always answered, “Son, if you want to catch a fish, you have to {{2}} like a fish”. I became even more confused (困惑的) because “I’m not a fish!” I didn’t know how to think like one. Also, how could what I think {{3}} me catch a fish?
As I got a little older, I began to understand what my dad really meant. I read some books on fish. I even {{4}} a fishing club and went to their meetings every month. I learned that a fish is a cold-blooded (冷血的) animal so its body temperature (温度) changes when the water temperature changes. That’s why they love to stay in shallow (浅的) water. It is {{5}} there when there is sunlight. But fish don’t have any eyelids (眼皮) and the sun hurts their {{6}} . The more I understood fish, the better I became at finding and catching them.
When I {{7}} and started my first job, my boss said, “We all need to think like sales people.” But I didn’t think so. My dad never said, “If you want to catch a fish you need to think like a fisherman.” What he said was, “You need to think like a fish.” So I tried to think like my customers (顾客). Over the years, I found out what they really liked and needed. It is not a (an) {{8}} job, but it is what made me successful.

“Let’s try creating a round robin story (故事接龙) today,” said Carlos’s teacher, Ms. Wade. “That’s a kind of story where one person starts with a few sentences, and then a new person tells the next part. We pass the story on, until the last storyteller {{1}} it.”
She looked around at the class and asked, “Who wants to start?”
Hands shot up, but Carlos made himself as {{2}} as he could in his seat in the back row, hoping he wouldn’t get picked.
In fact, when he was home, Carlos told fantastic stories to his family and everyone enjoyed them. But every day on the bus ride to school, he {{3}} his voice and became quiet.
All Carlos knew was that he just felt too {{4}} to talk in class, to be in the spotlight.
But now Ms. Wade was looking right at him. “Carlos, I know from our writing homework that you like telling stories. The one about the talking banana was so funny that it made me {{5}} so hard!”
“A talking banana?” cried Elena, “I want to hear that one!”
Ms. Wade was smiling when she turned again to Carlos.
“So, would you like to start, Carlos, or would you rather be one of our {{6}} today?” Ms. Wade asked.
Carlos looked around, and saw all the kids waiting for his {{7}} , with smiles as wide as Ms. Wade’s. Carlos heard himself begin, “Once there was a talking banana in Ms. Wade’s class...”
“That banana was always talking big,” Carlos continued. “One day, the banana told everyone that he could jump over the tallest kid in class. Now, this banana was a little one, and the tallest kid in class was ten feet tall! But that banana didn’t care. He shouted ‘Banana-ran-ran!’ and ran straight at that ten-foot-tall kid, and then...”
Carlos stopped.
Half the class was laughing. The others {{8}} , “Then what? What happened?!”
“Quiet, everyone! We’ll find out when the round robin ends,” Ms. Wade held up her hands and said, “Elena, maybe you can take the next part.”
Carlos sat back in his seat, feeling ten feet tall himself. He had found his voice!

blanks.why: 根据“We pass the story on, until the last storyteller...it.”可知, 应是故事传到最后一位讲述者, 这位讲述者用故事结束这个传递。故选C。

As Tony walked with his family along the river, he saw a man playing the saxophone by the river. At the same time, he was {{1}} to the beautiful music from his saxophone. Two weeks later, it was Tony’s birthday. When he opened his {{3}} from his parents, he was glad to find it was a saxophone!
He blew (吹) the mouth of the saxophone and tried to {{4}} it, but the saxophone wouldn’t make a sound. Then his dad told him to {{5}} the instrument (乐器) book to learn what to do. After about 15 minutes, he raised it slowly to his lips (嘴唇) as his family watched. But {{6}} there was no sound. He blew and blew but he couldn’t get the saxophone to work. He was almost {{7}} when suddenly the saxophone made the most beautiful sound which made him think of the music of the man by the river.
Then he began to take saxophone classes after school. His {{8}} taught him how to play it. When he was learning, he always {{9}} the man playing the saxophone by the river. His {{10}} of playing musical instrument were gradually improved and at last he could play music with his saxophone. Now Tony is in the TV studio. He is waiting to be called to give his first show on TV.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
完形填空（每题 1分, 共 8分）阅读下面的短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的 A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择最佳选项。

My parents were very excited on my first day at school and so was I. My dad gave me his father’s old pen. He loved that pen, so I was {{1}} to have it with me that day. My mum straightened (整理) my clothes and then she {{2}} me my lunch bag.
I said goodbye to my mum and waited for my dad in the garden. Hand in hand my dad and I soon got to school. He didn’t {{3}} long. I was on my own. I didn’t know anyone, so I decided (决定) to {{4}} other kids on the playground. It wasn’t difficult for me to make new friends that day.
There were many children in the first grade. All of them were nice and two of them were {{5}} . They were sisters and they were twins (双胞胎). It was amazing (神奇的). You couldn’t tell the {{6}} between them.
“Did your mum prepare (准备) anything for your lunch?” A girl asked me as I {{7}} my lunch bag.
“Yes, she did.” I answered. “Would you like to have some cheese?”
“Sure, thanks!” She said, “Have some of my fruit, too.”
We shared (分享) our {{8}} , and after lunch we played together on the playground. It was a memorable day for me.

blanks.mean: 他很喜欢那支铅笔, 所以那天带着它, 我很自豪。
blanks.gloss: afraid害怕的；nervous紧张的；proud自豪的；sad悲伤的。
blanks.why: 根据“My dad gave me his father’s old pen. He loved that pen”可知, 这只笔经历了爷爷和爸爸两代人, 爸爸还非常喜欢它, 因此我带着它非常自豪。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我妈妈把我的衣服拉直, 然后递给我午餐袋。
blanks.why: 根据“I said goodbye to my mum and waited for my dad in the garden”可知, 妈妈递给我午餐袋。hand sb. sth.“递给某人某物”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他没待多久。
blanks.why: 根据“I was on my own”可知, 我独自一人, 他没有待多久。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我不认识任何人, 所以我决定加入其它孩子, 和他们一起在操场上玩。
blanks.why: 根据“It wasn’t difficult for me to make new friends that day”可知, 我决定加入其他孩子, 和他们一起玩；join sb.“加入某人”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他们都很好, 其中两个很特别。
blanks.gloss: friendly友好的；boring无聊的；special特别的；wrong错误的。
blanks.why: 根据“They were sisters and they were twins. It was amazing.”可知, 这里指这对双胞胎姐妹很特别。故选C。

blanks.mean: 你分不清她们之间的区别。
blanks.gloss: secret秘密；difference差异, 区别；trouble麻烦；story故事。
blanks.why: 根据“They were sisters and they were twins,”可知, 此处指分不清这对双胞胎姐之间的区别。故选B。

blanks.mean: “你妈妈为你准备午餐了吗？
blanks.why: 根据“Did your mum prepare anything for your lunch?”可知, 此处指当作者打开午餐包时, 女孩和他谈论了午餐。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们分享了我们的食物, 午饭后我们一起在操场上玩耍。
blanks.why: 根据“Would you like to have some cheese?”可知, 两人分享了食物。故选D。

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:
Beth Jones was only eight years old when she first tried playing the drums. One day, she went to the music room. Of all the musical instruments (乐器), the {{1}} caught her eyes. She thought they looked cool, and there were many different kinds of drums. She hit them to hear how they sounded.
Now Beth is a drummer and gives concerts with her band (乐队) around the country. Many people like their {{2}} , but she has never had a drum lesson. “It’s easy to {{3}} drums on the Internet. So I don’t think it’s important for me to take classes.” said Beth.
Giving concerts wasn’t {{4}} for Beth in the beginning. She practiced (练习) a lot, but she never played in front of many people. At her first concert, she could feel hundreds of pairs of {{5}} around her. They were looking at her, and that made her feel {{6}} . But soon she got used to (适应) playing in front of lots of people.
Beth is very famous in her city now. So, does she enjoy being famous? “I never {{7}} to be famous,” she said. “I just want to show (展示) others what I {{8}} . I want everyone to have a great time at my concerts.”

blanks.mean: 在所有的乐器中, 鼓引起了她的注意。
blanks.why: 根据“and there were many different kinds of drums”可知, 在所有的乐器中, 鼓引起了她的注意。故选A。

blanks.mean: 很多人喜欢他们的音乐, 但她从未上过鼓课。
blanks.why: 根据“Now Beth is a drummer and gives concerts with her band (乐队) around the country.”可知, 许多人喜欢他们的音乐, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 在网上学鼓很容易。
blanks.why: 根据“So I don’t think it’s important for me to take classes”可知, 在网上学鼓很容易, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 一开始, 举办音乐会对贝丝来说并不容易。
blanks.gloss: lucky幸运的；funny有趣的；easy容易的；cheap便宜的。
blanks.why: 根据“She practiced (练习) a lot, but she never played in front of many people.”可知, 举办音乐会对贝丝来说并不容易, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 在她的第一场音乐会上, 她能感觉到周围有数百双眼睛。
blanks.why: 根据“They were looking at her”可知, 周围有数百双眼睛看着她。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他们看着她, 这使她感到害怕。
blanks.why: 根据“She practiced (练习) a lot, but she never played in front of many people.”可知, 第一次有那么多人看着, 她感觉很害怕, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 我从来没打算成名。
blanks.why: 根据“I just want to show (展示) others what I…I want everyone to have a great time at my concerts.”可知, 她没想过成名, 只是想让别人知道自己喜欢的是什么。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我只是想让别人知道我喜欢什么。
blanks.why: 根据“I want everyone to have a great time at my concerts.”可知, 她只是想让别人知道自己喜欢什么, 故选D。

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
Abby’s father was taking her to visit her grandmother. Abby was going to be away for three months. “I can’t leave Candy behind,” she said.
“You will have to,” said her father. “You can’t take a {{1}} into another country. It’s a rule.”
At the airport, Abby put her bag by the X-ray machine. Candy was hidden in a {{2}} . Abby hoped he didn’t squeak.
The bag rolled {{3}} the X-ray. Abby felt her legs shaking and her heart beating fast. But the woman by the X-ray machine just smiled and said, “Have a good flight.”
On the {{4}} , Abby waited until her dad and the woman next to her fell asleep. Then she opened up the sock to look at Candy. But Candy jumped onto the woman’s knee. The woman screamed (尖叫). Abby {{5}} caught him and put him into the sock and back into her bag.
A flight attendant (乘务员) rushed over. “A mouse!” cried the woman. “You were just dreaming,” said the flight attendant to the woman. “There is no mouse here.” Abby’s dad filled out a form before they landed. He ticked (打勾) no to “Are you bringing any live animals into the country?”
Abby saw the man at the X-ray machine frown and then Abby and her dad were taken into a small room. The police officer talked to Abby’s dad. “This is very serious,” he said. “You have tried to take an animal into this country and you have {{6}} on this form. Abby felt {{7}} , “It’s my fault,” she said in a small voice.
It was a real {{8}} for Abby. Candy had to go into quarantine (隔离) for six months. It cost a lot of money. Her dad had to pay a big fine as well.
The police officer said that she could have “animal smuggler (走私者)” next to her name. Then she wouldn’t be able to visit her grandmother again.
Abby learned there was a very good reason for rules.

blanks.mean: 你不能把老鼠带到另一个国家。
blanks.why: 根据下文““A mouse!” cried the woman.”可知, 应是不能把老鼠带到另一个国家。故选B。

blanks.mean: Candy被藏在袜子里。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Then she opened up the sock to look at Candy.”可知, Candy是被藏在袜子里。故选A。

blanks.mean: 袋子在X光下滚动。
blanks.gloss: beside在……旁边；behind在……后面；above在……上面；under在……下面。
blanks.why: 根据常识可知, 上飞机之前安检时, 行李是在X光下滚动。故选D。

blanks.mean: 在飞机上, Abby一直等到她爸爸和她旁边的女人睡着了。
blanks.gloss: train火车；bus公共汽车；plane飞机；machine机器。
blanks.why: 根据上句“Have a good flight.”可推理出应是在飞机上。故选C。

blanks.mean: Abby很快抓住他, 把他放进袜子, 然后放回包里。
blanks.gloss: quietly静静地；slowly慢慢地；gently轻轻地；quickly快地。
blanks.why: 根据前文“But Candy jumped onto the woman’s knee. The woman screamed (尖叫).”语境可知, 应是很快抓住老鼠。故选D。

blanks.mean: 你试图把一只动物带到这个国家, 你在这张表格上撒了谎。
blanks.why: 根据上文“He ticked (打勾) no to “Are you bringing any live animals into the country?””和前句“You have tried to take an animal into this country”可知, 是在填这张表格时撒了谎。故选B。

blanks.mean: Abby感到很害怕。
blanks.gloss: scared害怕的；excited激动的；pleased高兴的；surprised惊讶的。
blanks.why: 根据后句““It’s my fault,” she said in a small voice.”可知, 应是Abby感到害怕了。故选A。

blanks.mean: 这对Abby来说是一个真正的教训。
blanks.why: 根据标题“Abby’s Lesson”可知, 应是这件事对对Abby来说是一个教训。故选A。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
I was feeling a little blue because my mother had lost her job.
One day while I was walking on the street, I heard piano music and singing rising above the noise of the people. I walked more slowly to {{1}} where it was coming from. Then I saw a young lady sitting at a piano.
She was singing songs about love, believing yourself and keeping on trying. The way she was singing made me a little comfortable. I stood there {{2}} , watching her play in such a crowded New York square. I thought that she must be {{3}} enough to perform in front of so many people.
She noticed me. I walked over and told her how good her {{4}} sounded. “Thank you,” she said.
“I have been going through a hard time recently, and you’ve made me hopeful again,” I said to her.
“I’m glad that I could help,” she replied. “Why are you so {{5}} ?”
“Well, my mom has lost her job, and I’m not sure what to do.”
“Did you notice the way you were walking? Your head was down,” she said. “Don’t be upset, because {{6}} comes in different ways and if your head is down, you might not see it. You should {{7}} more, and lift your head up.”
I looked at her, amazed at how she was encouraging me. “Why are you playing the piano here?” I asked her with a smile.
She {{8}} that she saw a lot of unhappy people around and she tried to cheer them up by playing music.
I smiled a little wider, realizing that no difficulties could stop me from going on.

blanks.mean: 我走得慢了些, 想弄清楚它是从哪里来的。
blanks.why: 根据后文“Then I saw a young lady sitting at a piano.”可知, 我看见一位年轻的女士坐在钢琴变, 可推测空处应是去找出声音来源。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我安静地站在那里, 看她在一个如此拥挤的纽约广场演奏。
blanks.gloss: nervously紧张地；rudely粗鲁地；angrily生气地；quietly安静地。
blanks.why: 根据空后“watching her play”可知, 作者站在那里的目的是观看女人演奏, 结合常识, 空处应用quietly“安静地”。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我原以为她在这么多人面前表演, 一定足够勇敢。
blanks.gloss: brave勇敢的；shy害羞的；bored无聊的；honest诚实的。
blanks.why: 根据“perform in front of so many people”, 再结合常识可知, 在很多人面前表演需要非常勇敢。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我走过去告诉她, 她的音乐听起来多么好。
blanks.why: 根据前文可知, 年轻女士在广场上弹唱音乐, 所以作者听到并评价的是她的音乐。故选B。

blanks.mean: 你为什么如此沮丧？
blanks.gloss: dirty脏的；busy忙的；upset沮丧的；lazy懒惰的。
blanks.why: 根据前文“I was feeling a little blue because my mother had lost her job.”可知, 作者觉得有些悲伤因为妈妈失业了。故选C。

blanks.mean: 不要沮丧, 因为机会会以不同的方式到来。
blanks.why: 根据“Don’t be upset.”可知, 年轻女士在安慰作者不要沮丧, 结合给出四个选项, chance符合语境, 此处表示机会会到来的。故选A。

blanks.mean: 你应该多微笑, 抬起你的头。
blanks.why: 根据“...she tried to cheer them up by playing music”可知, 年轻女士想要帮不高兴的人快乐起来, 可推测她会劝作者抬头微笑。故选B。

blanks.mean: 她解释说她看见世界上很多人不高兴, 她努力通过演奏音乐让他们高兴起来。
blanks.why: 根据前文“Why are you playing the piano here?”可知, 作者问了年轻女士来广场弹唱的原因, 所以本句话是她在向作者解释。故选D。

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
When I was in the sixth grade, one day my teacher asked our class to think about the question “What does ‘doing the right thing’ mean to you?” over the weekend. By Monday, we had to hand in an essay(论文) on it, and be prepared to live up to(达到……；实践) our {{1}} .
The whole weekend, I was trying to think of something that would impress my teacher and be easy to live up to. I {{2}} to my parents, called my grandmother and asked my neighbor. Everyone had good answers, but I didn’t feel like I could live up to them.
On Sunday afternoon, my parents said they were going to my Aunt Cindy’s house. That usually meant that I would have to spend time with my four-year old cousin Andrea while my parents visited. I found a Disney movie for Andrea, and then I sat down and started to write my essay. It was due(到期的) the next morning and this was my last {{3}} .
Soon I felt a pair of eyes on me. It was Andrea.
“What are you doing?” Andrea asked.
“I have to write an essay about what ‘doing the right thing’ means to me.” I answered.
Andrea {{4}} . Could this smart four-year-old possibly know the answer?
“That’s easy,” she said. “Doing the right thing means being nice to your family and friends. Never lie. Eat lots of fruit and vegetables. Take a bath when you’re {{5}} . And never put rocks in your mouth.”
I stared (盯着) with great {{6}} at my little cousin. Then I jumped up and gave her the biggest hug. Not only had Andrea answered a very hard question for me, but I could {{7}} live up to all of her answers. All I had to do was to be nice, not to lie, to keep myself clean and healthy, and never put rocks in my mouth. So when I wrote my essay, I included the story about Andrea and how she had answered my question.
Two weeks later, my teacher {{8}} everyone’s essays. I received an A+ along with a little note my teacher had written at the top: “Always do the right thing and give Andrea an A+, too!”

blanks.mean: 在星期一之前, 我们必须交一篇关于它的文章, 并准备实践我们的答案。
blanks.why: 根据“be prepared to live up to(达到……；实践) our”以及上文“think about the question”可知是指问题的答案, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 我和父母谈了谈, 给祖母打了电话, 还问了邻居。
blanks.why: 根据“I was trying to think of something”以及“to my parents, called my grandmother and asked my neighbor.”可知应该是和父母谈话了, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 第二天早上就要交作业了, 这是我最后的机会了。
blanks.why: 根据“It was due(到期的) the next morning”可知交作业的时间要到了, 所以这是作者最后的机会了。故选B。

blanks.mean: Andrea笑了。
blanks.why: 根据“Could this smart four-year-old possibly know the answer”可推测Andrea应该是笑了, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 脏了就洗个澡。
blanks.gloss: dirty脏的；quiet安静的；sleepy困倦的；unhappy不开心的。
blanks.why: 根据“Take a bath”可知身体脏了就洗个澡。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我惊奇地盯着我的小表妹。
blanks.why: 根据“Then I jumped up and gave her the biggest hug”可知作者很惊讶小表妹竟然可以解决自己的问题。故选C。

blanks.mean: Andrea不仅为我回答了一个非常困难的问题, 而且我很容易就能履行她所有的回答。
blanks.gloss: hardly几乎不；terribly非常；never从不；easily容易地。
blanks.why: 根据“All I had to do was to be nice, not to lie, to keep myself clean and healthy, and never put rocks in my mouth”可知这些事对于作者来说都是很容易达到。故选D。

blanks.mean: 两周后, 我的老师退还了每个人的文章。
blanks.why: 根据“I received an A+ along with a little note my teacher had written at the top:”可知作者收到了老师退还的作文。故选C。 阅读理解：（共26分）

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

Near Hannah’s house there’s a new skatepark. A lot of young people in the town go there after school with their skateboards.
These days Hannah often goes there with her cousin Justin. With the new skatepark, she’s very interested in skateboarding. The only thing is—Hannah has no {{1}} !
Sometimes Justin asks Hannah, “Hey, do you want to get on my skateboard?” So she does—but not for long. She doesn’t want to fall off in front of everybody. Justin is a good skateboarder. He can do a lot of tricks (技巧). Hannah thinks, “I want to jump and do tricks, too. My {{2}} is coming. Maybe I can talk to Mom and Dad.”
On Hannah’s birthday morning, she opens her presents. There’s a big present from her parents. “Wow! A skateboard! Thanks! I have my skateboard now. So I can do more,” Hannah says {{3}} . That weekend, Hannah takes her new skateboard to the skatepark with Justin.
Hannah is excited. They begin skateboarding. Justin does a trick. “Maybe I can jump now,” she thinks. She goes faster and jumps—but she falls off her skateboard. When she is on the ground, somebody laughs. “Oh, no! This is really {{4}} ! No more skateboarding for me!” she thinks. She gets up quickly and {{5}} .
The next day, Hannah sees a woman sitting on the grass with her baby boy. The little boy is trying to stand. “Good boy, Michael,” his mother says. “Stand up now.” Michael stands up slowly.
He takes one little step and falls down. “Don’t cry. {{6}} again,” his mother says. Michael stops crying. He takes his mother’s hand and stands up again. Hannah watches them for five minutes.
“He doesn’t stop falling. But it doesn’t matter,” Hannah thinks.
One Saturday afternoon, Hannah goes to the skatepark with Justin. At the skatepark, Justin says, “Everybody falls off sometimes.” “Sure, how do you do that trick? I want to {{7}} it.” “Put your right foot here, and then push with your left foot.” “OK,” Hannah says, “I need some more practice.” “You’re a(n) {{8}} skateboarder now, Hannah,” Justin tells her quietly.

blanks.mean: 唯一的问题是汉娜没有滑板。
blanks.why: 根据前两句“These days Hannah… she’s very interested in skateboarding.”以及下文中“Sometimes Justin asks Hannah, ‘Hey, do you want to get on my skateboard?’”可猜测, 汉娜对滑板很感兴趣, 但是没有自己的滑板, 应填skateboard。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我的生日要到了。
blanks.gloss: holiday假期；birthday生日；party聚会；trip 旅行。
blanks.why: 根据下文“On Hannah’s birthday morning, … There’s a big present from her parents. ‘Wow! A skateboard! ...’”可知, 汉娜在她生日那天父母送给了她一个滑板, 由此可推测此处应是“我的生日要到了”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 汉娜兴奋地说：“哇！
blanks.why: 由上文可知, 汉娜非常想要一个滑板, 由此可推测在生日那天她收到滑板时应该很兴奋, 应填excitedly。故选D。

blanks.mean: 她想：“哦, 不！
blanks.gloss: 这太糟糕了！我再也不玩滑板了！” easy简单的；cold寒冷的；bad糟糕的；late迟到。
blanks.why: 根据上文“…she falls off her skateboard. When she is on the ground, somebody laughs.”可知, 汉娜从滑板上摔了下来, 有人也笑她了, 再结合下文“No more skateboarding for me!”可推断, 此刻汉娜应该感觉很糟糕, sad最符合语境。故选C。

blanks.mean: 她迅速起来并离开了。
blanks.why: 根据上文可知, 汉娜不想再玩滑板了, 由此可推测, 汉娜起来离开了, 应填leaves。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他母亲说：“不要哭。
blanks.why: 根据上文“He takes one little step and falls down.”和下文“He takes his mother’s hand and stands up again.”可知, 男婴的母亲是在鼓励他再试一次, 应填Try。故选D。

blanks.mean: “当然, 那个技巧你怎么做？
blanks.why: 根据“Sure, how do you do that trick?”和“Put your right foot here, and then push with your left foot.”可知, 汉娜想学习贾斯汀上次那个滑板技巧, 应填learn。故选A。

blanks.mean: 贾斯汀悄悄地告诉她：“你现在是一个真正的滑板运动员了, 汉娜。
blanks.gloss: ” famous著名的；usual寻常的；real真正的；special特殊的。
blanks.why: 根据上文可知, 汉娜不再害怕摔倒, 想开始学习滑板, 并且还会多加练习, 这就是一个运动员的体育精神, 由此可推测贾斯汀认为汉娜是一个真正的滑板运动员了。故选C。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
Are you interested in collecting (收集) pictures or any other things? Maybe you have heard of the scrapbook (剪贴簿), {{1}} you don’t know what it is. I know. Let me tell you more about it now.
Scrapbooks are useful and {{2}} things. They have been popular for more than 500 years. People usually use scrapbooks to keep pictures, letters, poems and other things they want to {{3}} .
Today people collect more things with scrapbooks. Some people have {{4}} collections like the world’s stupid ideas or pictures of the ugly dogs. Some people even collect videos about bad weather.
In fact, it is easy to start making your own scrapbook. First, you should decide (决定) {{5}} you want to collect. Start with just one idea. Next, you need a {{6}} with a white background (背景), a pair of scissors and glue. You need the scissors to cut out the {{7}} or the stories of magazines and newspapers. You also need the glue to stick (粘贴) them on the notebook.
You can be active and collect many things, or be {{8}} and collect a few things. It’s up to you. It will be interesting to make your scrapbook and you can share it with your friends.

blanks.mean: 也许你听说过剪贴簿, 但你不知道它是什么。
blanks.why: 前后两句是转折关系, 用but连接。故选D。

blanks.mean: 剪贴簿是有用和有趣的东西。
blanks.gloss: difficult困难的；boring无聊的；unusual不同寻常的；interesting有趣的。
blanks.why: 根据“Scrapbooks are useful...things”以及下文内容可知剪贴簿是有趣的。故选D。

blanks.mean: 人们通常使用剪贴簿来保存图片、信件、诗歌和其他他们想记住的东西。
blanks.why: 根据“keep pictures, letters, poems and other things they want to”可知剪贴簿可以帮助人们记住东西。故选B。

blanks.mean: 有些人有一些有趣的收藏, 比如世界上愚蠢的想法或丑狗的照片。
blanks.gloss: funny有趣的；serious严肃的；fresh新鲜的；old老的。
blanks.why: 根据“like the world’s stupid ideas or pictures of the ugly dogs”可知收集世界上愚蠢的想法或者丑陋小狗的照片, 这些收集都很有趣。故选A。

blanks.mean: 首先, 你应该决定要收集什么。
blanks.gloss: what什么；when什么时候；why为什么；who谁。
blanks.why: 宾语从句中缺少宾语, 用what引导。故选A。

blanks.mean: 接下来, 你需要一个白色背景的笔记本, 一把剪刀和胶水。
blanks.why: 根据“You also need the glue to stick (粘贴) them on the notebook”可知此处指一个笔记本。故选D。

blanks.mean: 你需要剪刀剪出杂志和报纸的图片或故事。
blanks.why: 根据“Are you interested in collecting (收集) pictures”可知是杂志或报纸上的图片。故选A。

blanks.mean: 你可以积极地收集很多东西, 也可以懒惰, 只收集一些东西。
blanks.gloss: angry生气的；lazy懒惰的；sleepy困倦的；lucky幸运的。
blanks.why: 根据“You can be active and collect many things, or be...and collect a few things”可知可以很积极, 也可以懒惰一些, 不用收集那么多东西。故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
My dad was a fisherman, and he loved the sea. He had a boat, but it was {{1}} to make a living on the sea. It was dangerous too. He worked very hard and stayed out all day and night to catch enough fish for the family.

When the weather was {{2}} , my father didn’t work, and he drove me to school. We talked a lot on the way. Before he {{3}} , he would tell me to be a good boy and give me a big kiss on the face. It was so embarrassing (尴尬的) for me.
I {{4}} the day. When I was 12 years old, I thought I was too old for a goodbye kiss. We got to school and came to a stop. He had his usual big smile and started to kiss me, but I put my hand up and said, “No, dad.” It was the first time that I talked to him in that way, and he felt very surprised.
I said, “Dad, I’m too old for a goodbye kiss. I’m too old for any kind of kiss.” My dad looked at me {{5}} for a long time. I never saw him cry before that day. But he really did this time. I sat there without knowing what to say. Then he said, “You are right. You are a big boy… a {{6}} . I won’t kiss you any more.”
It wasn’t long after that when my dad went to the sea and never {{7}} . I was so sad that I wanted one more {{8}} from my father. But I couldn’t get any.

blanks.mean: 他有一条船, 但在海上谋生很困难。
blanks.why: 根据“It was dangerous too. He worked very hard and stayed out all day and night to catch enough fish for the family.”可知, 海上谋生很难, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 天气不好时, 我父亲不工作, 开车送我上学。
blanks.why: 根据“my father didn’t work”可知, 爸爸不去出海是在天气不好的时候, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 在他离开之前, 他会告诉我要做个好孩子, 在我脸上给我一个大大的吻。
blanks.why: 根据“he would tell me to be a good boy and give me a big kiss on the face.”可知, 是爸爸离开的时候, 会亲吻作者, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 我记得那天。
blanks.why: 根据“When I was 12 years old, I thought I was too old for a goodbye kiss...”可知, 这是作者在回忆那一天的事情, 所以应是“记得那一天”, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 爸爸悲伤地看了我很长一段时间。
blanks.why: 根据“I never saw him cry before that day. But he really did this time.”可知, 爸爸很伤心, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 你是一个大男孩……一个男子汉。
blanks.why: 根据“I’m too old for a goodbye kiss. I’m too old for any kind of kiss.”可知, 此处是和boy同等意义的词汇, 结合选项, man最合语境, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 没过多久, 爸爸就出海了, 再也没有回来。
blanks.why: 根据“my dad went to the sea and never...I couldn’t get any.”可知, 爸爸出海再也没有回来, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 我很伤心, 我想让父亲再吻我一次。
blanks.why: 根据“He had his usual big smile and started to kiss me”可知, 作者想念爸爸的吻, 故选A。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
Rob tapped his foot on the ground impatiently（不耐烦地）. His friend, Steve, should meet him in five minutes. They were going to meet and watch a movie together, and Rob didn't want to miss a single minute of the show.
Both of them really liked {{1}} and tried to see one almost every week, but lately Steve had been arriving later and later. Rob complained about late friends in a low voice while he waited.
Rob began pacing（踱步）back and forth. When pacing didn't {{2}} him, he started to look at his watch from time to time. There were only three minutes left before he went in without his friend, Rob decided. Pacing was making him more impatient.
He wondered why Steve couldn't be on time. He wondered what {{3}} Steve would have this time. Last time Steve had said it was because his dad needed help in the garden. What would be this time? There was only one minute Left. Then he heard a familiar voice, " Rob, I {{4}} it! " Rob turned around and saw Steve. "You made it, and you are on time, too! " Rob said excitedly.
"Of course, " Steve replied, "I really wanted to see this movie."
"Well let's go then." Rob suggested. He {{5}} for his wallet, so he could buy a ticket. Where was his wallet?
"What's wrong?" Steve asked.
"I don't have my wallet." Rob replied {{6}} .
"Go check in your car."
"I might be late then." Rob answered, feeling foolish. Here he'd been standing around waiting, and he was going to be the late one now. He ran across the parking lot.
By the time he got his wallet from his car and bought a ticket, he'd already {{7}} the beginning and he didn't have time to get popcorn or a drink. Steve shared his popcorn, but Rob could hardly eat it. He felt guilty（内疚的）during the whole movie.
When the movie was over, he apologized to Steve. "I'm sorry, Steve. I was complaining about you being late, but then I was the one who was late."
Steve said. "Don't worry. It happens to all of us."
"I see that now. Thanks for {{8}} . "
"That's what friends, for." Steve replied.

blanks.mean: 他们俩都很喜欢电影。
blanks.why: 根据“tried to see one almost every week”几乎每个星期都想看一部, 所以此处电影, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 当踱步不能使他平静下来时。
blanks.why: 根据“he started to look at his watch from time to time”他开始时不时地看看表, 所以此处是平静。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他想知道这次史蒂夫会有什么借口。
blanks.why: 根据“Last time Steve had said it was because his dad needed help in the garden”上次史蒂夫说是因为他爸爸在花园里需要帮忙, 所以此处是借口, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 我准时到了。
blanks.gloss: had有；made使；saw看见；bought带来；根据make it表示“成功了”。
blanks.why: 结合“You made it, and you are on time, too”你成功了, 所以此处是made, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 他伸手去拿钱包, 以便买票。
blanks.why: 根据“so he could buy a ticket. ”所以此处缺拿, 故选A。

blanks.mean: “我没带钱包。
blanks.why: 根据“I don't have my wallet”我没带钱包, 所以此处是焦急地, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 他已经错过了开头。
blanks.why: 根据“ he didn't have time to get popcorn or a drink”没有时间买爆米花或饮料, 所以此处是错过, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 谢谢你的理解。
blanks.gloss: helping帮助；driving驾驶；understanding理解；waiting等待；根据“That's what friends for”这就是什么是朋友。
blanks.why: 根据上下文以及语境做题, 切忌主观臆断。另外, 平时还要多多积累词汇。完型填空常考名词、动词、形容词和副词等辨析。做词义辨析题时, 首先要确认四个选项的含义, 然后分析语境和逻辑关系, 确定答案。 本文第三题考查名词。先确定四个词的意思。plan计划；advice建议；excuse借口；example例子；根据“Last time Steve had said it was because his dad needed help in the garden”上次史蒂夫说是因为他爸爸在花园里需要帮忙, 所以此处是借口, 故选C。

title: A Story Found in a Book
text:
My little brother, Evan, is 12 years old.
Most kids don’t {{1}} Evan at all. He has never been invited to the parties. Nobody asks him to do sports together. Too many people see only the ways Evan is {{2}} . They don’t see that in so many ways, he’s just like anyone else. He loves video games, reading, and being outdoors.
He was born 1.5 weeks early and has something called cerebral palsy（脑瘫）. He has problems with {{3}} and speaking.
Evan’s cerebral palsy may make him seem different when you first meet him. He walks with braces（支架）on his legs. And sometimes he makes sudden big sounds when speaking. It can also be {{4}} for him to understand what other people are thinking and feeling. Sometimes that makes Evan {{5}} too much. But he doesn’t mean to take over（控制）the talking. Usually he’s just really excited and doesn’t want to lose people’s attention.
The way Evan looks and does things can sometimes surprise people or make them {{6}} . But think about this: When Evan was born, doctors said he might never walk or talk. He has worked so hard to be able to do these things. So what if he looks and sounds a little different when he does them? None of Evan’s progress（进展）has come easy. He has had many surgeries（手术）. He visits his {{7}} each week, working on his legs and his speech. Now he’s even able to help with some housework. As his sister, I am so proud of all that Evan has done.
The next time you see Even, you can say hi to him. That way he wouldn’t feel left out and he will face those {{8}} in his life.

blanks.mean: 大部分孩子根本不认识Evan。
blanks.why: “He has never been invited to the parties. Nobody asks him to do sports together”可知, 大多数孩子不认识Evan, 所以没有人邀请他, 也没有让他一起做运动, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 太多人只看到了Evan的不同之处。
blanks.gloss: bored无聊的；famous著名的；fit适合的；different不同的。
blanks.why: 根据“He was born 1.5 weeks early and has something called cerebral palsy”可知, 他的身体健康与其他人不一样, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 他走路和说话都有问题。
blanks.why: 根据“He walks with braces on his legs”可知, Evan行走有困难, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 他也很难理解别人的想法和感受。
blanks.why: 根据“He walks with braces（支架）on his legs. And sometimes he makes sudden big sounds when speaking”及also可知, 此处讲的仍是Evan平时遇到的困难或与其他人不同的地方, 故选hard, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 有时这会让Evan话太多。
blanks.why: 根据“But he doesn’t mean to take over（控制）the talking”可知, 此处应表示“说话太多”, 故选B。

blanks.mean: Evan的长相和做事方式有时会让人感到惊讶或不舒服。
blanks.gloss: uncomfortable不舒服的；quiet安静的；hopeful有希望的；brave勇敢的。
blanks.why: 根据前面“He walks with braces（支架）on his legs. And sometimes he makes sudden big sounds when speaking”可知, 他的行为举止让人感到不舒服, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 他每周都去看医生, 治疗他的腿和说话能力。
blanks.gloss: teachers教师；classmates同学；cousins堂（表）兄弟姐妹；doctors医生。
blanks.why: 根据“working on his legs and his speech”可知此处表示去看“医生”, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 这样他就不会觉得被忽视了, 他会面对生活中的困难。
blanks.why: 由空前的动词face（面对）可知, 此处指面对所有的困难, 故选B。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
通读下面短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择能填入相应空白处的最佳选项, 将其字母代号写在题前括号内。
I used to hate running because I was always the last student to cross the finishing line. Then, in 2019, my friend asked me to run a 10 km-running event (比赛项目) with him. “No. I hate {{1}} .” I immediately said.
Over the weekend I thought about his question. I thought, “Why do I hate running? I haven’t {{2}} it since I was in Grade 7.” Finally, I decided to have a try, so I told my friend I’d like to. He was pleased and advised me to look for a running program on the Internet to help me {{3}} how to run.
There were lots of running programs on the Internet. I chose a 14-week running program that would teach me how to {{4}} running for 30 minutes. I found it very easy to follow. I enjoyed following the program as I could see the improvement in my running each week. I went from not being able to run for more than 30 seconds to running for over 30 minutes. I went from hating running to {{5}} running.
On the day of the 10 km-running event, I was both excited and nervous. {{6}} , it was time to put my new skills into practice. My friends and family came to support (支持) me. It was lovely to have them there. With their support and my training, I managed to finish the 10 km running in 72 minutes. It was hard but I felt very {{7}} for having tried it.
From this {{8}} , I learnt it was a good idea to try something before saying I hated it.

blanks.mean: “不, 我讨厌跑步。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I used to hate running”, 可知是讨厌跑步。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我上七年级以后就没试过了。
blanks.why: 根据上文“Why do I hate running?”可知应是从七年级开始就没尝试过跑步了。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他很高兴, 并建议我在网上找一个跑步教程来帮助我学习如何跑步。
blanks.why: 根据“He was pleased and advised me to look for a running program on the Internet to help me … how to run.”可知跑步教程应是来帮助作者学习如何跑步的。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我选择了一个14周的跑步教程, 它将教会我如何坚持跑30分钟。
blanks.gloss: lose失去、失败；forget忘记；stop停止；keep持续、保持。
blanks.why: 根据“I chose a 14-week running program that would teach me how to … running for 30 minutes.”可知, 应是这个教程将教会作者怎么坚持跑30分钟, keep doing sth“持续做某事”, 固定搭配。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我从讨厌跑步变成了喜欢跑步。
blanks.why: 根据上文的描述“I found it very easy to follow. I enjoyed following the program as I could see the improvement in my running each week. I went from not being able to run for more than 30 seconds to running for over 30 minutes.” 可知, 作者在跑步上取得了很大的效果, 所以应是有讨厌变为了喜欢。故选A。

blanks.mean: 最后, 是时候把我新技能付诸实践了。
blanks.why: 根据“it was time to put my new skills into practice.”可知, 所有的训练都是为了最后的10公里赛跑, finally符合语境。故选C。

blanks.mean: 这是很难的, 但我为尝试过它而感到非常自豪。
blanks.gloss: afraid害怕的；proud骄傲的、自豪的；warm温暖的；funny滑稽的。
blanks.why: 根据“It was hard but I felt very … for having tried it.”由转折词but可知前后句之间表达的是转折关系, 虽然很难, 但完成之后作者感到很自豪。故选B。

blanks.mean: 从这次经历中, 我明白了在说不喜欢某件事之前先尝试一下是个好主意。
blanks.why: 根据“I learnt it was a good idea to try something before saying I hated it.”可知这是作者从自身的经历中得出的感悟。故选A。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
“Are you listening, Simon?” Simon’s teacher asks.
Simon smiles and shakes(摇晃) his head. He doesn’t often {{1}} or try hard in class. Talking is so much better. He wants to be heard.That evening, Simon starts to feel a bit sick. By bedtime, his throat(咽喉) feels really bad. He has cakes and hot chocolate to make his throat feel better but he isn’t sure it’ll work.
The next {{2}} , when he opens his mouth to say, “Good morning,” nothing comes out.
When he gets to school, Mrs. Jacobs says “hello” to him, and he just nods(点头). When his friends start to ask him what TV shows he watches, he just can’t say anything. By the time they start {{3}} , almost everyone is looking at him as if he’s got a third eye.
Simon sits in class, bored {{4}} he can’t talk to his classmates. He watches them talk to each other, but he can’t even do that. You know what? It isn’t that bad. He can really do his homework that night. It gives {{5}} more TV and game time because his work finished.
The next day, his voice is {{6}} back, but he stays quiet(安静的) again. The third day, he can talk {{7}} , but he doesn’t talk. He listens and puts up his {{8}} to speak.
What a difference that one day makes!

blanks.mean: 课堂上他不会经常听讲或者努力。
blanks.why: 根据“…or try hard in class. Talking is so much better. ”可知, 西蒙课堂上讲话更好, 因此可推知课堂上不听讲或努力。故选D。

blanks.mean: 第二天早上, 当他开口说“早上好”, 却说不出任何话。
blanks.why: 根据“Good morning”可知是早上。故选B。

blanks.mean: 到要上课的时间了, 几乎人人都看着他似乎他有第三只眼睛。
blanks.why: 从后文“Simon sits in class, bored…”可知西蒙在课堂上坐着, 因此他是开始上课了, start class表示“开始上课”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 西蒙坐在课堂上, 很无聊因为不能和同学讲话。
blanks.why: 根据“Simon sits in class, bored…he can’t talk to his classmates.”可知, 西蒙感觉无聊, 后面是解释原因是不能和同学讲话了, 表示原因, 用because引导。故选D。

blanks.mean: 这给了他更多的电视和游戏时间, 因为他的功课完成了。
blanks.gloss: her她的；him他；it它；them它们, 他们, 她们。
blanks.why: 根据后文“because his work finished.”可知此处表示西蒙的功课完成了, 因此是给予了西蒙更多时间, 西蒙是男性, 动词后用宾格。故选B。

blanks.mean: 第二天他的嗓音回来了, 但他还是安安静静的。
blanks.why: 根据前文可知, 西蒙嗓子说不出话来, 因此此处表示它的嗓音回来了, come back表示“回来”。故选A。

blanks.mean: 第三天他可以很好地谈话, 但是他不说。
blanks.gloss: along沿着；hard困难的, 努力的；back回来；fine好, 不错。
blanks.why: 根据“but he doesn’t talk. ”中的but可知, 表示转折, 前后意思有改变, 可推知他可以讲话讲得很好了, 但是没有讲。故选D。

title: A Lesson from Nature
text:

A

In the middle of this lake, there is a small {{3}} . People call it Pearl Island because it {{4}} like a pearl. title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
“But I feel good doing this!” the little boy’s voice rang in my ears when I entered the mall. He stood raising {{1}} for cancer research. In the cold wind, he pulled his hat down over his ears. He warmed one hand in his pocket and held a list with the other hand. I noticed him greeting the people passing by {{2}} gloves on his hands.
I checked my purse but I didn’t find any change. I was {{3}} ready to give money because I wished cancer could be cured (治愈) one day.
“I’ll bring you some money when I returned” I {{4}} the little boy.
“Thank you!” he smiled and he seemed almost {{5}} in the cold air. I suggested he come inside the mall, but he said, “The guard there said {{6}} is allowed to raise money for charities (慈善) in the mall. But I feel good doing this here. It’s OK.”
I did my shopping and {{7}} about buying something for him. Finally, I bought a pair of gloves, brown ones. The cashier (收银员) felt curious when I {{8}} the boy’s words “But I feel good doing this!”
The boy still stood where he had been. I offered some money to him and {{9}} in the list that he handed to me. Then he told me that his best friend George had leukemia (白血病). He did this in order to help him out of {{10}} .
With tears full of my eyes, I put the gloves that I bought for him into his hands.
“Will the cancer research give you something to thank you for doing this?”
“Oh yes!” the boy said and his eyes {{11}} up with joy “They sure do! Now I can stand here much {{12}} than I expected!”
“What do you receive then?” I asked. He answered with a smile, “I get another new, empty list.”

blanks.mean: 他站在那里为癌症研究筹集资金。
blanks.why: 根据“I offered some money to him”可知, 他在筹钱。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我注意到他和路过的人打招呼时没有戴手套。
blanks.why: 根据“I put the gloves that I bought for him into his hands”可知, 男孩没有戴手套。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我总是准备捐钱, 因为我希望癌症有一天能被治愈。
blanks.why: 根据“because I wished cancer could be cured (治愈) one day”可知, 我希望癌症被治愈, 所以总是准备捐钱。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我答应小男孩说：“我回来的时候会给你带些钱来。
blanks.why: 根据“I’ll bring you some money when I returned”可知, 此处是向小男孩做承诺。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他微微一笑, 似乎被冷空气冻住了。
blanks.gloss: relaxed放松的；bored厌倦的；frozen冻住的；pleased高兴的。
blanks.why: 根据“In the cold wind, he pulled his hat down over his ears.”和“I suggested he come inside the mall”可知, 天气很冷, 他似乎被冻住了。故选C。

blanks.mean: 那里的保安说, 在商场里, 没有人被允许为慈善机构筹款。
blanks.gloss: everyone所有人；anyone任何人；someone某人；no one没有人。
blanks.why: 根据上下文可知, 男孩在商场外面, 因为商场里没有人捐款。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我买了东西, 并考虑给他买点东西。
blanks.gloss: thought about考虑；worried about担心；talked about谈论；cared about关心。
blanks.why: 根据“Finally, I bought a pair of gloves, brown ones.”可知, 考虑给小男孩买些东西。故选A。

blanks.mean: 当我重复那个男孩的话“但是这样做我感觉很好!”的时候, 收银员感到好奇。
blanks.why: 根据“But I feel good doing this”可知, 这是小男孩说过的话, 此处是重复小男孩的话。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我给了他一些钱, 填好了他递给我的单子。
blanks.why: 根据“in the list”可知, 此处是fill in the list“填写单子”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他这样做是为了帮助他摆脱困境。
blanks.gloss: sight 视线；work工作；trouble麻烦, 困境；breath呼吸。
blanks.why: 根据“Then he told me that his best friend George had leukemia (白血病)”可知, 他的好朋友得了白血病, 所以筹集金钱用于癌症研究可以帮助他摆脱困境。故选C。

blanks.mean: 男孩说着, 眼睛里闪着喜悦的光。
blanks.gloss: lit up照亮, 点亮；came up发生；caught up赶上；took up占据。
blanks.why: 根据“up with joy”可知, 他很开心, 眼睛里充满了喜悦的光。故选A。

blanks.mean: 现在我可以站在这里比我预期的更久！
blanks.why: 根据“I put the gloves that I bought for him into his hands …He answered with a smile”可知, 小男孩很开心, 所以更有动力, 能站立的时间会越久。故选D。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
What do you do on weekends? Some people like to stay at home, but others like to go out for a walk {{1}} have a picnic. My friend John works hard in a factory during the {{2}} . On weekends he always {{3}} the same thing. On Saturday he {{4}} his car and on Sunday he takes his family to a nearby village. His uncle and aunt have a farm there. It isn’t a {{5}} one, but there are always {{6}} things to do. The children help with the animals and give them some {{7}} .
John and his wife work in the fields. At the end of the day, they are all tired but {{8}} . And John’s aunt cooks a big dinner for them.

blanks.mean: 有些人喜欢待在家里, 但其他人喜欢出去散步或野餐。
blanks.why: “go out for a walk”和“ have a picnic”之间是选择关系, 所以用or连接, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 我的朋友杰克在工作日期间在工厂努力上班 。
blanks.why: 根据“On weekends he always...the same thing”可知, 此处介绍的是工作日的工作情况, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 周末他总是做同样的事。
blanks.why: 联系下文“the same things”可知, 此处指的是他总是做相同的事情, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 它不是一个大农场, 但是有很多事要做。

blanks.mean: 它不是一个大农场, 但是有很多事情要做。
blanks.gloss: many许多, 修饰可数名词复数；much许多, 修饰不可数名词；fast快的；far远的。
blanks.why: 根据“The children help with the animals and give them their...Jack and his wife help in the fields”可知, 农场有很多活, things是可数名词复数, 所以用many修饰。故选A。

blanks.mean: 孩子们经常帮助动物, 给它们食物。
blanks.why: 根据“help with the animals ”及常识可知, 在农场帮忙, 应该是给动物食物, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 在一天结束的时候, 他们都很累, 但很快乐。

blanks.why: 由tired可知, 应是虽然很累但是很开心, 故选B。

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:
完形填空（共8分, 每小题8分）阅读下面的短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择最佳选项。

As usual, Jenny is playing on the playground. Then she {{1}} a quiet “meow” and looks around. She finds a kitten sitting at the corner. He wears a collar （颈圈） {{2}} the name“Lucky”.
Picking it up, she walks to her teacher and says, “I find this kitten on the playground. He has a collar, so he must have his owner. But there’s no {{3}} or phone number on the collar. Could we help find his home as a class project? ”
“Certainly! Would you like to be the {{4}} in this project? ” Mrs March asks. Jenny says “yes”. She thinks of an idea and begins taking charge （负责）. “Okay, we’ll need to make posters （海报） to put up around the neighborhood. We should call the newspaper. What else? ” She asks the class. John thinks that they should call the animal center in case （万一） the owner calls there. “Good idea!” Jenny says as she adds （添加） it to the list.
Soon students are busy {{5}} posters. Two students are making phone calls. Then one student says {{6}} , “The animal center says that a family {{7}} a lost kitten named Lucky!” The class cheer （欢呼）. Twenty minutes later, a woman shows up and says with joy, “Thank you! We’ve been looking all over for our cat! He is very ‘lucky’ to be found （找到） by such a {{8}} group of students like you!”

blanks.why: 根据空格处后的“a quiet “meow””可知此处是表示听到猫叫。故选B。

blanks.mean: 你愿意在这个项目中带领全班同学吗？

blanks.why: 根据后文“She thinks of an idea and begins taking charge（她想到一个主意并开始负责）”可知, 老师叫珍妮做课题的领导。故选A。

blanks.why: 根据空格后的“lost kitten named Lucky”以及结合常识可知有家庭报告一只名叫Lucky的猫丢失了。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他很“幸运”, 能被像你们这样一群乐于助人的学生找到！
blanks.gloss: busy繁忙的；famous著名的；funny有趣的；helpful有帮助的。
