title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship
There are two children in my family. I am three years younger than my {{1}} Tova, and I think everything she does is great. When I was a kid, I liked to follow her and her friends around, hoping to become one of them, but there wasn't much {{2}} for a troublesome sister. Over time, there is a distance（距离）between us although we live in the same {{3}} .
So when she tells me she's going to China to study, I don't care much. But the first night after she leaves, I kept thinking that something is {{4}} . The house is too quiet. I feel just how different it is when she isn't at home. I cry sadly. But as the night falls, my tears turn into tears of calm（平静）, tears of {{5}} beginnings—I decide to do something.
I pick up the phone.
"Hello?" Her voice sounds familiar（熟悉的）.
"Hey, Tova. It's me. Sara. I'm just {{6}} to tell you I love you. "My words come out quickly. I know that if I stop in the middle, I won't {{7}} them. "I know we aren't as close as some sisters, but that doesn't mean I'm not missing you. "
After a long silence, she finally says, "Your voice makes me feel that you are by my side. "And before the call ends, she says very quickly, "I love you, too."
I never feel so {{8}} to have Tova as my sister. I'm hoping to see my sister back home this December.

blanks.mean: 我比我姐姐托娃小三岁。
blanks.why: 根据“There are two children in my family.”以及后文中提到“she”和“her”可知, 此处指的是“姐姐”, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 当我还是个孩子的时候, 我喜欢跟着她和她的朋友, 希望成为她们中的一员, 但是没有太多的空间给一个麻烦的妹妹。
blanks.why: 根据“When I was a kid, I liked to follow her and her friends around, hoping to become one of them”可知, 此处指的是“太多的空间”, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 随着时间的推移, 虽然我们住在同一所房子里, 但我们之间仍有一段距离。
blanks.why: 根据“But the first night after she leaves, I kept thinking that something is…The house is too quiet. I feel just how different it is when she isn't at home.”可知, 一家人应该是住在同一个房子里, 此处指的是“房子”, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 但她离开后的第一个晚上, 我一直觉得有什么事情不对。
blanks.why: 根据“The house is too quiet. I feel just how different it is when she isn't at home.”可知, 姐姐不在家, 感觉不对劲, 所以此处指的是“不对”, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 但是随着夜幕降临, 我难过的泪水变成了平静的泪水, 新的开始的泪水, 我决定要做些事情了。
blanks.why: 根据“my tears turn into tears of calm”以及“beginnings”可知, 此处指的是“新的”, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 我打电话只是想告诉你我爱你。
blanks.why: 根据“I pick up the phone.”可知, 此处指的是“打电话”, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 我知道如果我中途停下来, 我是不会把它们说完的。
blanks.why: 根据“My words come out quickly. I know that if I stop in the middle”可知, 此处指的是“说完”, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 有托娃做我姐姐, 我从来没有这么高兴过。
blanks.why: 根据前面的对话“ “I know we aren't as close as some sisters, but that doesn't mean I'm not missing you.” After a long silence, she finally says, “Your voice makes me feel that you are by my side.” And before the call ends, she says very quickly, “I love you, too.” ”以及“I'm hoping to see my sister back home thi

title: A Family Lesson
text:
It was a sunny morning. Daniel sat down at the table and had his favorite breakfast.
“What do you want to do today?” Daniel’s mom asked him.
“I’m going to play in the woods (树林) behind the house,” Daniel said.
Daniel quickly finished his {{1}} and ran to get dressed.
“Mom, I’ll be back later!”
When he opened the door, Daniel felt the {{2}} air. He smiled at the sun. Perfect weather to play, he thought. The leaves were just beginning to grow on the trees.
Daniel picked up a long stick (木棍) and used it to {{3}} a way through the woods. Suddenly, he saw something that wasn’t a rock or a leaf. When he got closer, he found a small bird among the fallen leaves. He looked around and saw its nest in a tree. He carefully climbed up the tree to get a closer look. He didn’t see any birds around. Then, he {{4}} to tell his mom about all this.
“Mom, I found a bird and it couldn’t move!” he told her as he hurried through the door.
She looked for a {{5}} and then she said, “Well, let’s go and have a look.”
Daniel took his mom back to the bird. His mom looked carefully at it.
“Let’s try to {{6}} it!” she said. She picked up the bird and put it in the box.
Then she said, “We can take it to the animal hospital in town.”
They took the bird to the animal hospital. After a few days, with the bird, an animal doctor {{7}} Daniel’s house.
The animal doctor said, “The bird is ready to go back to its home in the trees.”
Daniel was so {{8}} . He looked at the bird and said, “I’m happy you’re all right. I hope I can see you again. Bye!”

blanks.why: 根据“Perfect weather to play, he thought”可知, 暖和的天气适合玩耍, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 丹尼尔捡起一根长棍子, 用它在树林里开辟了一条路。
blanks.why: 根据“Daniel picked up a long stick (木棍) and used it to… a way through the woods”可知, 用棍子在树林中清出一条路, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 然后, 他跑去告诉他妈妈这一切。

blanks.why: 根据“with the bird, an animal doctor…Daniel’s house”可知, 动物医生带着鸟来到丹尼尔的家, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 丹尼尔如此兴奋。
blanks.gloss: interested感兴趣的；excited兴奋的；kind善良的；lucky幸运的。
blanks.why: 根据“The bird is ready to go back to its home in the trees”可知, 看到鸟儿被救了, 丹尼尔应该是兴奋的, 故选B。

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:
Children’s Day is coming and Mrs. Black is reading a newspaper story to her class. The story says: The doctors in Children’s Hospital are asking for money for children’s toys. Some children are ill and have to stay in hospital for many days. They feel {{1}} and always cry, but toys can make sick children feel happy and quiet.
After Mrs. Black reads the story she says, “This story gives me a(n) {{2}} .”
“You want us to {{3}} some money for the toys.” “We could bring some of our own toys for the children in hospital,” say the boys and girls one after another.
“Well, your ideas would be nice,” Mrs. Black says, “but my idea is {{4}} .”
“We could make some toys,” says one of them.
Mrs. Black smiles (微笑), “Do you think you could make toys?”
“Yes, yes,” the whole class answer.
“Great! Let’s begin to {{5}} toys tomorrow,” says Mrs. Black.
It is Children’s Day. Mrs. Black takes her students to the hospital with the toys made by themselves. The children in hospital feel happy and excited. The colorful toys make the white hospital more lively.
A few days later, Mrs. Black {{6}} another newspaper story to the class: The students of Class Three in Green Street School made toys and brought them to Children’s Hospital on June 1st. The doctor says, “Our children enjoy themselves playing with the toys. It’s really their happiest day. Thank you, Class Three. You bring the best {{7}} for Children’s Day.”
The whole class smile {{8}} , “We are happy too, for we make the best presents.”

title: Life is always about ups and downs
text:
Life is always about ups and downs, but life can leach you to grow.
About two years ago, I was taking part in the first Table Tennis Championships (锦标赛). I was quite {{1}} about myself. My opponent (对手) was very short and thin. The thoughts in my head were something like “She’s so short and of course I’ll {{2}} ”. When the match started, I found my opponent was really good at playing table tennis. With a smile on her face, she scored three points in the first ten seconds. I was so surprised, afraid and {{3}} everything my coach (教练) said. I only hoped not to lose the match. But the fact made me sad. I lost 0-3. I had never lost before. From then on, I was afraid of the {{4}} , and to me, her name was connected with failure (失败).
The experience (经历) lasted with me. I worked and trained harder than before. I listened to my coach carefully and made sure I was not overconfident (过于自信的). The following year, I {{5}} the same girl once again at the championships. As the competition started, I wasn’t afraid like the past match but {{6}} to my coach’s words. I did as my coach told me. The main thought in my head was not about winning or losing, but doing my best.
Finally, I won. My hard work and listening to my coach worked. My opponent had the same thin shape, but did not make me afraid anymore. She helped me find out who I {{7}} was.
From this experience, I learned not to be too proud (骄傲的). It is important to know the fact that there are people better than you. But with this idea in mind, you can work hard to become that person who is better. This experience also taught me not to judge (判断) others by their {{8}} . We should learn more from others, especially from our opponents.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson



David had never been on a plane because he was afraid of flying, and he had no plans of changing this.
One day, his father told him his mom was dying. Hearing the sad news, he hugged his father and {{1}} .
“Is there anything I can do to ease (缓解) her pain?” David asked.
Then the old man told him about his mother’s last {{2}} . His mother hoped to have a vacation in the Caribbean for fresh air.
“I’ll {{3}} for the vacation and buy the tickets now,” David said.
“Thank you, son. But your mother wants you to come along,” his father said. “Sorry, Dad. I’d love to, but I can’t get on a plane.”
His father was sad and left.
Seeing his father leaving didn’t trouble him that much, but the dream he had that night really did.
In his dream, his mom gently closed the door and left silently after hearing he couldn’t make the {{4}} together with them.
When he woke up, he thought about how his mother was always there for him. She always tried her best to {{5}} him at every special moment (特殊时刻) in his life.
Now it was his turn to be there for her, so he drove to the hospital and rushed to his mother’s room. Without thinking twice, he told his mother he was {{6}} to take a plane and join her during the vacation.
His mother smiled and asked, “What made you change your mind, son? Your father told me you weren’t coming with us.”
David told his mother about the {{7}} . He also told her giving up his fear of flying was the only thing he could do for her.
Shortly after the family vacation, David’s mother passed away (去世). While he was heart-broken, he was glad he got on that plane for his mother. It was {{8}} that made him get over the fear of flying.

text:
Well, that was bad, I thought as I took off my ballet shoes.

I had just finished my dance class, and it was {{1}} I always got the wrong steps, but all the others seemed to do these steps easily. I got the {{2}} : I had no gift and there was no need to push myself so hard.
Just then, my big sister Julissa arrived. She took one look at me and asked, “What’s wrong, Lakeisha?”
“Nothing,” I said {{3}} . “Just maybe I shouldn’t be taking dance classes.”
Julissa shook her head and said, “Let’s get out of here.” I went out of the door with her.
We stopped at a store and Julissa bought me my favorite drink. “Listen, sis,” she said, “not every day is a great one, and not everything is going to work out as you want. The most important is to keep {{4}} . I believe you can find your own dancing style.”
We finished our drinks and {{5}} to the subway. On the platform(站台), a few swing dancers were jumping and tapping happily. Many people stopped to watch. Then the dancers began showing off hip hop moves. One of them threw his hat onto my head. Without thinking, I quickly {{6}} the hat off, turned it inside out, and threw it right back at him.
“You have some moves, kid,” the dancer said as I just made a graceful(优雅的) turn. I looked over and there was my sister. Her {{7}} was as big as a subway platform.
When we arrived home, Julissa gave me a hug and said, “Never forget everyone has off days! Just believe yourself. You can finally get through at some point.”
“Guess that’s true,” I replied. “But not everyone is {{8}} enough to have a great sister to help them!”

She says we are going to write to some students of Grade Seven in {{3}} to see what life is like in England. That sounds so {{4}} ! I can’t wait to get started. Mrs. Snow hands out the {{5}} of our pen pals, and asks us to use what we learned about friendly letters to write to our pen pals. My pen pal’s name is Oliver.
The only things Mrs. Snow says we have to write in our letter are two {{6}} :“ Which holidays do you have in the year?” and “ What do you like to play?” We also have to answer those questions in {{7}} letters.
It takes a few weeks, but the day we get {{8}} back from our pen pals is an exciting (令人兴奋的) one! Oliver plays video games like we do over here. Their holidays are a lot of the {{9}} holidays we have, like April Fool’s Day! One holiday they celebrate (庆祝) that I don’t is Boxing Day. It is interesting to {{10}} what is the same and what is different about living in different countries. I can’t wait to learn more about my new pen pal!

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
Tony is badly ill in bed and has to stay at home for a few days. He feels very lonely（孤独的）because other children can’t come near and play {{1}} him.
There isn’t much to do at home. He just looks out of the window every day. At the moment, {{2}} sees a penguin（企鹅）eating a sandwich. The penguin says “good afternoon” to him and lies away quickly.
Tony is surprised（惊奇的）. He wants to {{3}} out what is going on outside. Suddenly, he sees a monkey playing with a balloon（气球）outside his window. For the next days, Tony is {{4}} to see more and more strange（奇怪的）animals. He has a good time when he watches them.
Soon, he gets well {{5}} goes back to school. He tells his fiends about all the strange things outside his window. While he is talking to his friends, he sees something in his friend’s {{6}} . Tony asks what it is and his friend shows it to him.
Inside the bag are many {{7}} that look like animals. His friends wear them to cheer Tony up when he is ill!
From that day on, Tony always does {{8}} best to make sure his friends never feel sad or lonely.

blanks.mean: 他感到很孤独, 因为其他孩子不能靠近他和他一起玩。
blanks.gloss: for为了；with带有, 附有；about关于；at在。
blanks.why: play with sb.“与某人一起玩”, 符合语境, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 这时, 他看见一只企鹅在吃三明治。
blanks.why: 根据上句“He just looks out of the window every day.”主语是he, 这里应该是他看见一只企鹅。故选D。

blanks.why: 根据后面“what is going on outside”应该是想弄清楚外面发生了什么事, find out“找出, 查明”, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 在接下来的几天里, 托尼很高兴看到越来越多的奇怪的动物。
blanks.gloss: happy开心的；cool酷的；sure确实；free自由的, 免费的。
blanks.why: 根据后面“to see more and more strange(奇怪的) animals”看见很多奇怪的动物, 应该很开心。故选A。

blanks.mean: 很快, 他康复了, 回到了学校。
blanks.why: 他康复了, 回到了学校, 表并列, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 当他和他的朋友聊天时, 他看到他朋友的书包里有东西。
blanks.gloss: jacket夹克衫；pencil boxs铅笔盒；schoolbag书包；hat帽子。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Inside the bag are”可知是包。故选C。

blanks.mean: 包里有许多看起来像动物模型。
blanks.why: 根据“look like animals”可知应该是像动物的模型。故选A。

blanks.mean: 从那天起, 托尼总是尽他最大的努力确保他的朋友们不再感到悲伤或孤独。
blanks.gloss: your你(们)的；their他们的；his他的；her她的。
blanks.why: 根据主语是Tony, 应该是他以后也会不让朋友们伤心。故选C。

title: The Reward of Helping Others
text:
The Reward of Helping Others
My friend Jack is doing math puzzles at the table with me. His grandma, Emma, is {{1}} in the kitchen. The good smell comes to our noses. We can’t wait(等待) to taste.
Emma says, “We are very {{2}} . We have quite a lot of food to eat and share(分享).”
“We have a good luck, {{3}} some people don’t have that.” Jack says. “Maybe we can do something to help.” I say. “It’s a big problem.”
After some discussion(讨论), we want to volunteer at a soup kitchen. Jack and I {{4}} about it because we didn’t do anything like this before.
The day comes and we have different {{5}} . Emma makes soup. Jack is in charge(负责) of the fruit salad, and I am on mashed-potato duty.
A man puts his plate in front of me. “Those potatoes look delicious,” he says. “They do smell good,” I put some mashed-potatoes on {{6}} plate and ask him, “ What do you get when an elephant steps(踩) on a potato?”
“Um, I am not sure.” “Mashed potatoes.”
“That’s funny!” he grins (笑),” “I’m David. Thank you {{7}} brightening(照亮) up my day.”
On our way home, Jack, Emma and I share stories about the interesting things we learned and the great people we {{8}} . We don’t need a lot of money to make a difference. We can donate (贡献) our time, and we would like to go back and help again sometime.

blanks.mean: 他的奶奶, 艾玛, 正在厨房里做饭。
blanks.why: 根据“in the kitchen”以及“The good smell”可知, 奶奶在厨房做饭, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 我们非常幸运。
blanks.gloss: popular受欢迎的；early早的；excellent精彩的；lucky幸运的。
blanks.why: 根据“We have a good luck”可知, 认为自己有食物吃很幸运, 故选D。

blanks.why: “We have a good luck”与“some people don’t have that”是转折关系, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 我和杰克很担心, 因为我们以前没做过。
blanks.why: 根据“because we didn’t do anything like this before”可知, 因为以前没做过所以有些担心, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 这一天到来了, 我们有了不同的工作。
blanks.why: 根据“Emma makes soup. Jack is in charge(负责) of the fruit salad, and I am on mashed-potato duty”可知, 每个人都有不同的分工, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 我在他的盘子里放了一些土豆泥, 然后问他。
blanks.why: 根据“ask him”可知, 是放在他的盘子里, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 谢谢你让我的一天充满欢乐。
blanks.why: thank you for sth“因为某事感谢你”, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 在回家的路上, 杰克、艾玛和我分享了我们学到的有趣的事情和遇到的极好的人的故事。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
I used to hate (曾经厌恶) running because I was always the last student to cross the finishing line. Then, in 2019, my friend asked me to run a 10 km﹣running event with him. “No. I hate {{1}} .” I immediately said.
Over the weekend I thought about his question. I thought, “Why do I hate running? I haven’t {{2}} it since I was in Grade 7.” Finally, I decided (决定) to have a try, so I told my friend I’d like to. He was pleased and advised (建议) me to look for a running program on the Internet to help me {{3}} how to run.
There were lots of running programs on the Internet. I chose a 14﹣week running program that would teach me how to {{4}} running for 30 minutes. I found it very easy to follow. I enjoyed following the program as I could see the improvement in my running each week. I went from not being able to run for more than 30 seconds to running for over 30 minutes. I went from hating running to {{5}} running.
On the day of the 10 km﹣running event I was both excited and nervous. {{6}} , it was time to put my new skills into practice. My friends and family came to support (支持) me. It was lovely to have them there. With their support and my training, I managed (设法) to finish the 10 km running in 72 minutes. It was hard but I felt very {{7}} for having tried it.
From this {{8}} I learnt it was a good idea to try something before saying I hated it.

blanks.mean: “不, 我讨厌跑步。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I used to hate (曾经厌恶) running”, 可知是讨厌跑步, 故选B。

blanks.why: 根据上文的描述“I found it very easy to follow. I enjoyed following the program as I could see the improvement in my running each week. I went from not being able to run for more than 30 seconds to running for over 30 minutes.” 可知, 作者在跑步上取得了恨到肩部, 所以应是有讨厌变为了喜欢, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 最后, 是时候把我的新技能付诸实践了。

blanks.mean: 这是很难的, 但我为尝试过它而感到非常自豪。

blanks.why: 根据“It was hard but I felt very … for having tried it.”由转折词but可知前后句之间表达的是转折关系, 虽然很难, 但完成之后作者感到很自豪, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 从这次经历中, 我明白了在说不喜欢某件事之前先尝试一下是个好主意。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
When I was thirteen years old, a girl gave me an important gift. It was a smile.
It was the early autumn of my first year at a new school. It’s also the first year of middle school. I was {{1}} here, so I felt nervous and afraid to make friends with anyone.
Every time I {{2}} the other students talking and laughing, I felt lonely. I could not talk to anyone about my {{3}} , and I didn’t want my parents to worry about me.
One day, my {{4}} talked happily with their friends, but I sat at my desk unhappily as usual. At that moment, a girl {{5}} the classroom. I didn’t know who she was. She walked by me and then turned back. She looked at me and without a word, {{6}} .
Suddenly, I felt the touch (触动)of something friendly. It made me feel happy, lively and {{7}} .
That smile {{8}} my life. I started to talk with other students. Day by day, I became closer to everyone in my class. The girl with the lucky smile has become my best {{9}} now. I can talk to her about my study, feeling and hobbies, pretty much everything. I am so lucky that I met such a nice girl.
One day, I asked her why she smiled at me that day. She said she could not {{10}} smiling at me! It doesn’t matter because all the dark days have gone.
Now I believe that the world is what you think it is. If you think you are lonely, you might always be alone. But if you smile at it, it will always smile back.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
通读下面短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的四个选项中, 选择最佳选项。


“I love flowers,” said Douglas, the bear. “Tulips (郁金香) are my favourite, but I love every flower.”
“Annie grows flowers in her garden (花园). She has beautiful tulips, big and red and all of her flowers smell (闻起来) so pretty.” said Shannon.
“I could bring it home and look at it all {{1}} and all night.” Douglas said.
When he came to Annie’s house, he saw the fence (篱笆).“I’ll sneak (溜) in so she doesn’t {{2}} me.”
Douglas walked to the back garden {{3}} . “Shannon was right. Those tulips are beautiful. I must have one.” Douglas pulled one of the tulips out of the {{4}} . He held it up to his nose and sniffed (闻) it. “This smells so lovely.” He looked at all the other flowers. “They’re all lovely. I don’t think Annie would mind (介意) if I picked (采摘) one or two.”
Douglas picked one flower and then another, and another, and he picked half her garden. “What shall I do?” He saw a wheel barrow, so he brought it back to the pile (大量,堆) of flowers and put them inside it. He pushed (推) the wheel barrow to his house, planted all the flowers in his garden and took the wheel barrow back to Annie’s house. Then he {{5}} a noise (响声).
“What are you doing? Where are all my lowers?” Annie stomped (跺) her foot on the ground angrily.
“I, uh, borrowed a few.”
“You borrowed my lowers? You stole (偷) half of them. Bring them back right now.” Annie said.
“But I love flowers. Yours are so pretty. I only wanted one, but I couldn’t {{6}} once (一旦) I started.” Douglas said.
“Bring my flowers back right now, or I’ll tell your mother,” Annie said.
“OK.” Douglas {{7}} all day long to re-plant them in her garden. After he finished, he said to Annie. “I’m {{8}} . I didn’t mean to take them all.”
Annie saw the flowers back in her garden. She said, “Douglas, you are welcome to come to my garden anytime you want and sit among (在……之中) the flowers. Just don’t take any without (没有) asking me.”
Douglas said that he wouldn’t. Every day he stopped by. He helped Annie water them and one day she ever let him take a bunch (束) of them home. Douglas never took anything else without asking.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
“What! I’m a boy. I can’t look after a baby!” I said to Mom. But she wasn’t listening.
“Don’t be difficult, it’s only for an afternoon. I will help your Aunt Judy with her birthday party.”
Mother said as she got ready to go out. Then the door closed and I was left alone with my {{1}} . So unfair (不公平), I thought. I should be out playing football with my classmates. I was quite {{2}} being the only child for thirteen years. Why did my parents have another kid?
When I was watching TV in the sitting room, I heard the cry of my sister. I remembered what Mother said, “ {{3}} swing the cradle (摇篮) and she will go back to sleep.” But it didn’t {{4}} . The baby was still crying. I put my left hand under her head and my right hand under her body the {{5}} Mother did it. And she stopped crying!
She was just lying there looking at me. Then I remembered the song Mother usually sang to her. So I began to {{6}} for her and she liked my voice very much.
She kept looking at my face and smiling whenever I looked back. “Maybe when you’re {{7}} we could watch TV together and I could teach you to play football.”
When Mother came home at 5 o’clock, she {{8}} on the baby. “You are a good big brother,” said Mother happily.
“And she’s a good baby sister.”

blanks.mean: 然后门关上了, 留下我一个人和我妹妹在一起。
blanks.why: 由“What! I’m a boy. I can’t look after a baby”可知我需要照顾一个孩子, 留下的应是比我年纪小的人, 所以应该是我的妹妹。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我很高兴做了十三年的独生子。
blanks.gloss: happy高兴的；shy害羞的；funny有趣的；sad悲哀的。
blanks.why: 由“Why did my parents have another kid”可知我抱怨父母有了另一个孩子, 说明之前作为独生子的我感觉很高兴和快乐。故选A。

blanks.mean: 仅仅摇动摇篮, 她就会睡着的。
blanks.why: 由“she will go back to sleep”可知只仅仅需要我摇动下摇篮, 她就会睡着。故选B。

blanks.mean: 但是这没有起作用。
blanks.gloss: stop停止；work工作, 起作用；move移动；go去。
blanks.why: 由“The baby was still crying”可知这种方法不起作用。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我放我左手在她的头下面, 右手在她的身体下面, 就像妈妈做的那样。
blanks.why: 根据句意可知就像妈妈做的那样, the way等同于as, 意为“就像……”, “the way+从句”相当于一个状语从句来修饰全句。故选D。

blanks.mean: 所以我开始给她唱歌, 并且她非常喜欢我的声音。
blanks.why: 由“Then I remembered the song Mother usually sang to her”可知我准备唱歌给她听。故选C。

blanks.mean: 或许当你再长大一点时, 我们能够一起看电视, 并且我能够教你踢足球。
blanks.gloss: bigger较大的；richer较富裕的；fatter较胖的；stronger较强壮的。
blanks.why: 由“we could watch TV together and I could teach you to play football”可知是说当妹妹再长大一点时, 能一起看电视, 踢足球。故选A。

blanks.mean: 当妈妈5点钟回家时, 她检查了这个婴儿。
blanks.why: 由“You are a good big brother”可知妈妈夸我是一个好哥哥, 是因为她检查过妹妹后发现我做得很好, 对我进行夸奖。故选C。 阅读理解

title: A Family Lesson
text:
I live in Mexico. In my country, corn（玉米）is my favourite food. We use it to make many kinds of food. Most {{1}} eat a tortilla. It is my {{2}} meal because my mother makes delicious food. Dinner is the time that the family sits at table. Sometimes we have tamales(玉米粉蒸肉). Tamales come from corn and banana with some chicken.
Many Mexican {{3}} wear white T-shirts and pants. Sometimes, they wear hats called “sombreros”. The sombreros keep them from the sun and rain. The women in Mexico usually {{4}} skirts and blouses.
Sports here are fun! They are {{5}} things to see! Our favourite sport is soccer! My father sometimes {{6}} me to watch soccer games. We can have a good time then.
We have seven to ten people in a {{7}} . The mother usually does the cooking and the cleaning. I’m glad that I’m only fourteen, or I have to {{8}} my room. That’s what I’m talking about!

blanks.mean: 大多数墨西哥人吃玉米饼。
blanks.gloss: Mexicans 墨西哥人；Chinese中国人；Americans美国人；Japanese日本人。
blanks.why: 根据上文中“I live in Mexico.”可知, 我生活在墨西哥, 所以此处是“大部分墨西哥人吃玉米饼”。故选A。

blanks.mean: 这是我最喜欢的一餐, 因为我妈妈会做美味的食物。
blanks.gloss: cheap便宜的；expensive昂贵的；favourite最喜爱的；terrible可怕的。
blanks.why: 根据句中“my mother makes delicious food”可知, 此处是“这是我最喜欢的一餐, 因为妈妈会做美味的食物”。故选C。

blanks.mean: 很多墨西哥男人穿白色T恤和裤子。
blanks.why: 根据下文中“The women in Mexico usually wear skirts and blouses.”可知, 下文中在讲墨西哥女人所穿的衣服, 所以此处是“墨西哥男人穿白色T恤和裤子”。故选C。

blanks.mean: 墨西哥的女人通常穿裙子和衬衫。
blanks.why: 根据句中“skirts and blouses”可知, 此处是“墨西哥女人通常穿裙子和衬衫”。故选D。

blanks.mean: 它们是值得一看的有趣的东西！
blanks.gloss: important 重要的；interesting有趣的；boring令人厌烦的；difficult困难的。
blanks.why: 根据上一句“Sports here are fun!”可知, 此处是“这里的体育运动是有趣的”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我父亲有时会带我去看足球比赛。
blanks.why: 根据句中“to watch soccer games”可知, 此处是“带我去看足球比赛”。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们家有七到十个人。
blanks.why: 根据句中“have seven to ten people”可知, 此处是“在一个家庭里有七到十个人”。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我很高兴我只有十四岁, 否则我就得打扫我的房间。
blanks.why: 根据上文中cleaning和句中or可知, 此处是“我只有十四岁, 要不然我就要打扫我的房间”。故选D。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
The end of the school year was coming quickly. Rick was so excited because it was time for the school play tryouts(选拔). This year's play was called Mystery at the Lighthouse. Rick was hoping to get the lead part(主角) of Joe who lives at the lighthouse.
After school, students who wanted to try out for the {{1}} met in the gym at 3:30. Rick and his friend Kevin, sat and waited for their turn to read for the play. The next day the parts were {{2}} on the wall outside of the gym. Kevin got a part in the play. But Rick did not see his {{3}} .
He felt funny inside. Rick was sure he would get the part. “I can’t understand why I’m not in the play,” said Rick to his mom. “Rick, it just means that someone was a little better than you. You shouldn’t give up! Look at all the other things you’re good at, you’re great with {{4}} and you’re a super football player,” said Mom. Rick didn’t say any words and went to his room.
The next day at school Mr. Carter, the art teacher, asked Rick, “I know how good you are in art. Are you interested in doing some drawing for the play?” “You want me to draw for the play?” asked Rick. “I sure do,” said Rick {{5}} . Rick was so happy about being part of the play again. Rick stayed after school each day for the next week and drew a big lighthouse and painted it. He also drew some boats in the water and painted those too. He was so excited on the night of the play. When it was time for the play, he {{6}} from the side of the stage as his friend, Kevin, said his part of the play. At the end of the show, Mr. Carter called all the students onto the stage that helped with the artwork, lights, and {{7}} things around on stage during this time. Rick felt {{8}} of his work. He thought he would do the artwork better. It was so much fun.

blanks.mean: 放学后, 想参加演出选拔的学生在3:30在体育馆集合。
blanks.why: 根据“the school play tryouts”可知是戏剧表演得选拔, 用play符合语境。故选C。

blanks.mean: 第二天, 这些角色就被贴在了体育馆外面的墙上。
blanks.gloss: posted邮寄, 贴；lost丢失；picked捡起；written写。
blanks.why: 根据“Kevin got a part in the play.”可知选拔结果出来了, 应是贴在墙上, 用posted符合语境。故选A。

blanks.mean: 但是Rick没有看到他的名字。
blanks.gloss: picture图片；artwork插画, 艺术作品；house房子；name名字。
blanks.why: 根据“I can’t understand why I’m not in the play”可知Rick落选了, 应是没看到自己的名字, 用name符合语境。故选D。

blanks.mean: 看看你所擅长的其他方面, 你擅长美术, 你还是个超级足球运动员…… act动作；speech演讲；art美术, 艺术；music音乐。
blanks.why: 根据“I know how good you are in art.”可知Rick擅长美术, 用art符合语境。故选C。

blanks.mean: “我当然愿意, ”Rick兴奋地说。
blanks.gloss: sadly难过地；excitedly兴奋地；easily容易地；worriedly担忧地。
blanks.why: 根据“Rick was so happy about being part of the play again.”可知Rick为能参与戏剧而高兴, 他应该是兴奋的。故选B。

blanks.mean: 到了开演的时间, 他在舞台的一边看着他的朋友Kevin表演他在剧中的角色 watched观看；moved移动；noticed注意：followed跟随。
blanks.why: 根据“as his friend, Kevin, said his part of the play”可知朋友在表演时候, 他在观看, 用watched符合语境。故选A。

blanks.mean: 演出结束时, Mr. Carter把所有的学生都叫到台上, 在这段时间里, 他们帮助布置艺术品、灯光和移动舞台上的东西。
blanks.why: 根据“things around on stage”可知是在舞台上移动东西, 用moving符合语境。故选D。

blanks.mean: Rick为自己的工作感到自豪 tired疲劳的；proud骄傲的；surprised惊讶的；afraid害怕的。
blanks.why: 根据“Mr. Carter called all the students onto the stage”可知Rick站到了舞台上, 他应该很骄傲, 用proud符合语境。故选B。

title: Working Toward a Dream
text:
New Land, New Home

Joe immigrated(移民) to Canada at the age of 41. There were many stressful days as he had his whole family to take care of. He rented an apartment and bought a few pieces of furniture and some cookware.
Since he had no {{1}} , the savings they brought with them were diminishing(减少) rapidly. They needed to buy groceries and pay the rent After getting his family settled, Joe went out to look for a job.
As he walked, he saw many things on the street that people threw away on garbage day---TVs, washers, furniture and refrigerators. Joe could not believe his eyes. “Why would people get rid of such things?” he asked himself. Seeing all the “junk”, Joe decided to take the {{2}} home to see what the problem was. After all, he was an electrician before he came to Canada.
Since he was twelve years old, Joe’s main hobby has been electronics. He assembled a radio back in the 1970s which was quite something for a {{3}} boy.
Now, he had no job and no income. All he had was time and his hobby. He plugged the television into a wall plug. There were images on the screen, {{4}} there was no sound. He opened the back cover using the tools he’d brought with him. Before long, Joe diagnosed the {{5}} . The loudspeaker was broken.
He went out again. And there was garbage placed on the sidewalk waiting to be picked up in the morning. He found a toy keyboard. He was delighted and carried the keyboard home. The keyboard didn’t
 {{6}} , but luckily its loudspeaker did. Fifteen minutes later, Joe had a TV with both picture and sound.
Joe began to question people why they threw away so many electronics. The {{7}} was the same from everyone: repair services were too expensive. He discovered that people would rather buy new products.
Joe made up his mind to open an electronics repair shop that would offer fair(公平的) prices.
Today, Joe has much success in his new country. He could have lost hope. Instead, he chose to make the best out of a {{8}} situation.

blanks.mean: 因为他没有工作。
blanks.why: 根据the savings they brought with them were diminishing(减少) rapidly. 他们带来的存款在快速的减少, 可知是没有工作；故选B。

blanks.mean: 乔伊决定把这个电视带回家看看问题是什么。
blanks.why: 根据后文 He plugged the television into a wall plug.他把电视机插上电源；可知是电视；故选C。

blanks.mean: 他在20世纪70年代组装了一台收音机, 那对一个十几岁的孩子来说是非常了不起的。
blanks.why: 根据Since he was twelve years old, Joe’s main hobby has been electronics.自从他12岁, 乔伊的主要爱好是电气, 可知是十几岁的孩子；故选A。

blanks.mean: 但是没有声音。
blanks.why: 根据There were images on the screen屏幕上有图像, 和there was no sound.没有声音, 这两句之间是转折关系；故选C。

blanks.mean: 乔伊判断出了问题是什么。
blanks.why: 根据The loudspeaker was broken喇叭坏了, 可知是诊断出问题, 需要解决；故选B。

blanks.mean: 这个琴键不工作了。
blanks.why: 根据 but luckily its loudspeaker did但是幸运的是, 它的喇叭工作；根据上文在街上捡回的东西, 应该是坏的, 所以是不工作；故选C。

blanks.mean: 每个人的答案是一样的。
blanks.why: 根据上文Joe began to question people why they threw away so many electronics.乔伊开始问人们为什么扔那么多电器, 可知是答案是一样的；故选B。

blanks.mean: 他选择充分利用来脱离困境。
blanks.why: 根据上文一开始没工作, 存款急剧减少, 可知是困难情况；故选D。 阅读理解

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship
Dear Annie,
Thank you for your letter. I'm happy you like your school.
I {{1}} our school in China, too. I go to school from Monday to Friday. We {{2}} four classes in the morning and two classes in the {{3}} . We have many interesting things to do after class. On Monday afternoon, we play sports. We {{4}} basketball or ping pong. It's relaxing（放松的）! On Tuesday afternoon, some of us have a singing class, and on Thursday afternoon, some have a {{5}} class. It's a little difficult（困难的）. But I can draw {{6}} pictures. On Wednesday afternoon, our English class finishes（结束, 完成） at 4: 00. My Chinese friends want to talk with me in {{7}} . They think I look like an English teacher. I like Friday best because I can learn Beijing Opera on {{8}} afternoon. It is great!
On Saturdays and Sundays, I don’t go to school. Very often I go to the park and have a good time with my family there.
Best wishes!
Yours,
Henry

blanks.mean: 我也喜欢我们中国的学校。
blanks.why: 根据“I'm happy you like your school”及“too”, 可知, 作者也喜欢自己的学校, 故选B。 18题详解】 句意：我们上午有四节课, 下午有两节课 give给；get得到；have有；want想要。根据“four classes”, 可知, 上午有四节课, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们上午有四节课, 下午有两节课。
blanks.why: 根据“in the morning”, 可知, 前面提到了上午, 此处应该描述下午, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 我们打篮球或打乒乓球。
blanks.why: 根据“basketball or ping pong”, 可知, 此处表示“打篮球或打乒乓球”, 英文表达为play basketball“打篮球”, play ping pong“打乒乓球”, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 在周四下午, 一些人上画画课。
blanks.why: 根据“ It's a little difficult”及“But I can draw…pictures”, 可知, 对其他人有点困难, 但是作者擅长画画, 说明此空提到的是上画画课, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 但是我可以画漂亮的画。
blanks.why: 根据“ It's a little difficult”及“But I can draw…pictures”, 可知, 对其他人来说画画有点困难, 但是作者可以画出漂亮的画, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 我的中国朋友想用英语跟我聊天。
blanks.why: 根据“They think I look like an English teacher”, 可知, 作者看起来像一名英语老师, 所以朋友都想用英语跟他聊天, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 我最喜欢星期五, 因为我可以在星期五的下午学习京剧。
blanks.gloss: Tuesday星期二；Wednesday星期三；Friday星期五；Sunday星期日。
blanks.why: 根据“I like Friday best”, 可知, 最喜欢星期五, 说明在星期五下午可以学习京剧, 故选C。 阅读理解

title: A Family Lesson
text:
It is time to go home from the park, and the cars are waiting for the boys. But Mike is not going to get into the car because he can not find his dog Rocky anywhere. He calls and calls, but the little dog does not {{1}} .
All the other boys help Mike {{2}} Rocky. But no one can find the little black and white dog, and at last Mike has to go home without him.
“Maybe Rocky goes home,” says one of the boys.
But Mike does not find Rocky at home. “He may find his way home tomorrow morning,” says Mike’s father. “The park is so far away, I don’t think Rocky can find his way home. I can {{3}} see him again,” says Mike. He is very {{4}} . And his parents are sorry for him.
“Come and eat your dinner now,” says his mother. “We will all look for Rocky tomorrow morning.”
But Mike can’t eat his dinner. He keeps thinking about his lost dog.
Just then he hears the telephone ringing and runs to {{5}} it. A man is talking.
“Hello,” says the man. Do you have a little black and white dog? A boy tells me your dog runs away.”
“Oh, yes,” says Mike. “His name is Rocky. I can’t find him today at the {{6}} .”
“He is here at my house,” says the man.
“Thank you! Can you put him up to the {{7}} ?” says Mike.
“Just a minute,” says the man. “Here he is!”
“Hello, Rocky!” says Mike.
“Bow-wow, bow-wow!” answers Rocky.
The man says “Rocky {{8}} you. He is trying to get out of the house. Please come and get him at No.3 Park Road. Goodbye.”
Mike goes to get Rocky with his father excitedly.

blanks.mean: 他叫了又叫, 但是小狗没来。
blanks.why: 根据后文“But no one can find the little black and white dog”可知, 大家都没找到狗, 所以此处表示小狗没回来。故选A。

blanks.mean: 所有其他的男孩帮助迈克寻找洛基。
blanks.gloss: look after照顾；look up向上看, 查阅；look for寻找；look at看。
blanks.why: 根据前文“But Mike is not going to get into the car because he can not find his dog Rocky anywhere.”可知, 迈克找不到洛基了, 所以其他男孩帮助迈克寻找洛基。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我再也见不到他了。
blanks.why: 根据前句“The park is so far away, I don’t think Rocky can find his way home.”可知, 公园太远了, 迈克认为洛基找不到回家的路, 所以再也见不到洛基了。故选D。

blanks.mean: 他很伤心。
blanks.gloss: happy开心的；sad悲伤的；funny滑稽的；fine好的。
blanks.why: 结合上下文及“And his parents are sorry for him.”可知, 狗丢了, 迈克很伤心, 他的父母也为他感到难过。故选B。

blanks.mean: 就在这时, 他听到电话铃响, 跑过去接电话。
blanks.gloss: return归还；carry携带；answer回答, 接电话；move移动。
blanks.why: 根据前半句“Just then he hears the telephone ringing”可知, 电话响了, 所以迈克去接电话。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我今天在公园找不到他。
blanks.why: 根据前文“It is time to go home from the park”可知, 在公园丢了狗, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 你能让他来听电话吗？
blanks.why: 根据后文“‘Bow-wow, bow-wow!’ answers Rocky.”可知, 迈克请男士让洛基接电话。故选C。

blanks.mean: 洛基听见你了。
blanks.why: 分析语境可知, 捡到洛基的男士是打电话给迈克的, 并且迈克在电话里叫洛基的名字, 所以洛基通过电话听到了。故选B。 阅读理解

title: A Family Lesson
text:
I was in fifth grade. One day, my dad’s car was broken into and all of the things inside were stolen(偷), including my schoolbag. It had my binder, my textbooks and my notebooks where I used to write stories. I was really {{1}} .
I had to go to school with nothing the next day. My teacher, Miss Taylor, was very kind to me. She gave me a new binder(活页夹) after I told her what had happened. She also {{2}} me some crayons and asked me if I’d like to color the front of the binder. I really appreciated her kindness.
But I never did {{3}} the new binder because something even better happened later that same day. Miss Taylor got a call from the office. After she hung up the phone, she said {{4}} , “Zoe, a miracle(奇迹) has happened! Someone found your schoolbag!” I ran to the office and got my {{5}} . Mrs. Black lends her two. In the afternoon, there is another knock at the door. Mrs Black opens it and sees a {{4}} standing there. “My name is Jack White,”he says. "My mother sends (送) you this cake and the two eggs.Well, thank you, Jack,”says Mrs Black. "Come in and {{5}} my son Bob.” Jack gets in the room and talks with Bob happily.
Look! Bob and Jack are {{6}} the cake and milk. They are playing football. Now they are friends! Jack says, “I'm glad you live next door.” Bob says, “I must thank your mother for coming for eggs.”Jack laughs and tells Bob,"She doesn't want the two eggs, but she wants to make friends with your mother. Bob says, “That's a(n) {{7}} way to make friends. It's an easy way, too. It can work!”

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Once there was a little girl Lily, who was very friendly and popular in her class. She was friends with everyone in her class. There was no one in class who didn't {{1}} her.
She was very {{2}} and would always be busy with her friends. She felt very happy that she had so many friends at school.
On Friendship Day, their class organized an event, in which everyone had to prepare three {{3}} and give them to their best friends. Lily was very happy for the coming Friendship Day and was expecting gifts from her {{4}} .
However, when all gifts were shared in class, she was the only one who didn't receive any gift! She felt {{5}} and cried a lot. She thought to herself how it was possible. She had made so much effort (努力) to be friends with everyone but in the end no one thought of her as one of their best friends.
Everyone came and tried to comfort (安慰) her but each one only stayed for a short time before {{6}} . This was exactly what Lily had done so many times to others.
When she got home seeing her sad face, her mother asked her why she looked so down. She questioned, "Where can I {{7}} true friends?"
Her mother was surprised at her question. Then Lily told her about the day in school. Her mother comforted her and said, "You cannot get real friends with a smile or a few good words. if you really want true friends, you will have to {{8}} them real time and love. For a true friend, you must always be there, in good times and bad. There just isn't enough {{9}} to be there for everyone, so it's only possible to have some true friends."
With tears in her eyes, Lily got to know what makes {{10}} friends. She nodded and made up her mind to do something different.

blanks.why: 根据前文“have some true friends.”可知, 应该是真正的朋友, 故选B。 【点睛】做完型填空时, 首先要通读课文, 明白主旨大意, 然后再做题。做完型时要记住“瞻前顾后想结果”这一原则, 根据上下文以及语境做题, 切忌主观臆断。另外, 平时还要多多积累词汇。完型填空常考名词、动词、形容词和副词等辨析。做词义辨析题时, 首先要确认四个选项的含义, 然后分析语境和逻辑关系, 确定答案。 例如题目8中, 首先确定四个选项含义, tell告诉；sell卖；give给；teach教, 根据后文“them real time and love.”可知, 应该是给, 故选C。 阅读理解 阅

title: A Family Lesson
text:
完形填空（共8分,每小题8分）阅读下面的短文,掌握其大意,然后从下面各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中,选择可以填入空白处的最佳选项。

Romain Rolland once said, “There is only one kind of heroism in the world, and that is to still love life after recognizing the truth of life.” Cai Lei, a patient with ALS (渐冻症), perfectly {{1}} this sentence.
Cai Lei was once the vice president of Jingdong Group, with a {{2}} job and a happy family.
But who would have thought that at the age of 41, he was diagnosed (诊断) with ALS and could only watch his body “frozen” until he could not breathe.
The illness gave him a fatal (致命的) wound but he didn’t want to bow to it. He began to think about {{3}} he could do for the people with ALS in the remaining days.
After much thought, Cai Lei {{4}} an idea: he wants to produce medicine that is good for the treatment of ALS.
When Cai Lei told others about this idea, everyone thought he was {{5}} . You know medicine development takes at least 10 years. {{6}} , the period from diagnosis to death of patients with ALS is no more than 5 years. Allowing patients at the moment to use medicine is impossible.
What’s worse, many people in society still misunderstand him. That misunderstanding is like a {{7}} , burning Cai Lei’s heart.
Although he is heartbroken, he never says anything for himself. He devotes himself to the research and development of the {{8}} . He believes: “Even if we can’t use this medicine, we should let our future generations use it.”

blanks.why: 根据“he wants to produce medicine”以及“...the research and development of...”可知, 此处表示药物的研究和开发。故选C。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Jim, a successful businessman, told us the experience of his childhood (童年).
When he was 12, his parents died. He was {{1}} and didn’t get on well with others. People always laughed at him. No one showed kindness to him. His only friend was a dog named Lucky.
One day as he walked down the street, a young lady was walking in front of him. Suddenly one of her bags dropped (掉落) from her arms. As she stopped to {{2}} it up, she dropped other bags. He came to help her. “Thank you, dear! You are a nice little boy!” she said kindly, smiling.
A {{3}} feeling came to him. These were the first kind words that he never heard them before. He {{4}} her until she went far away, and then he whistled (吹口哨) to his dog and went directly to the river nearby.
“Thank you, dear! You are a nice little boy!” he repeated (重复) the woman’s words. Then he said them to his dog in a low voice, “You are a nice little dog!” Lucky raised its ears and it seemed that it {{5}} the boy’s words.
“Uh! Even a dog likes it!” he said, “Well, Lucky, I won’t say unkind words to you any more.” Lucky wagged its tail happily.
The boy thought and thought. Finally he looked at himself in the river. He saw nothing but a dirty boy. He washed his {{6}} carefully. Again he looked. He saw a clean face. He was amazed. From then on, he had a new {{7}} .
After telling this, the businessman stopped for a while, and then he said, “Ladies and gentlemen, this is the very place, where that kind woman {{8}} the first seed (种子) of kindness in me there. All of us should learn about kindness. What a great power it has!” If you show kindness to others, you will be an able man.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

David had to make the pie for tonight’s dinner. His parents were busy, so they {{1}} him the task. However, he didn’t make a pie before. His mother put all the foods for making the pie and cooking tools out on the table in the kitchen, along with a {{2}} . It said, “Follow the recipe!”
How {{3}} could it be anyway? He read the instructions (说明) on the back of the can of pumpkin pie filling. It didn’t seem bad. He preheated the oven and then began with the pie.
First, he got the pie filling, the milk and two eggs and put them into a bowl. Next, he stirred (搅拌) them {{4}} to make sure the filling stayed in the bowl.
Then he poured the filling into the pie crust (外壳), but there was a little extra (额外). He {{5}} all the instructions, so he wasn’t sure why there was any extra at all.
He put the pie into the oven. Then he waited 15 minutes, and turned the oven down. Now it was a waiting game, because he needed to wait 50~60 minutes, but he wouldn’t know if the pie was ready without {{6}} it.
After 50 minutes, he opened the {{7}} , and stuck (插入) a toothpick into the filling. It came out a bit wet, so he let the pie cook five more minutes. This time, the toothpick came out clean.
He took the pie out of the oven and set it on his mother’s pie cooling rack. He felt pretty good about himself. The pie smelled great and everything turned out {{8}} .
Suddenly, he had an idea. He read the cookbook and looked for pumpkin recipes. He wanted to cook with the extra pumpkin pie filling.

blanks.mean: 他的父母很忙, 所以把任务留给了他。
blanks.why: 根据“His parents were busy,”可知, 此处是指父母把任务留给了大卫。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他的母亲把所有做馅饼的食物和烹饪工具都放在厨房的桌子上, 还有一张纸条。
blanks.why: 根据下文“It said, ‘Follow the recipe!’”可知, 此处是指一张便条。故选B。

blanks.mean: 这能有多难呢？
blanks.gloss: surprising令人惊讶的；boring无聊的；hard难的；exciting令人兴奋的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“Follow the recipe!”可知, 此处是指按照食谱做, 所以感觉不难。故选C。 16题详解】 句意：接着, 他小心地搅拌, 确保馅料留在碗里。 carefully小心地；politely有礼貌地；sadly难过地；kindly亲切地。根据下文“make sure the filling stayed in the bowl”可知, 此处是指小心地搅拌。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他遵循了所有的说明, 所以他不确定为什么会有额外的东西。
blanks.why: 根据“all the instructions”可知, 此处是指按照说明做。故选D。

blanks.mean: 现在, 这是一场等待游戏, 因为他需要等待50—60分钟, 但如果不检测一下, 他就不知道馅饼是否做好了。
blanks.why: 根据下文“stuck a toothpick into the filling. It came out a bit wet, so he let the pie cook five more minutes.”可知, 大卫用牙签插进饮料的方法来检测馅饼是不是做好了。故选B。

blanks.mean: 50分钟后, 他打开烤箱, 把一根牙签插进馅料里。
blanks.why: 根据上文“He put the pie into the oven.”可知, 此处是指打开烤箱。故选B。

blanks.mean: 馅饼闻起来很香, 一切都很完美。
blanks.gloss: difficult困难的；strange奇怪的；traditional传统的；perfect完美的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“He felt pretty good about himself. The pie smelled great”可知, 大卫自我感觉良好, 馅饼闻起来很香, 一切都完美。故选D。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
On my father’s birthday, my parents and I went out for dinner. The restaurant was very noisy, with lots of diners. Waiters moved {{1}} between the tables.
We had just ordered our meals when suddenly all the {{2}} in the restaurant went out. The place went completely dark. All the conversations in the restaurant stopped for a moment, and then everybody started {{3}} together again. “What’s happened to the lights?” “Ooh, it’s a blackout!” Some people laughed, and others seemed a little worried.
Then the restaurant manager came in, holding a candle. He spoke to all the diners, “Ladies and gentlemen, I am very sorry for this. Our power (电力) has gone out. The power has gone out across the whole neighborhood, and we don’t know when it will be restored. Please be {{4}} . Our waiters will bring candles so that you can continue with your evening.”
The waiters came in with candles and {{5}} them on the tables. One of the diners asked, “What about our meals?”
“Don’t worry, sir,” replied the manager. “Fortunately, we use gas in our kitchen, not electricity, so the chef can continue cooking all your meals.”
My father said to me, “Let’s go out to the street and take a look.”
He and I went out of the front door and looked up and down the street. Sure enough, it was in total {{6}} .
We went back in and sat at the table. Our faces were {{7}} up by the candlelight. The waiter brought our meals and we started eating.

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship
Daisy enjoyed walking around with her long black hair. She enjoyed the attention from her friends. Daisy never wanted to {{1}} it ever again. This would all change after listening to a speech on a Saturday morning.
That day, Daisy learned about a hospital that specialized in treating children with serious illnesses. Children there hold the {{2}} to have their hair like the other children at their age.
The speech touched Daisy {{3}} , and she knew she had to do something to help these children feel happy and beautiful.
Daisy decided to donate (捐赠) her long hair to the sick children in the hospital. The next day, Daisy arrived at a salon (美发厅) with a big smile on her face, {{4}} to cut her hair. Then she let the hairdresser begin his work.
Stephen, the hairdresser in the salon was amazed at Daisy’s idea because of the length of her hair. After listening to Daisy’s explanation, he {{5}} his friend who had such an illness, and he understood how important it was for these children to feel beautiful and confident, even if it was just for a little while.
A few days later, as Stephen worked his magic on the children’s hair, everyone in the hospital felt excited. The children looked beautiful and happy, and their families {{6}} Daisy for her act of kindness. The story of Daisy’s donation spread throughout Huntsvile, and soon, other children began donating their {{7}} to the hospital as well. The community supported these children and gave them books for their kind act.
Daisy’s long hair became a symbol (象征) of hope and love for all those who received them. She {{8}} away her hair. In return, happiness came to her from making others feel special and loved.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

“Look! How cute he is!” Jack cried, looking into the pet shop. “Wouldn’t it be great to have a puppy running around the house?”
His mum and dad looked at one another. “Come on, Jack. We’ve got to get a move on,” his dad said, hoping to change the {{1}} . “We have to get to the shops before they close, or there’ll be no dinner tonight.”
Jack’s parents hoped that would have been the end of it, but Jack didn’t give up. “Can we please buy Pluto?” Jack asked again the following week. “He needs a good {{2}} and we’ve got the perfect backyard for him.”
His parents were prepared with an answer this time. “I don’t think so, Jack.” Dad replied (回答) {{3}} , “Do you remember what happened with Rupert? Before we took him home, you {{4}} us the same thing. After a couple of weeks, you stopped cleaning his cage (笼子), and later you didn’t even remember to {{5}} the poor little thing. In the end it was your mother and I who had to look after him.”
“This will be different. A dog will be a better friend. We can do things together” Jack explained. But his mum and dad still didn’t {{6}} him. Jack wasn’t about to give up. He borrowed books from the library on dog care. He also remembered to do all his chores (家务).
Two weeks passed and Jack’s parents were beginning to seem more {{7}} to the idea of having a new pet. They decided to give Jack the chance to show if he was responsible (负责的) enough to look after a dog.
“Mr and Mrs Clark have agreed to lend us Buster for a week,” Dad said. “You will be able to show us how well you look after him.”
Jack could hardly {{8}} his excitement. He wasn’t going to mess (搞砸) this up.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Joaquin and his mother caught the bus every day to his new school after moving to England. Joaquin didn’t know much English. When they got on the bus, his mom would buy {{1}} .
Every morning she would say “Two returns to Blackfriars”. When they got off the bus, she would make Joaquin say “Thank you very much”. Joaquin wanted to {{2}} his English before he spoke it, but he never took the chance to practice.
One day, Joaquin’s mother caught a cold and had a bad cough. She told Joaquin to buy tickets.
Joaquin took a deep breath. He stepped onto the bus. With a sudden burst of confidence, Joaquin said in his most polite voice, “Two tickets to Blackfries, please.”
The bus driver was confused, “Blackfries?”
Joaquin felt his face go red, “To Blackfries. My school is at Blackfries.”
“Do you mean Blackfriars?”
“Yes.”
Once he had paid for their tickets, he {{3}} himself behind his mom and covered his face. Joaquin felt ashamed (羞愧的). When they got off the bus, Joaquin didn’t say “Thank you” to the bus driver like he usually did.
For the rest of the day, Joaquin was {{4}} and upset. When Joaquin’s mother came to school to {{5}} him, she noticed that her son was unhappy.
“Joaquin, what’s wrong?”
“I’ve been worried all day about my English. I tried to {{6}} you, but I couldn’t do it. I want my English to be perfect, but I find it scary to speak. I want to go home.”
“It’s okay, my love,” Joaquin’s mother said {{7}} , “You don’t need to be perfect. You just need to be confident.” She smiled,“You are doing so well, and I am proud of you. Don’t give up, Joaquin.”
Joaquin nodded.
The bus arrived to take them home. When they reached their stop, he confidently thanked the bus driver with a bright smile. The bus driver smiled and thanked him back. As Joaquin and his mother walked home, he realized that if he had enough {{8}} and held his head high, then he could do anything.

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
Sam and his family were spending their holiday at the seaside. When Sam and his grandma stood on the beach watching the sunrise, a perfect shell {{1}} ashore (上岸). Sam quickly picked it up and turned it over. Inside, the shell was as pink as a rabbit’s ear!
“It is a gift from the sea,” said Grandma, “Take good care of it.” “I will,” said Sam.
Sam {{2}} showed his treasure to his family. His parents loved it, but his brother Vikram thought it was nothing special.
The next day, Sam {{3}} the shell on the shelf in their cottage (小屋) and then went with his family to the boardwalk. Vikram didn’t go with them, because he was busy taking pictures.
At the boardwalk, Sam saw shells on sale, but none were as {{4}} as his. Back at the cottage, he ran to his room to admire (欣赏) the shell. But it was gone!
“Dad, where is my shell?” Sam cried.
“Where did you put it?” Dad asked.
“I put it on the shelf but it’s not there!” answered Sam. Then something caught his eye...under Vikram’s bed. “Vikram took it,” he said.
“I did not!” shouted Vikram. “I was taking pictures at the beach. Who cares about your {{5}} shell?”
Sam didn’t say a word but quietly hid the shell under his clothes in a drawer. He checked on his {{6}} twice before everyone went to the beach for the last time.
That afternoon, Sam and his family packed (收拾行李) to go home. Sam opened his drawer only to find his shell gone again.
During dinner, Sam {{7}} his family. He thought someone was hiding his shell. Who? And why?
Suddenly, his missing shell walked into the room. “Look!” said Sam, pointing.
Everyone looked. The shell that was pink inside now had {{8}} that raced for the door. It turned out to be a hermit crab. Everyone was amazed. Sam ran over and picked it up. “I’ll call you Sandy,” said Sam. “You can live at my house.”
“He already has a home,” said Grandma.
Sam {{9}} how his shell had washed up from the ocean. That was Sandy’s real home. That was where he wanted to be.
“Grandma, will you come to the beach with me again? I have to {{10}} a gift.” Grandma smiled.

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:
I looked out at the smiling faces packed into the school gym. The applause (掌声) filled my ears. I had done it. I had really done it! I found a new person inside me, a much more confident, outgoing person who had been hidden all along, just waiting for the {{1}} to appear.
Just a few months earlier, it was impossible to {{2}} myself acting in a play in front of two hundred people. But without my teacher, Mrs. Sather, I couldn’t get that chance.
In the first and second grade, I was extremely shy. But Mrs. Sather always {{3}} me.
One day, she announced, “Our class was going to {{4}} a play. Anybody, want to try?”
A few excited hands shot up—mine, of course, was not one of them.
After school she stopped me and invited me for a talk. Puzzled, I followed her to her desk. She said, “I think you are {{5}} for the lead character. But I was surprised you didn’t raise your hand.”
Me, the lead? Was she crazy?
Mrs. Sather gazed into my eyes as if seeing my inner {{6}} locked away inside. “But I’d like you to give this a try for me,” she continued. “If you reach for the stars, you might at least grab a piece of the moon.”
I realized it was time to throw off {{7}} and show the world who I really was. I looked Mrs. Sather right in her sparkling blue eyes and said, “OK. I’ll try.”
In the following months, in spite of fears, I did everything I could to prove I could do it in practice.
At the end of the play, when the audience applauded, I knew they were not just cheering for my performance that night, but for the performances they knew would come in later years because of my new-found {{8}} .

title: Working Toward a Dream
text:
After years of experience, Brenda faced a big challenge(挑战)in Sunday School, and she just didn’t know how to {{1}} it in a good way. She had never been able to touch the heart of a child called Cindy!
Cindy was quite different. She came from a broken home. And although she was really {{2}} she thought she was so bad that she could not be successful. In fact, Cindy needed care, and most of all Cindy needed love! There just had to be a way of {{3}} her. Day after day, Brenda would pray for Cindy, yet Sunday would come and go and she saw little change.
Then one day Brenda asked Cindy if she could {{4}} a role in a Christmas programme the children were planning to do. Cindy’s answer was, “Don’t you think you can find someone better than me?”
“Better than you?” came Brenda’s reply. “What makes you think there is {{5}} better than you? ”
“Well, I’ve {{6}} been asked to do anything before because I’m not good. I won’t get the part right and then everyone will be mad at me for messing up(弄糟) their {{7}} ,” came Cindy’s answer.
“Oh, Cindy,” said Brenda in a gentle voice. “I am so {{8}} that you think like that, but you are so wrong. Don’t you realize how clever you are?”
“No,” Cindy replied in a low voice because she was now in tears.
“But Cindy, in my eyes, you are special and you can also do something well like others,” Brenda said.
Cindy was very happy, and she decided to have a try.

Day after day, Brenda would pray for Cindy, yet Sunday would come and go and

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
I forgot the name of the old lady, who was a customer (顾客) on my newspaper route when I was twelve. Yet she taught me a {{1}} that I shall never forget.
On a winter afternoon, a friend and I were throwing stones onto the roof of the old lady’s house near her garden. I found a perfectly smooth (光滑的) rock and threw it. The stone was too {{2}} , however, so it slipped (滑) from my hand as I let it go and headed straight for a small window on the lady’s door. At the {{3}} of broken glass, we knew we were in trouble. We ran faster than any of our stones flew off her roof.
I was too {{4}} of getting caught that first night to be concerned about the old lady with the broken window in winter. However, a few days later, when I was sure that I hadn’t been discovered I started to feel guilty (内疚的). She still greeted me with a smile each day when I gave her the newspaper, but I was no longer able to act comfortably when seeing her.
I decided that I would {{5}} my paper delivery (送) money, and in three weeks I had the seven dollars that I thought would cover the cost of her window. I put the money in an envelope with a {{6}} saying that I was sorry for breaking her window and hoped that the seven dollars would cover the cost of repairing it.
The next day, I {{7}} the old lady her paper. She thanked me for the paper and gave me a bag of biscuits she had made herself. I thanked her and ate the biscuits as I continued my route.
After several biscuits, I {{8}} an envelope and pulled it out of the bag. When I opened the envelope, I was shocked. Inside were the seven dollars and a short note that said, “I’m proud of you.”

blanks.why: teach sb. a lesson“给某人一个教训”。故选B。

title: The Reward of Helping Others
text:
Tobey always likes zoos. It is great to see animals around his house such as cows, horses and all different kinds of birds. For Tobey, going to the zoo was a great and wonderful way to spend his weekend learning about animals. Today, he was trying to go to somewhere a little {{1}} .
There was an animal shelter (收容所) near his house. It wasn’t a common place to adopt (收养) dogs and cats, but a place with lions, tigers and bears.
As he arrived, he was {{2}} , because he heard lions even from the parking lot. The place was small, but clean. And the volunteers (志愿者) there were very helpful. Tobey and his family {{3}} the place at their own pace (节奏), looking at the cages and places the animals lived in.
Tobey {{4}} understood the differences between this place and a zoo. Zoos had beautiful habitats set up for each animal, but you could not get near the animals at all. At this shelter, he was almost close enough to reach out and touch the animals, even if there were two fences between him and the animals. There weren’t as many people, either, so it seemed like a more personal {{5}} . The paths were covered with trees and it made the animals feel more at home.
It was interesting to look into the eyes of a lion when you could almost reach out and touch it. It was {{6}} to watch the bears walking slowly in front of you. Then there were lions lying lazily in the midday heat and monkeys cleaning themselves. It was a very special experience.
The best part about the place was the stories. Each animal had a story posted on the side of their cage. People {{7}} them from abuse (虐待) or took them to the shelter when they were no longer wanted. These were hard luck stories with a happy ending.
When it was finally time to go, they all {{8}} the volunteers and made a donation. Shelters always needed money, food for animals, and help. It made them feel good to do something they could. It was a great place, and Tobey couldn’t wait to return.

blanks.gloss: common普遍的；different不同的；beautiful美丽的；interesting有趣的。
blanks.why: 根据“There was an animal shelter near his house.”可知不去动物园, 而是去了动物收容所, 这是个不同的地方。故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
阅读下而的短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择最佳选项。
“Mommy, I got something for you!” Cody ran through the door after school. His face wore the biggest smile ever. He waved something above his head. “It’s a pen. But not just any pen. It’s a lucky pen!” He handed me the pen {{1}} , waiting for my reaction.
I looked at the pen in my hand. There was nothing special about it. It looked just like any other ballpoint pen. I had a drawer full of them. But looks can {{2}} people. At that moment, I didn’t realize how special it was or how much I would come to treasure it.
I had made the decision to be a writer. I had dreamed about it for a long time but I was afraid of being refused by the publishers (出版社). The night before, I told my husband my fear when I thought Cody wasn’t listening. “What if nobody likes my writing and I fail?” But Cody did {{3}} what I said. Now he stood in front of me, watching me examine the pen. “You don’t have to be afraid now,” he said. “This pen will make your stories great and everyone will love you.”
Tears filled my eyes. Refusal and failure didn’t seem like such a big problem any more. Even if I {{4}} sold the first book, I had everything I could ever need. I knew that pen would bring me luck, though. And I felt {{5}} already, just by having Cody in my life, especially when I heard what he did to get it.
In the lunchroom, Cody heard an older boy talking about having a lucky pen. He decided to get it for me. The boy was a tough negotiator (强硬的谈判者) but Cody didn’t give up. In the end, he {{6}} his lunch, his favorite Matchbox car, two army men his brother gave him, a crayon, and a piece of candy — his most important things, for that pen. Just to make me feel better.
I still have that pen, though it’s long out of ink, in a cup on my desk. When a refusal letter arrives and I start feeling {{7}} , I look at it and remember just how lucky I am. For while I value that pen, it’s Cody who I really {{8}} in my life.

blanks.gloss: easily容易地；secretly秘密地；proudly骄傲地；naturally自然地。
blanks.why: 根据“His face wore the biggest smile ever. He waved something above his head.”可知, 为自己做的事情感到骄傲。故选C。

blanks.why: 根据“The night before, I told my husband my fear when I thought Cody wasn’t listening.”可知, 以为科迪没听, 其实他听到了。故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“just by having Cody in my life, especially when I heard what he did to get it”可知, 觉得生命中有科迪是幸运的。故选B。

blanks.mean: 最后, 他用他的午餐、他最喜欢的火柴盒汽车、哥哥送给他的两个士兵、一支蜡笔和一块糖果——他最重要的东西——换了那支笔。

blanks.why: 根据“When a refusal letter arrives”可知, 收到了拒绝信会感到难过。故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Right from childhood, my brothers began to play rugby (橄榄球) with me. They all {{1}} me to become rugby player some day. My mom {{2}} , and she pushed me into skating though I always had a strong hope for rugby.
Finally we reached an agreement that I became the referee (裁判) of rugby. At that time, I didn’t realize that I was beginning an activity that would influence my character. At first I only worked with my brothers. Everyone was {{3}} and we got along quite well with each other. I soon realized that I needed to work with other people, and that’s when my experience changed. As I began to work with more coaches (教练) who acted in unpleasant ways, all I wanted to do was to get through each game and then be able to leave {{4}} getting into trouble. Although as a referee I tried my best in every match, they sometimes shouted at me. That made me feel {{5}} , but I decided not to let them drive me away.
I decided to stand up for myself. I never answered rudely to the coaches, but I did not let them break my confidence anymore. There were still a few situations that made me frightened. Once I called a penalty (判罚) and the team ended up {{6}} . I knew I had made the right {{7}} , even though I was scared when I saw that team’s fans waiting for me at my room. I stood my ground and overcame (克服) my fears.
I’ve been a referee for six years, but I still can’t say it’s easy. Every game hands me something new and I {{8}} know what I will face. Now I’m always prepared to face the unexpected. These are the little lessons that I’m grateful to have learned as a woman referee.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Last Saturday afternoon, my friend Allan and I were having fun playing catch in my yard. Then, I threw the ball too hard and Allan {{1}} his catch. The ball hit my neighbor’s window. We heard the big sound. Crash! Smash! The window broke into many pieces.
We were {{2}} . We rushed into my backyard, and hid. Mr. Jones, the neighbor, came out of his house and looked around. He was trying to see who threw the ball. We hid until Mr. Jones went back into his house.
Later, I saw that Mr. Jones had repaired the broken glass. He was sitting outside. He waved at me. I felt ashamed as I waved back at him. I knew what I should do, but I was {{3}} to do it.
When I came back home, my mom told me about the broken window. “Poor Mr. Jones,” she said, “he’s such a nice guy that everyone likes him. I can’t believe anyone would break his window and not stay around to {{4}} .”
Right away, I knew what I had to do. I told Mom that I broke the window by accident. I told her that I escaped. Mom said I could easily {{5}} that mistake. She said I should go right over now and own up to my mistake. It wasn’t easy, knocking on Mr. Jones’s door and telling him what I did.
Mr. Jones looked at me after I explained what happened. He was not angry at all. I asked him how much it cost to repair the window. I told him that I would save my {{6}} and pay back every penny of it. Mr. Jones smiled. “It’s not the money that {{7}} ,” he said. “I was really hurt that someone would do that to me without stopping to apologize. Now that you have come and explained the accident, I feel {{8}} again.”

blanks.mean: 然后, 我把球扔得太用力了, 艾伦没接住。

title: When my brother and I were children
text:
When my brother and I were children, we spent a few weeks each summer in the countryside with our uncle. He was a geologist and loved to go on long walks to {{1}} stones to add to his collection at the university.
One day our uncle gave us two {{2}} and asked us to help him carry the stones. The whole day, we walked around the countryside, and every now and then, our uncle put stones in our bags. We were a bit surprised that sometimes he also {{3}} some stones out from our bags. We thought he had just found better stones.
We got back home in the late afternoon. The bags were so {{4}} that we were really tired out when we put them on the ground. Yet our uncle’s bag was half-empty.
“Why did you give us so many stones?” we asked.
“I didn’t. You did.” he said, waiting for a while before continuing. “You did not know it, but I gave you a little attitude (态度) test today. And whenever you complained (抱怨) about anyone or anything, I {{5}} a stone in your bags. And whenever you talked about something in an attitude of positive (积极的) thinking, I took out a stone. And now look at your bags.”
The bags were {{6}} full.
“Your negative (负面的) thoughts are like stones. You carry them in your {{7}} just like those stones in a bag. The more negative thoughts you have, the heavier your mind is. So look at those bags and start paying attention to what you say and how you say things”
This little {{8}} was one of the most important I ever had. And I remember my uncle with great love for teaching us one of the most important lessons of life—the power of attitude.

blanks.mean: 他是一名地质学家, 喜欢走很长的路去寻找石头来增加他在大学里的收藏。
blanks.why: 根据“to add to his collection at the university”可知, 是去找石头。故选D。

blanks.why: 根据“we were really tired out”可知作者和弟弟很累是因为袋子太重了。故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“we were really tired out when we put them on the ground”可知袋子几乎满了。故选C。

blanks.mean: 这是我上过的最重要的一课。
blanks.gloss: lesson课, 教训；word单词；thought思想；attitude态度。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Promise Is a Promise!

Lance ran into the house and took his skate shoes from the closet. He was so {{1}} that he put everything on even though Mum wasn’t home yet. A few minutes later, Mum walked through the door and asked if he was ready. Lance held his arms out and rushed out from his room.
Out of the {{2}} , they saw Haley his classmate sitting by the mailbox. He told Mum that he once told Haley he would do a science project (项目) with her today, but that was before Mum said she would take him to the skate park. So, he called and told her he would do the science project with her, just not today but tomorrow.
Mum nodded and understood that Lance promised Haley to work on it today, but then he got a better {{3}} and canceled (取消) on Haley. However, Mum didn’t think it was good to break a promise. She thought for a while and had an idea.
She walked to another room and asked Lance to wait for her here. A few moments later, she came back with her car keys. Then she told Lance that Uncle Scott just called her and said he got tickets to the Big Baseball Game for tonight.
Lance {{4}} ,“You’ re going to the ball game with him? What about the skate park?”
Mum ruffied Lance’s hair. “We’ll go tomorrow. You don’t {{5}} , right?”
“Well, kind of. You promised to take me skating today.”
Mum’s smile faded (消失). “Like you {{6}} Haley you’d work on your project today?”
Lance {{7}} understood that Uncle Scott didn’t call. Mum just wanted him to know how Haley was feeling. Lance looked out of the window, Haley was still sitting by the mailbox.
“I’ll go get her and work on the project.”
“Good for you. Haley would be {{8}} .” Mum said. “And ask her if she wants to go to the skate park after you’re finished.”
“Really? You’d take us?”
“Of course. I promise.”
Lance nodded, “And a promise is a promise.”

blanks.mean: 他很兴奋, 尽管妈妈还没回家, 他还是把所有的东西都穿上了。
blanks.gloss: nervous紧张的；excited兴奋的；tired疲劳的；cool凉爽的。
blanks.why: 根据“Lance held his arms out and rushed out from his room.”可知, 兰斯伸出双臂, 冲出房间, 因此表示他很兴奋, 故选B。

blanks.why: 根据后文的“Lance looked out of the window, Haley was still sitting by the mailbox.”可知, 此处表示向窗外看去, 故选C。

blanks.gloss: 去滑板公园怎么办？” cried大喊；explained解释；agreed同意；advised建议。

blanks.mean: “我们明天去。
blanks.gloss: 你不介意吧？” go去；understand理解；excuse原谅；mind介意。
blanks.why: 根据“We’ll go tomorrow.”可知, 他妈妈答应他明天再去滑板公园, 因此让他不要介意, 故选D。

blanks.why: 根据“You promised to take me skating today.”可知, 此处表示就像你答应了海莉一样, 故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“Mum’s smile faded (消失).‘Like you...Haley you’d work on your project today?’”可知, 妈妈答应了他的事不做了, 她说就像他答应了海莉的事不做了, 因此他突然明白了这是他妈妈在教育他, 斯科特叔叔没有打电话来, 故选C。

blanks.why: 根据“‘I’ll go get her and work on the project.’”可知, 兰斯答应了海莉去做那个项目, 现在就和她一起去做, 因此她会感到高兴的, 故选D。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
It was getting dark. Paul looked out of the window and signed (叹气). Dad said he could come home by 5:30, but it was almost 7:00. Even if Dad came back, it wouldn’t be much fun playing {{1}} in the dark. Paul walked into his room and threw his baseball into the corner. He tried to do some homework, but he couldn’t.
The phone rang at about 8:00. It was Dad: “Paul, I’m sorry, but I can’t play baseball with you tonight. I have to finish my work at the office. Maybe we can play this weekend. Oh no. How about next weekend?”
Paul couldn’t understand why Dad was so {{2}} . He threw himself on the sofa and soon fell asleep. His book was still opened to the first page.
The next day at school, Paul didn’t hand in his homework and he {{3}} a test. Mrs. Green, his teacher, asked him to stay after school. “Paul, you didn’t do your homework. You didn’t pass the test and only got a D. This isn’t like you. What’s wrong?”
Paul just sat there {{4}} . “Paul, if you don’t want to talk, I will. I know that something’s worrying with you, but you have to get it out. You need to tell someone.”
As Paul walked home, he thought of what Mrs. Green said. Maybe he didn’t do his homework because he wanted to get his dad’s attention (注意). He knew Mrs. Green was right. He decided to take her advice.
When Paul got home, he {{5}} his dad. But there was no answer. Then it went to voicemail (语音信箱). Paul began talking: “Dad, I can’t play with you next weekend. I’ve got lots of problems with my homework. Also, I really don’t want to spend another day looking out of the window and waiting. Whenever you {{6}} our plans, Dad, it hurts me. It’s not too late to rebuild our relationship, but we have to start small. Maybe you can help me with my {{7}} sometime. Dad, I love you.”
As Paul ended the call, he felt relaxed. He didn’t know whether his dad would feel different, but it didn’t matter. He himself {{8}} his mood. He expressed his feelings to the right person. He had a clear head when he was doing his homework that evening.

blanks.mean: 即使爸爸回来了, 在黑暗中打棒球也不会有太多的乐趣。
blanks.gloss: baseball棒球；cards卡片；chess国际象棋；toys玩具。
blanks.why: 根据“threw his baseball into the corner.”可知, 是与爸爸约好打棒球。故选A。

blanks.mean: Paul不能理解爸爸为什么如此忙。
blanks.gloss: famous著名的；helpful有帮助的；lazy懒惰的；busy忙碌的。
blanks.why: 根据“but I can’t play baseball with you tonight. I have to finish my work at the office.”可知, 爸爸很忙。故选D。

blanks.mean: 第二天在学校, Paul没有交家庭作业, 他未能通过考试。
blanks.gloss: made使；missed错过；failed失败, 不及格；chose选择。
blanks.why: 根据“You didn’t pass the test and only got a D.”可知, 他考试不及格。故选C。

blanks.mean: Paul只是安静地坐在那儿。
blanks.gloss: cheerfully高兴地；comfortably舒服地；hopefully有希望地；quietly安静地。
blanks.why: 根据“if you don’t want to talk,”可知, Paul没有说话, 只是静静地坐着。故选D。

blanks.mean: 当Paul回到家, 他给爸爸打电话。
blanks.why: 根据“But there was no answer. Then it went to voicemail (语音信箱).”可知, 此处指给爸爸打电话。故选C。

blanks.mean: 每当你违背我们的计划时, 爸爸, 我很伤心。
blanks.gloss: prepare准备；break违背, 打破；follow跟随；question询问。
blanks.why: 根据前文可知, 爸爸很忙, 总是违约, 因此是“违背”我们的计划。故选B。

blanks.mean: 也许你有时候能够帮助我的作业。
blanks.why: 根据“I’ve got lots of problems with my homework.”可知, 是指爸爸在作业上帮助自己。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他自己改变了他的心情。
blanks.why: 根据“As Paul ended the call, he felt relaxed”可知, 给爸爸打电话说出了内心的话后, 感觉放松了, 心情也就发生了改变。故选A。

title: A Lesson About Food and Family
text:
GE Money has recently done a study. It shows that women spend over 8 years of their life shopping. According to the study, women {{1}} about 400 hours each year shopping. Almost a quarter of that time is spent doing {{2}} for food.
Luckily, Million Looks magazine says that shopping can be a good thing, and it gives some interesting {{3}} about women and shopping. The magazine says that women who shop for more than 17 hours a week are thinner and {{4}} than those who spend less time shopping. The magazine also says that women who shop more often look much younger than those who dislike shopping. Finally, they say that most {{5}} who enjoy shopping are much {{6}} .
We cannot be sure if these things are true, but that shopping is big business is really {{7}} . There are now about 50,000 shopping malls in the United States alone, and each person spends about $75 each time they {{8}} a mall.
The shopping malls also try their best to encourage people to spend as much as possible, and stay in the mall as {{9}} as possible. There are escalators (电扶梯) in malls, so people use them to pass many different stores. You may have also noticed that places to sit in malls are {{10}} to find. This is because people can’t spend money when they are sitting down!

blanks.mean: 根据这项研究, 女性每年花大约400小时购物。
blanks.gloss: cost花费, 主语为物；take花费, 主语为it；spend花费, 主语为人；pay花费, 人+pay+for+sth。
blanks.why: 根据前文“about 400 hours each year shopping”可知, 此处表示买食物, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 幸运的是, Million Looks杂志说购物是件好事, 它提供了一些关于女性和购物的有趣事实。
blanks.why: 根据“The magazine says that women who shop for more than 17 hours a week are thinner...”可知, 此处在介绍一些事实, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 该杂志称, 每周购物时间超过17小时的女性比那些购物时间较少的女性更瘦、更健康。
blanks.gloss: taller更高的；busier更忙的；richer更富有的；healthier更健康的。
blanks.why: 根据空前“thinner and”可知, 此空应该填与“thinner”同类词, healthier“更健康的”符合语境, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 最后, 他们说, 大多数喜欢购物的女性更快乐。
blanks.gloss: men男人们；women女人们；boys男孩们；girls女孩们。
blanks.why: 本段一直在说女性购物的好处, 所以此处表示大多数喜欢购物的女性更快乐。故选B。

blanks.mean: 最后, 他们说, 大多数喜欢购物的女性更快乐。
blanks.gloss: sadder更伤心的；older更老的；happier更开心的；better更好的。
blanks.why: 本段一直在说女性购物的好处, 所以此处应填褒义词, happier“更开心的”符合语境, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们不能确定这些事情是否属实, 但购物是大生意确实是真的。
blanks.why: 根据“There are now about 50,000 shopping malls in the United States alone,”可知, 在美国就有大约50000家购物中心, 所以购物是大生意确实是真的。故选A。

blanks.mean: 仅在美国, 现在就有大约50000家购物中心, 每个人每次逛一家购物中心都要花大约75美元。
blanks.why: 根据“and each person spends about $75 each time”可知, 人们在购物中心消费, 所以是逛超市, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 商场也尽力鼓励人们尽可能多地消费, 并尽可能长时间地呆在商场里。
blanks.why: 根据“The shopping malls also try their best to encourage people to spend as much as possible”可知, 商场尽力鼓励人们尽可能多地消费, 所以他们会使人们尽可能长时间地呆在商场里。故选B。
