title: A Family Lesson
text:
通读下面短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中, 选择最佳选项。
I stood there listening to my father shout at top of his voice. The look on his face said that one of us had done something {{1}} .
“Which one of you did this?”
We all looked down at the step. There was child’s handwriting in chalk there. I was filled with a lot of fear. I hoped no one could see it. Would he guess it was me? I was so worried. When he asked me, I lied, “Not me, Dad.”
The others denied (否认) it as well. Of course, we all knew that one of us {{2}} have done it. But as the youngest and smallest of the three, I just couldn’t find the courage to tell the truth.
To {{3}} who had written on the step, Father gave us each a piece of paper and a pencil. “I want each of you to {{4}} exactly what you see on the step.”
I tried my best to write the words {{5}} . I didn’t want Dad to be able to tell it was me.
He {{6}} our pieces of paper and looked at them. “Since none of you admit (承认) to have done it, then I will punish you all.” I stood there and said nothing. The last thing I wanted was for Dad to {{7}} me!
“I did it.” My sister stepped forward and said she had done something she hadn’t. She was grounded (限制外出) for a month.
We didn’t talk about that day for many years. Not until we were all older and I knew it was {{8}} to finally tell my dad it was really me. But I always felt sorry because of it. That was the last time I let anyone take the blame (责备) for me.

blanks.mean: 他脸上的表情表明我们中有人做了错事。
blanks.gloss: hard艰难的；special特别的；wrong错误的；true真的。
blanks.why: 根据“The look on his face said that one of us had done something...”以及下文“There was child’s handwriting in chalk there. I was filled with a lot of fear. I hoped no one could see it.”可知, 他脸上的表情说明我们当中的一个人做了错事。故选C。

blanks.mean: 当然, 我们都知道一定是我们中的一个人干的。
blanks.why: 根据“we all knew that one of us...have done it.”可知, 这里表示推测, 一定是我们中的一个人做的这个事情, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 为了查明是谁在台阶上写字, 父亲给了我们每人一张纸和一支铅笔。
blanks.gloss: find out查明；talk about谈论；think about思考；pay attention to注意。
blanks.why: 根据“...who had written on the step”可知, 是为了找到是谁在台阶上写的, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 我要你们每个人把你们在台阶上看到的都写下来。
blanks.why: 根据后半部分“what you see on the step”可知, 是写下在台阶上看到的东西。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我尽了最大的努力把单词写得不同。
blanks.gloss: carefully仔细地；slowly慢慢地；differently不同地；clearly清晰地。
blanks.why: 根据下一句“I didn’t want Dad to be able to tell it was me.”可知, 不想让父亲认出来, 所以是尽量地把单词写的不一样。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他收集起我们的纸片, 看着它们。
blanks.why: 根据空格后面的词语是“our pieces of paper”可知, 是他收集了我们的纸。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我最不希望的就是爸爸惩罚我！
blanks.why: 根据上文“I will punish you all.”可知, 作者最不想要的就是爸爸惩罚他。故选C。

blanks.mean: 直到我们都长大了, 我知道安全了, 我才告诉我爸爸那其实是我做的。
blanks.gloss: lucky幸运的；silly愚蠢的；easy容易的；safe安全的。
blanks.why: 根据“Not until we were all older and I knew it was...to finally tell my dad it was really me.”可知, 直到作者长大了, 他明白告诉他爸爸那件事是他做的是安全的。故选D。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
There’s No “I” in Team I love hockey (冰球). I mean I r-e-a-l-l-y love hockey. I love the feeling when I {{1}} in and out of players on the ice. I love taking the risk to score even if I miss.
At the end of the year, the team had a dinner party and the coaches handed out {{2}} . I was pretty sure I was going to get one because I was one of the lead scorers on our team. title: A Family Lesson
text:
“Where is Trevor?” asked Dad.
Trevor was my brother. He was older and bigger than I was but acted much younger.
“I don’t know.” I answered. I was busy choosing the perfect {{1}} for Dad’s birthday. This year Dad wanted something that couldn’t be bought at a shop.
“Daddy! There is a dragon toy!” Trevor came back with a box in his hand. But when he {{2}} it, there was only candy in it! He cried loudly. I came to him and read the words “dragon candy” on the cover（封面）of the box. But in fact, my big brother had trouble {{3}} .
What Trevor said took away my worry about Dad’s gift. I came up with an idea, but when {{4}} my idea with Trevor, he shook his head. “Let’s make a deal（交易）, ” I said, “We’ll try only for ten days.” When he heard this, he agreed.
The first day was the most {{5}} . Trevor didn’t want to read anything. Then I began to ask him how he felt about not finding a dragon in the box. He slowly opened his mouth. That was a start! Each day after that, Trevor told more of his dragon story, and I wrote it down. We {{6}} reading aloud in my room so many times that he got ready for the performance（表演）at last.
On Dad’s birthday, Trevor asked Dad and me to sit on the sofa. He stood before us with confidence（自信心）. I sat closer to Dad and said, “This is a surprise from both of us!” “Wow!” Dad already sounded {{7}} .
“My Dragon Friend. Written by Trevor Johnson.” I could hear how {{8}} he read. After he finished it, Trevor began to laugh when we couldn’t stop clapping hands（拍手）. Dad took off his glasses and dried them on his shirt.
“That is the best birthday gift ever!” Dad said. I knew, in Trevor’s world, that was more than just a start.

Jayden watched the kids on the school playground. Some were running and playing games, while others were kicking a dirty old football. It was his third day at his new school, and he {{1}} someone would ask him to play. But no one did.
Jayden missed his old {{2}} “Why did we have to move?” he said to himself quietly. “I don’t have any friends here. Back home, I had Shawn and Jorge and Nora.”
When he reached his house, it was {{3}} . Then he noticed a note. It read, “Barry and I are across the street at our neighbor’s house. Come on over.”
In the neighbor’s backyard, Jayden saw his mother and a woman drinking tea and chatting. His three-year-old brother Barry was playing with a little girl in a sandbox.
“Hi!” his mother called. “How was school today?”
“Okay,” Jayden said, {{4}} it wasn’t.
“This is our neighbor, Mrs. Ori, and her little girl Ava.”
Just then Ava {{5}} out for the toy car at Barry’s feet.
“Uh-oh,” Jayden thought.
The car was Barry’s favourite toy, and if anybody else touched it, he would cry and kick. But that didn’t {{6}} . Instead, Barry watched Ava push the car through the sand. Then he picked up a toy truck and did the same.
That night, Jayden did some thinking. “Maybe I was wrong. I have been {{7}} people to make friends with me. Maybe I should try to make friends with them.” he said to himself.
The next day, Jayden took a football to school. He went to Tyler, one of the players, on the playground.
“Hi,” Jayden smiled. “I got this new ball for my birthday. Do you want to try it instead of that old one?”
“Sure!” Tyler answered. “Do you want to be on my side? What position do you play?”
Out loud, Jayden said, “I would love to.” To himself, he said, “Whoever thought I could {{8}} something from my three-year-old brother!”

Finally, Mr. Larson said to the class, “Okay, Ryan, let’s hear what you have to say. Come up and give us your speech.” Ryan took a few deep breaths (呼吸). He still couldn’t help feeling a little worried. Then, he {{3}} his notes, straightened up and walked slowly to the front of the room. Mr. Larson sat down in one of the front-row seats and gave Ryan a {{4}} as he nodded for him to begin. Ryan cleared his throat, took a quick look at his {{5}} , and then started his speech.
For a moment or two, Ryan still felt very nervous. But as he went through his speech, he felt less and less like running away. He had practiced often enough so that nothing in his speech was new to him anymore. It wasn’t long before he {{6}} and was able to almost enjoy what he was doing. By the time Ryan finished his speech, he felt almost comfortable.
When Ryan stopped speaking, everyone in the class stood up and {{7}} . Mr. Larson said, “That was a very well-prepared speech, Ryan. title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
I looked at the words on the page. I knew how to say them, but my {{1}} wouldn’t work. It was my first class in this new school, so nobody here knew me. My teacher just asked me to read some texts out loud. The whole class was waiting for me silently. I could even hear my heartbeats.
I just sat there. Seconds passed. Some students started to {{2}} . “What’s wrong with her?” one boy said. “Maybe she can’t read at all!” said another student.
“Just open your mouth and speak!” I told myself. I tried to get the words out. But the first was always the most difficult. The teacher was waiting. More of my classmates were making fun of me. I wanted to {{3}} under my desk. I soon felt tears (眼泪) running down.
I often faced situations (情况) like this during my grade school. Why? I had a stuttering (结巴) problem. Because of this, I often felt embarrassed (尴尬的) at school.
 {{4}} , I met a great teacher, Mrs. Brown. She never rushed me when I was trying to talk. She helped me to relax when I was speaking, and would always wait patiently for me to finish my sentences.
Mrs. Brown offered me the most encouragement (鼓励). She always let me know that my stuttering problem didn’t mean I wasn’t smart. She said, “Your brain (大脑) is moving too fast, and your mouth just can’t {{5}} up!” Those simple words made me feel {{6}} and encouraged.
Great changes happened to me. When I entered high school, I almost {{7}} stuttering. In college, I had no trouble at all. As a child, I never imagined (想象) that I would become a {{8}} just like Mrs. Brown, passing love and care to my students.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
It was a sunny day in the summer of 2018 when I decided to take a trip alone to a nearby national park. As I was hiking trails, I came across a group of tourists. They were lost and hurriedly trying to find their way back to the {{1}} center.
I offering to {{2}} and led them back to the visitor center. They thanked me and invited me to join them for a picnic lunch. As we were eating, I learned that they were from {{3}} countries: England, America, Australia, France, Japan…and had come here for a study abroad program.
Jane, one of the tourists, told me she was an American. Her Chinese penfriend, Da Ming {{4}} her to his family. She was very happy with this invitation. When she went to his family, Da Ming’s mother prepared delicious food to entertain her. She gave Jane so much food that she couldn’t take another bite. And they also drove Jane around the city. Jane left Da Ming’s family {{5}} and she told me that she began to love food, people here and our country.
We spent the afternoon {{6}} stories and experiences, and I was surprised at the difference of their backgrounds and the similarities of their desires. It made me realize how important it is to step out and {{7}} different cultures.
As the day came to an end, I said goodbye to my new friends and headed back home. But the memory of that day stayed with me, reminding me of the value of kindness and the power of human connection. The experience {{8}} me to always be open to new experiences and to never underestimate (低估) the influence we can have on others, even in small ways.

text:
Love, joy and the warm feeling of getting together don’t cost a thing. But gifts do cost money. So what should a poor family do?
Before New Year, I told my mother that the only thing I {{1}} was a pogo stick. However, my mother said they were so expensive that we didn’t have enough money to {{2}} one.
On a Saturday before New Year, my family went shopping together.
While my mother and I were {{3}} the gifts, my dad said, “I’ll be back soon—I need to see something in the tool area.” A little later, he came back with a long box. I remember wondering if there was a pogo stick in it.
When we arrived home, my dad put the box in the garage (车库). While my parents were busy with their chores, I {{4}} walked out to the garage and found the box. I was so excited and I know as soon as I opened that magical box my bright, shiny pogo stick would appear. No such {{5}} ! Inside the box was a silly old broom (扫帚).
That New Year morning, I got some nice gifts but I didn’t get the present that I really wanted.
After cleaning up the room, my dad went to the garage. When he came back in, he was carrying a beautiful pogo stick. I couldn’t {{6}} it! My parents probably got quite a laugh from the trick (戏法) they played on me.
Although we didn’t have much {{7}} , my parents gave me the most important gift of all: lots of love. That was over 60 years age and I still think about those {{8}} memories. I will never forget all the joy my parents brought into my life.

George grew up in an environment where winning was the most valuable thing, and he expected to succeed, too. George was good at running and he called everyone from the nearby {{1}} for a race. A large group of people came to see this exciting event. When the race started, George ran among the boys from around the villages. Finally, he won the race. The crowd (人群) went wild with joy and cheer. George {{2}} this moment. It made him proud and satisfied.
But among the crowd was an old man who did not seem as {{3}} as other people. He shouted from the crowd, “There is one more race left, the most important one.” George was {{4}} , but he was confident he could win any race.
The old man brought two new competitors for the boy, a blind man and a weak old lady. “I can easily win them,” said George {{5}} . When he crossed the finish line, the blind man was still at the start, and the old lady had just started to move. He raised his hands in great excitement after his winning, but he {{6}} that the crowd wasn’t cheering, instead, they were very quiet. He was unclear about it. At the same time, the old man said, “Let’s start the race again, but all three of you should finish together this time.”
George raced again, he guided the blind man and supported the old lady. Finally, all three crossed the finish line together. The crowd cheered more loudly. The boy was full of {{7}} .
“Who was the crowd cheering for?” he asked the old man. “Boy, you have won much more than the first prize in this race, and the crowd is not cheering for any winners,” the old man replied.
What are you running for in your life? Do you strongly {{8}} success? Actually, life is not all about winning for ourselves. It is about growing together and helping others who are less lucky than us.

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
Years ago, we were asked to create a newspaper in groups about world culture in our history class.
We first wrote the names of three friends we {{1}} in our group. Unluckily, Mrs. Bartlett, our teacher, didn’t put me in the group with any of my friends. Instead, I was with Mauro, who never spoke English, Juliette, who always wore thick glasses and Rachel, who wore strange clothes. I had never {{2}} to them. Oh, how badly I wanted to be with my friends!
I was so sad that I walked up to Mrs. Bartlett. “I know what you want, Karina,” she gently patted me on my shoulder, “but your group needs a {{3}} . I need you to help them get a passing grade on this project. Only you can make it.”
I was pretty surprised.
“Will you {{4}} them?” she asked.
“Yes,” I answered. I couldn’t believe it came out of my mouth, but it did.
I bravely walked to my group and started our project. We had different tasks according to our interests. Little by little, I felt myself enjoying their {{5}} . I found out Mauro was fighting with English. Behind Juliette’s thick glasses were her shining eyes. Rachel was good at painting and always had new ideas. She did things so {{6}} that she wanted to be a fashion designer (时装设计师). I realized that they were not strange; they were just people that no one {{7}} enough for—except Mrs.Bartlett. Her thoughtfulness brought out the best in the four of us.
I learned something that week. I was given a chance to see other people in a new light. I learned that inner (内在的) beauty was more {{8}} than appearance.
Mrs. Bartlett gave us an A on that project, but we thought we should have handed it right back, for she was the one who should truly have it.

text:
A Family Lesson
Marquez had just finished trying out for Oakwood High’s basketball team Making the team was a sure thing since he was gifted and worked hard enough.
Basketball was a way of life in Marquez’s {{1}} . His older brother Reggie was playing at a top college, which made his family very proud. Marquez was expected to be like Reggie. But he had a secret.
Marquez had started training in another sport—cheerleading. Although it was much {{2}} for him, he was improving with practice.
On the bus home, he pulled out a sheet with big letters CHEER TEAM AUDITIONS (面试) on it. Now, he knew he’d have to deal with his parents’ {{3}} .
“Mom, Dad—I don’t want to play ball anymore,” he told them as soon as he got home, “I want to do something else.”
The family were {{4}} .
“Like what, son?” his father broke the silence.
“Cheerleading,” Marquez replied.
“Instead of playing ball, cheer for ball players?” his father questioned.
“Yes!” Marquez said in a voice that came out louder than expected. “I only started playing basketball because that’s what you wanted me to do. I did it, and I got really good, but now, it bores me. Cheerleading {{5}} me.”
He turned to his brother, “Sorry, bro. I know you wanted me to follow in your footsteps but...”
“Actually, I want you to do what you like.” Reggie hugged (拥抱) Marquez.
“I don’t {{6}} being the only basketball star of the family. We don’t need two! Am I right, Dad?”
Reggie smiled to their father.
This time, everyone laughed. Then Marquez offered an idea {{7}} : he would audition for the cheer team and make a choice according to the results of both tryouts. His father agreed.
A week later, both results were posted.
“I {{8}} both, Dad,” Marquez said.
“A clear choice, right?” his father replied.
Marquez smiled and gave his answer.

title: My Work Experience in a Nursing Home
text:
My Work Experience in a Nursing Home

A few weeks ago, I had my first work experience in a nursing home. I worked alongside the manager and helped her carry out different games and {{1}} with the residents (居民, 住户).
When I arrived, my first work was to {{2}} their names and faces by going in and talking to some of the residents. Although most of them did not communicate easily, it was obvious (明显的) which patients were beginning to show signs of dementia (痴呆).
First on the list of activities was indoor boules (滚球). It was surprising how such a simple activity could show so clearly how the different afflictions (折磨, 痛苦) that were so common in old age could affect a person’s ability to {{3}} simple tasks, such as roll a ball as close as possible to another ball in the middle of the room. What {{4}} me most was that the overall winner was a long term stroke victim (中风患者), who was paralyzed (瘫痪的) down the left hand side of her body.
I sat down with the winner and she told me about her grandchildren and the games they played with her when they came to visit. She also praised the home for the {{5}} she was receiving. I noticed, as she was talking although she was paralyzed down one side, her {{6}} was good, and the words she said indicated (表明, 显示) that she was recovering from a stroke, but her cognitive (认知的) ability was good.
After finishing my work, I headed home. I was still thinking everything I had just experienced and how I might be asked to {{7}} next week. I realize that the most helpful thing I can do for the benefit of the residents is just to {{8}} to them. Yes, I’m sure that staying there for a long time, they must become lonely.

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship
The library at Jefferson Middle School was a quiet and peaceful place, perfect for studying and reading. But there were rumors (谣言) that a ghost was in the {{1}} , scaring students and making strange noises at night. One day, a group of friends decided to explore the mystery of the library ghost.
They started by looking around the library, searching for any clues that might help them {{2}} the mystery. They found nothing at first, until they saw a small door hidden behind one of the bookshelves. They decided to open the door and see where it led.
To their surprise, the door opened up into a small closet (壁橱). Inside, they found an old book with {{3}} writing on its cover and they were interested. As they opened the book, they heard a strange noise coming from the shadows (阴影). Suddenly, a ghost appeared, walking in a sheet and {{4}} the friends.
But as the ghost took off the sheet, they realized that it was just the school librarian, Mrs. Johnson, playing a prank (恶作剧) on them. She explained that she had been dressing up as a ghost to keep the students interested in mysteries, but promised to {{5}} the pranks from then on.
As the friends walked back to their table, they realized that the mystery of the library ghost had been {{6}} solved. But they also knew that they had made a new friend in the library and shared their {{7}} of mysteries and reading.
From then on, they spent their afternoons at the library, reading books and sharing stories with Mrs. Johnson. And while they might not have solved any more mysteries that year, they knew that they had found something even more important —a {{8}} of community and a love of learning.
So, the next time you’re in the library and think you hear a ghostly noise, remember this story and know that it might just be a librarian playing a harmless prank.

blanks.mean: 但有传言称, 图书馆里有一个鬼魂, 晚上会吓到学生并发出奇怪的声音。
blanks.why: 根据“One day, a group of friends decided to explore the mystery of the library ghost.”可知是图书馆里有鬼魂。故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“help them...the mystery”可知是帮助他们解决谜团。故选C。 15题详解】 句意：在里面, 他们发现了一本旧书, 封面上写着令人费解的文字, 他们很感兴趣。 careless粗心的；puzzling困惑的；formal正式的；clean干净的。根据“writing on its cover and they were interested”可知他们对那些令人困惑的文字感兴趣。故选B。

blanks.mean: 突然, 一个鬼魂出现了, 在床单里走着, 吓坏了朋友们。
blanks.why: 根据“Suddenly, a ghost appeared, walking in a sheet and”可知鬼魂吓坏了学生。故选C。

blanks.mean: 她解释说, 为了让学生们对神秘感兴趣, 她一直打扮成鬼魂, 但她承诺从那时起停止恶作剧。
blanks.why: 根据“the pranks from then on.”可知转折词后表示她承诺会停止恶作剧。故选B。

blanks.mean: 当朋友们走回餐桌时, 他们意识到图书馆幽灵之谜已经成功解开。
blanks.why: 根据“ they realized that the mystery of the library ghost had been...solved”可知他们知道鬼魂是图书管理员, 所以这个谜团是成功解决了。故选D。

blanks.mean: 但他们也知道, 他们在图书馆交了一个新朋友, 并分享了他们对神秘和阅读的热爱。
blanks.why: 根据“of mysteries and reading.”可知是对神秘和阅读的热爱。故选A。

blanks.mean: 但他们知道他们发现了更重要的东西——社区意识和对学习的热爱。
blanks.why: 根据“of community and a love of learning.”可知是有社区意识。故选C。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
I used to be the shyest person in the world. I hid behind my elder sister whenever I had to speak to a stranger. When asked to speak in class, I could hardly {{1}} , much less speak. Even among the few friends I had, my low, timid (怯怯的) voice earned me jokes—about being a girl.
Then in the seventh grade, my sister suggested I {{2}} voice lessons. After considering it for a short time, I did. I began a series of vocal exercises.
After exercising a lot, I felt {{3}} in my voice.
A few months later I was asked to sing for some retired people, I thought I would do better than before because of the voice lessons. I opened my mouth and—nothing. I couldn’t remember the {{4}} ! My face turned hot. The kind pianist whispered a prompt (提示), and I remembered just enough to keep singing.
Then the thought hit me: I’ve already embarrassed (尴尬) myself enough. There’s really nothing else to {{5}} . So in my second song, I just relaxed and felt the {{6}} of the song lift (振奋) me. And I did much better.
After that, I started singing to myself as {{7}} as I could in my own room. That’s something I would never have done before. One classmate even said that I should be in the school’s talent show.
I am not a shy person any more. Singing has made me more outgoing (外向的). Today, I can also stand in front of the whole class and give a big {{8}} . I am proud of myself.

blanks.gloss: lucky幸运的；upset沮丧的；worried担忧的；confident自信的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“I thought I would do better than before because of the voice lessons”可知, 上过声乐课后, 作者认为自己能够表现得比从前好, 由此推知, 此处表示作者对自己的声音感到自信。故选D。

blanks.mean: 所以在我的第二首歌中, 我只是放松了下来, 感觉到这首歌的精神鼓舞了我。
blanks.why: 结合选项和“felt the...of the song lift (振奋) me”可知, 此处表示作者感受到了这首歌的精神。故选C。

blanks.mean: 从那以后, 我开始在自己的房间里尽可能大声地唱歌。
blanks.gloss: softly柔和地；loudly大声地；safely安全地；excitedly激动地。
blanks.why: 根据下文“That’s something I would never have done before.”可推知, 此处表示作者开始在自己的房间里尽可能大声地唱歌, 因为作者以前很害羞, 所以这是作者从来没做过的事。故选B。

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:
New York, Tokyo, Paris and {{1}} cities are {{2}} places to live in. There are {{3}} interesting things to see and to do. You can go to {{4}} kinds of museums, cinemas and parks. You can also go {{5}} , to buy things from all over the world.
But there are {{6}} problems in big cities, too. The cost of living is high. Every year many new visitors get to the cities to find {{7}} , to study at good schools and receive good medical care. Also too many people in a small space make it hard to keep the cities safe and {{8}} .

title: Working Toward a Dream
text:
Everyone has dreams. Lily dreamed of being a dancer. She took {{1}} lessons and all her teachers thought she was an excellent student.
One day she saw a notice. It said that a famous dancing group would be performing in her town. {{2}} thought, “I must show the leader my dancing skills.” She waited for the group leader in the dressing room. {{3}} the leader appeared, she came up and handed him the flowers she prepared. The thorns （刺） hurt her fingers and blood came out. But she was too {{4}} to care about her pain. She expressed her strong wish to be a dancer and begged （乞求） to show her dance.
“All right. You dance,” the leader agreed. But half way through the dance, he stopped her, “I’m sorry, in my mind you’re not good enough!” On hearing this, Lily {{5}} out as fast as her legs could carry her. It was so hard for her to accept this. She lost heart and {{6}} her dream.
Several years later, the dancing group came to her town again. She decided to find out {{7}} the leader had told her she was not good enough. This was his reply, “I tell this to every student.” “You’ve ruined（毁掉） my life!” She shouted angrily.
The leader went on, “I remember your present of flowers and how the thorns had hurt your fingers but you carried on bravely. It was a pity that you didn’t take dancing like that and stopped trying so {{8}} . So you are still not good enough for dancing!”

blanks.why: 根据“Lily dreamed of being a dancer.”可推出她上舞蹈课。故选C。

blanks.mean: 她太激动以至于不感到疼了。

blanks.mean: 听到这句话, 莉莉以最快的速度跑了出去。

blanks.mean: 很遗憾你对待跳舞并没有像那样, 并且轻易地就放弃了 happily开心地；easily容易地；luckily幸运地；safely安全地。

title: An Important Lesson at School
text:

The game began.
One of our boys {{4}} the ball and he shot a long pass to our forward (前锋). From out of nowhere a boy in a dirty T-shirt {{5}} the pass and with a beautiful form he shot and got two points.
They {{6}} us.
Then they got another pair of points in a minute.
Soon it was all over. The country team {{7}} us.
We certainly learned that even though a team is good, there is usually another just a little better. But the important lesson learned was: One can’t tell a man, or a team, by the {{8}} .

blanks.mean: 我们的一个男孩得到了球, 他长传给了我们的前锋。

title: Working Toward a Dream
text:
David was really afraid of flying on airplanes, as he was worried that there would be air-crashes（坠机）. In fact, he couldn’t stop thinking about all the bad news he had heard of. Every time David thought about flying, his heart started beating fast.
But as time went on, David’s {{1}} began to stop him from doing things he really cared about. He missed his son’s graduation and important meetings, and his fear stopped him from realizing his dream—taking his family on the {{2}} to the beach 3,000 miles away.
As his worry grew, David decided to turn to a therapist（治疗师）for help. The therapist asked David to do a careful study on flying first. After he learnt more about it, David had to admit（承认）that flying is in fact {{3}} and air-crashes hardly ever happen. That made him feel much better. Then the doctor told David a good way to relax himself when taking a plane. He said, “As the plane takes off, take it easy. Keep your breath {{4}} and calm. Whenever ideas about crashing go into your mind, please replace（取代）them with a much better one, like how much {{5}} you will have with your family when you land.”
David decided to have a try. Weeks later he booked tickets and took his family on their dream vacation. When the flying started, he closed his eyes and {{6}} the warm sand and waves at his feet, his children laughing and playing with sand nearby. Little by little, David began to relax, and he even {{7}} looking out of the window—it was the first time in his life that he saw such fantastic views! Anytime he felt himself getting nervous, he turned his attention back to his breath until the feeling passed.
When the plane landed, he felt quite {{8}} as he finally could face his biggest fear. “I gained power from somewhere inside me. I can face the problem with a positive（积极的）mind. I feel free!”

blanks.mean: 但随着时间的推移, 大卫的恐惧开始阻止他去做他真正关心的事情。
blanks.why: 根据“and his fear stopped him from realizing his dream”可知, 恐惧阻止了大卫做很多想要做的事情。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他错过了儿子的毕业典礼和重要会议, 恐惧使他无法实现带家人去3000英里外海滩度假的梦想。
blanks.why: 根据“taking his family on the…to the beach 3,000 miles away”可知, 此处指假期去海滩度假。故选D。

blanks.mean: 在了解了更多情况后, 大卫不得不承认, 飞行实际上是安全的, 很少发生空难。
blanks.gloss: boring无聊的；cheap便宜的；safe安全的；hard困难的。

title: 通读下面短文, 掌握其大意
text:
通读下面短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的 A, B, C, D 四个选项中, 选择能填入相应空白处的最佳选项。
A
A Second Chance

I was in fifth grade and about to take a science test. Since first grade, I had always been good at school. Simple science was easy for me and I always did well on tests. When it came to fifth-grade science, however, I was struggling (挣扎). I couldn’t seem to {{1}} it no matter how hard I tried. I was anxious.
My mom and dad had always been so proud of my grade, and I didn’t want to let them down. So just before the test I had written several {{2}} from the textbook on my desk in pencil. The writing was so light that it could hardly be seen. I sat {{3}} as the teacher started to hand out to the test. I didn’t want to get caught, but I didn’t want to fail, either.
As the teacher was starting down my row, suddenly the fire alarm went off. It was an unscheduled fire drill (消防演习).We all {{4}} out of the door and stood together, waiting to be allowed back into the building.
As I stood outside in the warm sunshine, I realized what a fool I had been. I knew my mom and dad would still love me no matter what my grade was. As soon as we came into the classroom, I walked to my desk and {{5}} the notes away. I had been given a second chance, and I wasn’t going to waste it. I took the test, did my best and felt {{6}} . I don’t remember what my grade was, but what happened that day has {{7}} in my heart and mind ever since.
Life is full of second chances, but you have to be willing to take them. You have to be willing to accept your {{8}} and grow from them. Every day when you wake up, you are given a second chance at life. Treasure it! And use it wisely!

blanks.mean: 不管我怎么努力都无法理解它。
blanks.why: 根据上句“When it came to fifth-grade science, however, I was struggling (挣扎).”可知, 应是无论怎么努力, 都不能理解五年级的科学课。故选B。

blanks.mean: 所以就在考试前, 我用铅笔从我桌上的课本上抄了几个笔记。
blanks.why: 根据下文“As soon as we came into the classroom, I walked to my desk and…the notes away.”可知, 应是抄了几篇笔记。故选C。

blanks.mean: 当老师开始分发试卷时, 我紧张地坐着。

blanks.why: 根据前句“The writing was so light that it could hardly be seen.”和后句“I didn’t want to get caught, but I didn’t want to fail, either.”可猜测出, 应是紧张地坐着。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我们都冲出房门, 站在一起, 等着被允许回到楼里。
blanks.why: 根据下句“It was an unscheduled fire drill (消防演习).”可知, 火警一响, 大家都冲了出去, 然后站在外面等待。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我参加了考试, 尽了我最大的努力, 感觉很平静。

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
I will never forget the Sunday afternoons I spent at my grandfather’s farm in western Pennsylvania when I was a little boy. Miles of winding stone walls around the house provided endless hours of {{1}} for a city kid like me.
I can still remember one afternoon when I was eight years old. Since my first visit to the {{2}} , I’ d wanted to be allowed to climb the stone walls around the farm. My parents would never approve (赞同) . Still, my wish to climb across those walls grew so {{3}} . One spring afternoon, I picked up all my courage and {{4}} the living room, where the adults were sitting and talking over tea after dinner. “ Can I climb the stone walls? ” I asked. Immediately the women in the room cried. “Heavens, no! You’ ll {{5}} yourself! ” I wasn’ t too disappointed; their reply was just as I’ d expected. But before I could leave the room, my {{6}} stopped me. “ Wait a minute. ” I heard him say, “ Let the boy climb the stone walls. He has to {{7}} to do things for himself. ”“ Hurry up, ” he said to me, “ and come and see me when you get back”. For the next two and a half hours I climbed those old walls and had the {{8}} of my life. Later I met with my grandfather to tell him about my adventure (冒险) . I’ ll never forget what he said. “ Fred, ” he said, smiling, “ you made day a {{9}} day just by being yourself. Always {{10}} , there’ s only one person in this whole world like you, and I like you exactly as you are. ”

blanks.why: 根据句意及后文“Still, my wish to climb across those walls grew so... ”和“ I’ ll never forget what he said. ‘Fred, ’ he said, smiling, ‘you made day a ...day just by being yourself. Always...there’ s only one person in this whole world like you, and I like you exactly as you are.’ ”可知作者渴望爬墙并且这次经历爷爷让作者明白了一个道理,

blanks.why: 根据“Since my first visit to the ... , I’ d wanted to be allowed to climb the stone walls around the farm. My parents would never approve (赞同) . Still, my wish to climb across those walls grew so... ”可知作者自从第一次来农场就希望爬石头墙, 进而猜测这种愿望依然强烈。故选D。 19题详解】 句意：一个春天的下午我鼓起所有的勇气进入了客厅, 大人们都正坐在那儿边谈话喝饭后茶。 visited参观；enter

blanks.mean: 天哪, 不, 你会伤着你自己。
blanks.why: 根据“Immediately the women in the room cried. ‘Heavens, no! You’ ll ... yourself! ’ ”可知女人们不同意作者去爬墙并且哭了, 进而猜测这样会受伤的。故选B。

blanks.mean: 但在我离开房间之前我的爷爷拦住了我。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
A lot of people have one problem with books—they buy them and then never start reading them.
To {{1}} this problem, a foreign publisher(出版商) called Eterna Cadencia came up with a very clever idea: it printed(印刷) the words of the books in disappearing ink(墨水)—the text of the book vanishes(消失) two months after the special package(包装) of the book is opened, so that encouraging buyers to start reading it {{2}} it goes away. They call this “the book that can’t wait.” The book was really a {{3}} . The publisher just sold out the whole first edition(版) at a/an {{4}} the day it was printed, and received “thousands of requests” for more copies of the book. It also got a lot of news reports. As a result, the publisher is planning to publish {{5}} kinds of books in disappearing ink.
In some ways, the idea is pretty clever. {{6}} , we still have some suggestions. First, the book should start the vanishing process(过程) after the reader first opens the book. If the vanishing ink books become {{7}} in the future, readers will need to read them one at a time. They don’t want their books to vanish before they read the first page. Second, we have to find a better use of the vanished books later. It’s a good idea if they can be {{8}} . Or maybe we can use them as notebooks. Only in that way, can it be more environmentally friendly to have such interesting books.

blanks.mean: 为了解决这个问题, 一家名为Eterna Cadencia的外国出版商想出了一个非常聪明的主意…… solve解决；answer回答；find发现；take拿。
blanks.why: 根据“this problem”可知, 是解决问题, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 在书的特殊包装被打开两个月后, 书中的文字就会消失, 这样可以鼓励买家在书消失之前开始阅读。
blanks.gloss: before在……之前；after在……之后；when当……时；until直到。
blanks.why: 根据“so that encouraging buyers to start reading it...it goes away”可知, 是在文字消失之前阅读, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 这本书真的很成功。
blanks.gloss: terrible dream糟糕的梦；big problem大问题；great success巨大的成功；large amusement大型娱乐。
blanks.why: 根据“The publisher just sold out the whole first edition(版) at a/an...the day it was printed”可知, 这本书很成功, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 出版商在一家书店的第一版刚印完, 就收到了“成千上万的要求”, 想要更多的书。
blanks.why: 根据“The publisher just sold out the whole first edition(版) at a/an...the day it was printed”可知, 书在书店售卖, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 因此, 出版社计划用消失的墨水出版不同种类的书。
blanks.gloss: successful成功的；strange奇怪的；expensive昂贵的；different不同的。
blanks.why: 根据“As a result, the publisher is planning to publish...kinds of books in disappearing ink.”可知, 出版不同种类的书, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 但是, 我们仍然有一些建议。
blanks.why: 前后构成转折关系, 用However连接, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 如果消失的墨水书在未来变得流行, 读者将需要一次阅读一本书。
blanks.gloss: dirty脏的；popular流行的；boring无聊的；famous著名的。
blanks.why: 根据“If the vanishing ink books become...in the future, readers will need to read them one at a time.”可知, 如果变得流行, 那么将需要一次阅读一本书。故选B。

blanks.why: 根据“Only in that way, can it be more environmentally friendly to have such interesting books.”可知, 更环保, 所以是回收利用。故选C。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Growing up in a military (部队) family, I moved a lot. I mostly went to school with other kids whose parents were also in the military. But when my dad retired(退伍), I moved to a common school with twelve-year-olds who shared no {{1}} life experience with me.
I was a stranger in a strange land. I wore different clothes, had different thoughts, and spoke with an accent(口音). For the first few weeks of school, I had no friends, no activities, and no promise of a bright future. To deal with it all, I began {{2}} in my diary every day—stories of adventure, of old friends, of feelings that I could not speak. I wrote as if the very next breath I took could not happen unless I wrote down words.
One day, my teacher, Mrs. Bush, came to me and asked why I always sat there writing instead of playing with others. I told her I enjoyed writing more than playing. She just smiled and left.
About 2 weeks later, she gave us a writing task. I was {{3}} that I could now take part in something that I was good at.
That night I worked and worked on my story for a long time. It was my one chance to feel important and let the class {{4}} me.
A few days after we handed in our works, Mrs. Bush called me up to the front of the classroom one day. I stood before thirty pairs of eyes looking at me, and I got worried. Was I in trouble? Did I do something wrong? Then Mrs. Bush told the class that everyone had done a great job. “But”, she said, “one student {{5}} out as an excellent writer, one with imagination and creativity.” That student was ME!
The class clapped politely and Mrs. Bush handed me my paper, with the following {{6}} on it: “Malinda, you are an excellent writer. You fill your paper with the breathings of your heart. Please keep on writing and share your {{7}} of writing with the world. I am proud of you and glad you are in my class.”
Mrs. Bush helped me feel a sense of {{8}} , and a way to survive a transition (转变) in life. She helped me gain confidence in myself that stayed with me beyond sixth grade.

blanks.gloss: different不同；similar相似的；real真的；recent最近的。
blanks.why: 根据“I mostly went to school with other kids whose parents were also in the military. But when my dad retired(退伍), I moved to a common school with twelve-year-olds who shared no…life experience with me.”可知, 之前作者父亲没有退伍的时候, 作者总是和其他父母在部队的孩子一起上学, 现在换到了一所普通学校, 里面的学生和作者的生活经历不相似。故选B。

blanks.mean: 为了应对这一切, 我开始每天在日记中写一些冒险故事, 老朋友的故事, 我无法表达的情感。
blanks.why: 根据“I wrote as if the very next breath I took could not happen unless I wrote down words.”可知, 此处指我开始每天在日记中写一些内容。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我很兴奋我现在可以参加一些我擅长的事情。
blanks.gloss: worried担忧的；surprised惊讶的；excited兴奋的；scared害怕的。
blanks.why: 根据“I could now take part in something that I was good at”可知, 可以参加一些擅长的事情应该让作者很兴奋。故选C。

blanks.mean: 这是我唯一一次感到重要并让全班接受我的机会。
blanks.why: 根据“I was a stranger in a strange land. I wore different clothes, had different thoughts, and spoke with an accent(口音). For the first few weeks of school, I had no friends, no activities, and no promise of a bright future.”和“That night I worked and worked on my story for a long time.”可知, 作者在这所学校是与其他学生不

blanks.mean: “但是”, 她说, “一个作为一名优秀的作家脱颖而出, 有想象力和创造力的学生。
blanks.why: 根据“Then Mrs. Bush told the class that everyone had done a great job.”和“one student…out as an excellent writer”可知, 此处是对学生的认同和表扬, stand out“脱颖而出”, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 全班同学礼貌地鼓掌, Bush夫人把我的试卷递给了我, 上面写着以下几句话。
blanks.why: 根据“Malinda, you are an excellent writer. You fill your paper with the breathings of your heart. Please keep on writing and share your…of writing with the world. I am proud of you and glad you are in my class.”可知, 这些都是Bush夫人给我写的话。故选B。

blanks.mean: 请继续写作, 与世界分享你的写作天赋。
blanks.why: 根据“as an excellent writer, one with imagination and creativity”可知, Bush夫人夸赞作者的写作水平, 作者拥有写作天赋。故选C。

blanks.mean: Bush夫人帮助我感受到了归属感, 并帮助我度过了人生的过渡期。
blanks.why: 根据“I am proud of you and glad you are in my class.”和“ She helped me gain confidence in myself that stayed with me beyond sixth grade.”可知, Bush夫人的认可让作者可以被接受, 有了归属感。故选B。 阅读理解(共36分)

title: A Family Lesson
text:
When I was in primary school, I enjoyed learning about interesting things. But one thing {{1}} me. I could never get a perfect mark on my math tests like some of the girls did.
Every time I brought home my report card, before my mom read it, she could guess what the math score was — it had always been sitting just above 90. My mom even {{2}} about it. She said sweetly, “Could you bring home a perfect mark just once?”
One day I talked to my mom about this. She asked me to think about why this was so. I thought about it. After a lot of thinking, I understood what my problem was.
“Mom, some questions are really simple. I know how to solve them right away. So I work them out fast.” “Oh?” Mom listened carefully. “Yes. They are so easy that I get {{3}} . And I make mistakes like copying my answer with an extra (额外的) zero. And I don’t check.”
“I see,” Mom said. “When the questions are simple, you are not careful enough. So any mistake {{4}} you the perfect mark.”
She continued, “But I don’t think copying an extra zero is a {{5}} mistake. If you’re calculating (计算) a number of a spaceship, extra zero may cause a total failure of the launch (发射).”
“I see. I’ll try to be fast and careful, too.” Our {{6}} continued. “How about the difficult questions?” asked Mom.
“I tried to solve them, but they are hard.”
Mom laughed, “Difficult questions take a long time to solve. The first thing you have to do is to understand the question. Then you do your best to solve it. And you never give up easily, right?”
Mom’s {{7}} made it really easy. I could hardly {{8}} until the next math exam.
You know what? A few weeks later, I did finally get a perfect mark!

blanks.mean: 但有一件事困扰着我。
blanks.why: 根据“I could never get a perfect mark on my math tests like some of the girls did.”可知这是困扰作者的问题。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我妈妈甚至开与此相关的玩笑。
blanks.why: 根据“Could you bring home a perfect mark just once?”可知这是妈妈在开玩笑。故选A。

blanks.mean: 它们太容易了, 以至于我很粗心。
blanks.gloss: bored无聊的；angry生气的；nervous紧张的；careless粗心的。
blanks.why: 根据“Mom, some questions are really simple. I know how to solve them right away. So I work them out fast.”可知容易题还错了, 作者是粗心的。故选D。

blanks.mean: 所以任何错误都会让你丢掉满分。
blanks.why: 根据“So any mistake ... you the perfect mark.”可知任何错误都会使作者失去得满分的机会。故选C。

blanks.mean: 但我不认为抄额外的零是一个小错误。
blanks.gloss: small小的；special特别的；serious严重的；strange奇怪的。
blanks.why: 根据“If you’re calculating a number of a spaceship, extra zero may cause a total failure of the launch.”可知妈妈认为多写一个零不是小错误。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我们的讨论继续着。
blanks.why: 根据“One day I talked to my mom about this.”及上下文可知此处是作者和妈妈在讨论问题。故选C。

blanks.mean: 妈妈的建议让事情变得很简单。
blanks.why: 根据上文内容可知妈妈就作者考不了满分的问题给出了一些建议。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我几乎等不及要进行下次数学考试了。
blanks.why: 根据“You know what? A few weeks later, I did finally get a perfect mark!”可知作者等不及要再考试, 想试试妈妈的建议是否凑效。故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Interest is the {{1}} to success. A person who is interested in something will devote himself to it. At the same time, a big miracle(奇迹) will be made. I have invented robots which improve the work of cars. My love of making things began when I was a kid. I really became excited about inventing after I learned about Thomas Edison.
One day in fourth grade, our teacher gave us a project in class. We had to write to a company and learn about the products(产品). I thought and thought. Finally I {{2}} the Thomas A. Edison Company. Soon after, the company sent me a book about the life of Thomas Edison. How I enjoyed reading and re-reading about his inventions! I liked the recorded sound and the electric light most. The inventions were clearly {{3}} on my brain.
My dad noticed my interest in inventing and {{4}} me. He showed me how to turn my ideas into plans and then into new things. Once, I surprised my dad with a model plane I made. Later, we found a similar model plane in a store. I learned that different inventors often invent similar things. It is not {{5}} for this to happen. I also learned that not all great ideas {{6}} . Failure is a common part of the inventing. And failure can make a positive contribution(贡献) to your life once you learn to use it.
As my father and I worked together, I began to realize that my dad was quite an inventor himself. He was always looking for a better way to make his job {{7}} . His guiding hands, together with my {{8}} in inventing, led me to become an engineer and an inventor. It’s well known to all that interest plays an important role in one’s life. Of course, I also thank Thomas Edison. He is my hero.

blanks.mean: 兴趣是成功的关键。
blanks.gloss: result结果；key关键；lift电梯；lesson课程, 教训。
blanks.why: 根据“Interest is the...to success.”可知, 兴趣是成功的关键。故选B。

blanks.mean: 最后我选择了托马斯爱迪生公司。
blanks.gloss: ran跑； organized组织； chose选择； managed成功做成。
blanks.why: 根据“Finally I...the Thomas A. Edison Company.”可知, 此处表示作者选择了爱迪生公司, 用动词chose。故选C。

blanks.mean: 这些发明清楚地印在我的脑海里。
blanks.gloss: guessed猜；printed打印；put放；examined检查, 考试。
blanks.why: 根据“How I enjoyed reading and re-reading about his inventions!”可知, 作者反复阅读之后那些发明印在他的脑子里, 用动词printed。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我爸爸注意到我对发明的兴趣, 并鼓励我。
blanks.gloss: questioned询问；judged判断；allowed允许； encouraged鼓励。
blanks.why: 根据“He showed me how to turn my ideas into plans and then into new things.”可知, 父亲鼓励我, 用动词encouraged。故选D。

blanks.mean: 发生这种情况并不罕见。
blanks.gloss: unusual不寻常的； unlucky不幸的；unfair不公平的；uneasy担心的。
blanks.why: 根据“I learned that different inventors often invent similar things.”可知, 事情不是不寻常的, 用形容词unusual。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我还了解到, 并非所有伟大的想法都能奏效。
blanks.gloss: work工作, 起作用；fail失败；come来；end结束。
blanks.why: 根据“Failure is a common part of the inventing.”可知, 失败很正常, 此处用动词work表示“不是所有的想法都起作用”。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他总是在寻找一种更好的方法来简化他的工作。
blanks.gloss: important重要的； exciting令人兴奋的；simple简单的； hard难的。
blanks.why: 根据“my dad was quite an inventor himself”可知, 父亲也是一个发明者, 此处用形容词simple表示“让他的工作变得简单”。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他的指导之手, 加上我对发明的兴趣, 使我成为了一名工程师和发明家。
blanks.gloss: habit习惯； story故事； plan计划； interest兴趣。
blanks.why: 根据“It’s well known to all that interest plays an important role in one’s life.”可知, 兴趣在人的一生中扮演着重要的角色。故选D。 阅读理解(共38分)

title: 从下面各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中
text:
从下面各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择可以填入空白处的最佳选项。
When I was just a few months old, my parents realized that I might have a hearing problem because I couldn’t even hear loud noises. They {{1}} all sorts of methods (方法). Sadly, I couldn’t hear a thing.
The doctor advised my parents to put me in a {{2}} school so I could learn to communicate. But they found it a little hard to take. They wanted me to be able to {{3}} a normal life. So first my parents sent me to private speech {{4}} where I learned to read lips (唇) and pronounce words.
Next my parents decided to send me to a normal primary school. In order for that to {{5}} , they managed to make the headmaster to accept me. At school, I sat at the {{6}} of class and paid attention to the teacher, which wasn’t always easy, especially when she had her back to the class in order to write on the board. But I tried on and did a lot of work after school.
My parents’ effort paid off and I left primary school with good enough {{7}} to get into a number of Singapore’s top middle schools. Also my parents went to several schools to explain my needs. {{8}} , a school in my neighborhood accepted me.
I worked very hard and did well enough to go to one of the top junior colleges. Since then I have achieved (取得) many things inside and outside school. None of these would have been {{9}} without one of the most important lessons from my parents. If you {{10}} yourself and work hard, you can win great results.

blanks.mean: 他们尝试了各种方法。
blanks.why: 根据“my parents realized that I might have a hearing problem because I couldn’t even hear loud noises...all sorts of methods (方法)”可知, 作者听力有问题, 所以应说父母尝试了很多方法, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 医生建议我的父母把我送到一所特殊的学校, 这样我就可以学会交流。
blanks.gloss: expensive昂贵的；modern现代的；unusual不寻常的；special特殊的。
blanks.why: 结合常识及下文“But they found it a little hard to take. They wanted me to be able to ... a normal life.”可知, 医生应是建议作者去特殊的学校, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 他们希望我能过正常的生活。
blanks.gloss: lead过（某种生活）；make使变得；enjoy享受, 喜爱；take拿走。
blanks.why: 根据“ So first my parents sent me to private speech...where I learned to read lips (唇) and pronounce words.”可知, 父母希望作者能过正常的生活, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 所以, 我的父母首先送我去参加私人演讲班, 在那里我学会了读唇语和发音。
blanks.why: 根据“ private speech”和“where I learned to read lips (唇) and pronounce words.”可知, 学习唇语和发音的应是私人课堂, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 为了做到这一点, 他们设法让校长接受了我。
blanks.why: 根据“ they managed to make the headmaster to accept me”可知, 设法让校长接受作者是为了使作者能进入正常的小学, 是这件事发生, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 在学校, 我坐在教室的前面, 专心听老师讲课, 这并不总是容易的, 尤其是当她背对着教室在黑板上写字的时候。
blanks.gloss: back背面；center中心；front前面；side一边, 一侧。
blanks.why: 根据“I sat at the ...of class and paid attention to the teacher”及作者听力有问题的这一情况, 可推断, 作者应是坐在前面, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 我父母的努力得到了回报, 我小学毕业时取得了足够好的成绩, 进入了新加坡的几所顶尖中学。
blanks.why: 根据“My parents’ effort paid off ”和“get into a number of Singapore’s top middle schools. ”可知, 应是作者取得了好成绩, 才能进去顶尖中学, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 最后, 我家附近的一所学校录取了我。
blanks.gloss: Finally最后；Sadly伤心地；Hardly几乎不；Quickly快速地。
blanks.why: 根据“a school in my neighborhood accepted me.”可知, 此处是介绍最后的录取结果, 所以finally符合语境, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 如果没有我父母最重要的一课, 这一切都不可能实现。
blanks.gloss: necessary必要的； important重要的；possible可能的；easy简单的。
blanks.why: 根据“. None of these would have been ...without one of the most important lessons from my parents.”及上文可知, 此处指没有父母的努力, 作者现在获得的一切都是不可能的, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 如果你相信自己并努力工作, 你就能赢得伟大的成绩。
blanks.gloss: care for关心；believe in信任；stand for代表；depend on依靠。
blanks.why: 根据“...yourself and work hard, you can win great results”及作者的经历可知, 能取得现在的成绩都是源于相信自己和刻苦努力, 故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
I had been playing hockey (冰球) for about 10 years. I was always the one sitting at the end of the bench, and seldom got into a game. I went to all the practices and showed up even when it was so cold that your “breath froze” and when the other players had decided to stay home. I felt I had {{1}} enough and thought of quitting.
I finally decided to break the news to my mom that I was leaving the team. My mom may have looked like a tiny and quiet lady but on {{2}} my words, she said, “Remember, ‘A quitter never wins and a winner never quits (放弃).’ Your mother didn’t raise {{3}} , so think about yourself in a {{4}} way and see yourself as a winner!” So I worked harder than ever at getting in better shape, improving my shot accuracy and changing my {{5}} .
Once in a match, we {{6}} our first game badly. What’s worse, one of our best players got hurt. I was sitting at my {{7}} place, at the end of the bench, when the coach came over and told me I was going in. I was nervous, excited and terrified all at the same time.
The opposing team was fast and I had to admit I was a little scared. But my mom’s words rang out in my head like a church bell. Instead of being afraid, I was “pumped” and I very quickly found that all my extra work was paying off. I was as fast a skater as anyone else on the ice, and I seemed to get the {{8}} to score. The crowd went quiet. All the time I spent on the ice when everyone had gone home had prepared me for this moment.
Won! I won!
The lesson I learned from my mom’s {{9}} has stayed with me over the years. I hear them whenever I am faced with a challenge, or whenever I {{10}} myself.

blanks.mean: 我觉得我已经受够了, 于是想退出。
blanks.why: 根据下文“thought of quitting”可知, 作者受够了, 所以想退出。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我妈妈可能看起来像个娇小安静的女士, 但一听到我的话, 她说。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I finally decided to break the news to my mom that I was leaving the team”可知, 作者把自己的想法告诉了母亲, 听到儿子的话之后母亲开口说话了。故选C。

blanks.mean: 你母亲不会养育失败者。
blanks.gloss: talkers谈话者；dreamers梦想家；attackers袭击者；losers失败者。
blanks.why: 根据下文“see yourself as a winner!”可知, 作者母亲不愿养育失败者, 所以让作者振作起来。故选D。

blanks.mean: 所以要以积极的方式思考自己, 把自己视为赢家！
blanks.gloss: positive积极的；familiar熟悉的；brief简洁的；convenient方便的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“see yourself as a winner!”可知, 母亲要求作者以积极的心态思考问题, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 因此, 我比以往任何时候都更加努力地锻炼身体, 提高射门精度, 改变态度。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I felt I had suffered enough and thought of quitting”可知, 作者原本想放弃了, 但是在母亲开导之后又改变了态度。故选D。

blanks.mean: 曾经有一次在比赛中, 我们第一场比赛输得很惨。
blanks.why: 根据下文“What’s worse, one of our best players got hurt”可知, 是比赛中出现了不利的状况, 即输了比赛。故选A。

blanks.mean: 当教练过来告诉我, 我要上场的时候, 我正坐在我惯常的位置, 在板凳的末端。
blanks.gloss: usual寻常的；safe安全的；secret秘密的；private私人的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I was always the one sitting at the end of the bench”可知, 作者一直都坐着冷板凳, 所以这次也像往常一样坐着。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我在冰上滑得和其他人一样快, 似乎有机会得分。
blanks.why: 根据下文“to score”可知, 指的是作者似乎有机会得分了。故选B。

blanks.mean: 多年来, 我从妈妈的话中学到的道理一直伴随着我。
blanks.why: 根据下文“I hear them”可知, 此处指的是当初母亲的一番话。故选C。

blanks.mean: 每当我面临挑战或怀疑自己时, 我都会听到这个声音。
blanks.why: 根据上文“I am faced with a challenge”可知, 此处指的是遇到困境时, 即“怀疑自己”时。故选D。

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
“I was thinking of our spring house cleaning.” John’s mom suggested. “Tomorrow, John, you have no school. You can help me, OK?” “OK.” John said.
The next day, John and his mom clean the {{1}} . They cleaned until everything was tidy. Suddenly John’s mom pointed to the Grandpa’s {{2}} and shouted, “That old chair has got to go. We will buy Grandpa a new one.”
It was {{3}} . John had to agree. The chair was unsightly (不美观的). It was too old.
“John, let’s take the chair outside.” Mom said. As they were trying to {{4}} the chair, Grandpa came in. He blocked their way. “Oh, no! You can’t take my chair.”
“Grandpa, we’ll buy you a new one.” John’s mom said. “No, I don’t want a new one.” Grandpa tried to push his chair back into place. John’s mom gave up and left the room. Grandpa sat into his chair and closed his eyes. “Grandpa, why don’t you let us throw away the chair?” John asked. “It’s so old.”
“You don’t {{5}} , John. I sat in this chair with your grandma when I asked her to marry me. It was so long ago, but when I sit in this chair and close my eyes, I {{6}} she is near.”
It’s amazing(令人惊奇的), John thought, how Grandpa could {{7}} things from the past. In the present, he forgot almost everything.
“And the night your father was born, I sat in this chair. When they placed the tiny baby into my arms, I was never happier.” A smile now flashed (闪现) across his old face. “I think I’m going to understand.” John said {{8}} .
“Many years later,” Grandpa’s voice broke, “I sat in this chair when the doctor called and told me your grandma was ill. I was lost without her but the chair gave me comfort and warmth.”
“I’m {{9}} , Grandpa.” John looked at Grandpa and said, “This is not just any old chair. You’ve gone through a lot together.”
That night, John told his mom this chair was like Grandpa’s {{10}} . They realized how much the chair meant to Grandpa. When they looked at the chair the next day, they found the room would be very dull(单调的) without this old chair.

blanks.mean: 第二天, 约翰和妈妈打扫房子。
blanks.why: 根据前文“I was thinking of our spring house cleaning.”, 可知他们第二天打扫房子, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 突然, 约翰的妈妈指向爷爷的椅子喊道。
blanks.why: 根据后文“That old chair has got to go.”, 可知此处指的是椅子, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 确实如此。
blanks.gloss: difficult困难的；true正确的；impossible不可能的；sad悲伤的。
blanks.why: 根据后文“John had to agree.”, 约翰不得不赞成, 可知妈妈说得对, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 当他们努力搬动这把椅子时, 爷爷进来了。
blanks.why: 根据“Oh, no! You can’t take my chair.”, 可知此处是在搬走它, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 约翰, 你不懂。
blanks.why: 根据上一段“It’s so old.”以及下文“I sat in this chair with your grandma …she is near.”可知, 此处爷爷在反驳他, 说他不懂, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 那是很久以前的事了, 但是当我坐在椅子里, 闭上眼睛, 我感觉她就在我身边。
blanks.gloss: realize认识到；feel感觉；hope希望；notice察觉到。
blanks.why: 根据“when I sit in this chair and close my eyes, I…she is near.”, 可知此处表示感觉, feel“感觉”符合语境, 故选B。

blanks.mean: 这是惊人的, 约翰想, 爷爷是怎么记得这些过去的事的呢？
blanks.why: 根据后文“In the present, he forgot almost everything.”, 可知约翰很震惊爷爷竟然记得以前的事, remember“记得”符合语境, 故选C。

blanks.mean: “我想我会理解的”, 约翰若有所思地说。
blanks.gloss: nervously紧张地；bravely勇敢地；excitedly兴奋地；thoughtfully若有所思地。
blanks.why: 根据“I think I’m going to understand.”, 可知约翰认为他会懂的, thoughtfully“若有所思地”符合语境, 故选D。

blanks.mean: 我很抱歉, 爷爷。
blanks.gloss: sorry抱歉的；worried担心的；bored无聊的；curious好奇的。
blanks.why: 根据“This is not just an old chair. You've gone through a lot together.”, 可知约翰很抱歉之前想扔掉这把椅子, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 那晚, 约翰告诉妈妈那把椅子就像爷爷的朋友。
blanks.gloss: child孩子；dad父亲；teacher老师； friend朋友。
blanks.why: 根据前文爷爷的描述, 可知椅子一直陪伴着他, 就像是一个忠实的朋友, friend“朋友”符合语境, 故选D。 阅读理解(共32分)

title: 通读下面短文, 掌握其大意
text:
通读下面短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择能填入相应空白处的最佳选项。
The students of the seventh grade walked into the hall with laughter and voices. We were told to listen to a speech by Mrs. Marks about bullying（欺负）and peer pressure（同伴压力）. During the whole year, our grade had listened to speeches on these topics over and over again. My friends and I sat back, preparing to sit through another {{1}} speech.
But as soon as Mrs. Marks started talking, she caught my attention. She talked in the way as if she knew how to reach into our minds and make us {{2}} . And for once, I actually began to think about what she was talking about.
One boy, especially, came to my mind. Every day, this boy came to school late. The students in the class would always make fun of him. They said, “Hey, man! Where have you been?” And then another added a more unfriendly joke. Their jokes would continue until the teacher stopped them. But it was always too late. The boy would put his head down on his desk in {{3}} .
I felt really sorry for this {{4}} boy. Then I turned my attention back to the speaker and listened carefully till the end.
“Now, before I leave today, I would like to give everyone here a chance to say something on the topics of bullying or peer pressure. You may apologize（道歉）to or thank someone. And I can promise that no one will laugh at you this time.”
The silence in the room made me believe her. Slowly I saw a few hands rise. One girl wanted to apologize to a friend, and another thanked a boy for his kindness. It was then that my moment of {{5}} happened. I put up my hand. The speaker called on me, and I began to talk.
“What you said today {{6}} makes sense. I know that it’s true, because I see it every day in class. There is one person who is always made fun of.” My voice shook, “I think that everyone here has made fun of him. I know I have. And now I really {{7}} it. To us, it may just be a game, but to him, it must hurt. And I think… well, I think we need to stop.”
There was a silence for several seconds, but then, clapping quickly spread through the crowd.
Later that day, the boy thanked me. And from then on, the other students began to {{8}} him better. They stopped playing jokes on him and greeted him with a friendly “Hi”. I was pleased I had voiced something that everyone was feeling.

blanks.mean: 我和我的朋友坐回来, 准备坐着听另一个无聊的演讲。
blanks.gloss: important重要的；interesting有趣的；boring无聊的；different不同的。
blanks.why: 根据上句“During the whole year, our grade had listened to speeches on these topics over and over again”可推知作者觉得那些演讲很无聊, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 她那说话的方式好像她知道如何进入我们的思想, 让我们思考。
blanks.gloss: speak说, 讲；think思考；relax放松；imagine想象。
blanks.why: 根据“reach into our minds”可知是指思考事情。故选B。

blanks.mean: 那个男孩羞愧地把他的头放在他的桌上。
blanks.why: 根据“The students in the class would always make fun of him.”可知班上的学生总是取笑这个男孩, 所以他会很羞愧。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我真的为这个可怜的男孩感到难过。
blanks.gloss: lazy懒惰的；poor可怜的；shy害羞的；naughty顽皮的, 淘气的。
blanks.why: 根据“I felt really sorry for this”结合上文这个小男孩总是被取笑, 可知他是可怜的孩子。故选B。

blanks.mean: 就在那时, 我鼓起了勇气。
blanks.gloss: pride骄傲, 自豪；interest兴趣；courage勇气；pity遗憾。
blanks.why: 根据“I put up my hand.”可知作者鼓起勇气举起手。故选C。

blanks.mean: 你今天说的真的有意义。
blanks.gloss: really真正地；carefully认真地；hardly几乎不；hopefully充满希望地。
blanks.why: 根据“What you said today...makes sense. I know that it’s true, because I see it every day in class”可知作者认为老师今天所说的内容真地很有意义。故选A。

blanks.mean: 现在我真的很后悔。
blanks.why: 根据“To us, it may just be a game, but to him, it must hurt.”可知作者很后悔自己取笑过同学。故选A。

blanks.mean: 从那时起, 其他的学生开始对待他更好。
blanks.why: 根据“Later that day, the boy thanked me. And from then on, the other students began to...him better. ”可知从那以后, 班级里的同学对这个男孩更好了。故选D。

title: Working Toward a Dream
text:
Working Toward a Dream
A month before my first marathon, one of my ankles (脚踝) was injured and this meant not running for two weeks, leaving me only two weeks to train. Yet, I decided to go ahead.
I remember back to my 7th year in school. In my first P.E. class, the teacher asked us to run laps and then hit a softball. I didn’t do {{1}} . He later told me that I was “not athletic”.
The idea that I was “not athletic” {{2}} me for years. When I started running in my 30s, I realized running was a battle against myself, not about competition or if I was athletic. It was all about the battle against my own body and mind. A test of wills!
The night before my {{3}} , I dreamt that I couldn’t even find the finish line. I woke up sweating (出汗) and nervous, but ready to prove something to myself.
Shortly after crossing the start line, my shoe laces (鞋带) became untied. So I {{4}} to readjust (再调整). Not the start I wanted!
At mile 3, I passed a sign: “GO FOR IT, RUNNERS!”
By mile 17, I became out of breath and the once injured ankle hurt badly. Despite the pain, I stayed the course walking a bit and then {{5}} again.
By mile 21, I was starving!
As I got mile 23, I could see my wife waving a sign. She is my biggest fan. She never {{6}} the alarm clock sounding at 4 a.m. or questioned my expenses on running.
I was one of the {{7}} runners to finish. But I finished! And I got a medal. In fact, I got the same medal as the one that the guy who came in first place had.
Determined to be myself, move forward, free of shame and worldly labels (世俗标签), I can now call myself a “marathon {{8}} ”.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
My dad used to say he knew I would be a singer. When I was a baby, I was always singing loudly. Dad was a big sports fan, but he was happy to know I loved {{1}} .
After dinner, dad would often ask me to sing. He always said that I sang “I Will Always Love You” much better than Whitney Houston!
At every school concert he cheered me on. The look of {{2}} on his face made me happy.
My life was full of concerts, singing lessons and laughter. Though my mum and brothers helped me, they did not {{3}} our love for music.
Our lives changed when dad was told he had cancer (癌症). We always hoped that something would happen and he would get better, but the doctors told us that they could not {{4}} him.
About a week before my dad died, he fell into a coma (昏迷). The nurses said even though dad did not answer, he could still {{5}} me.
The nurses said I should sing him a song. I sang one of our favourites. As I sang, my dad smiled {{6}} .
I will always remember that smile. I was so pleased to know that dad had heard me sing one more song. My dad died on May 14, 2000. I don’t know how to say how much I missed him.
Now I have all the memories of him and his beautiful {{7}} deep inside my heart. I will always know that he is {{8}} from his front row seat in heaven. He used to say, “Sing from your heart.” My dad has and will always be my hero.

title: 通读下面两篇短文
text:
通读下面两篇短文, 掌握其大意, 然后从短文后各题所给的 A, B, C, D 四个选项中, 选择能填入相应空白处的最佳选项。
A
This Old Chair
“I was thinking of our spring house cleaning.” John’s mom suggested. “Tomorrow, John, you have no school. You can help me, OK?” “OK.” John said.

The next day John and his mom clean the house. They cleaned until everything was tidy. Suddenly John’s mom pointed to the Grandpa’s {{1}} and shouted, “That old chair has got to go. We will buy Grandpa a new one.”
It was {{2}} . John had to agree. The chair was unsightly(不美观的). It was too old.
“John, let’s take the chair outside.” Mom said. As they were trying to {{3}} the chair, Grandpa came in. He blocked their way. “Oh, no! You can’t take my chair.”
“Grandpa, we’ll buy you a new one.” John’s mom said. “No, I don’t want a new one.” Grandpa tried to push his chair back into place. John’s mom gave up and left the room. Grandpa sat into his chair and closed his eyes. “Grandpa, why don’t you let us throw away the chair?” John asked. “It’s so old.”
“You don’t {{4}} , John. I sat in this chair with your grandma when I asked her to marry me. It was so long ago, but when I sit in this chair and close my eyes I {{5}} she is near.”
It’s amazing(令人惊奇的), John thought, how Grandpa could {{6}} things from the past. In the present, he forgot almost everything.
“And the night your father was born, I sat in this chair. When they placed the tiny baby into my arms, I was never happier.” A smile now flashed(闪现) across his old face. “I think I’m going to understand.” John said {{7}} .
“Many years later,” Grandpa’s voice broke, “I sat in this chair when the doctor called and told me your grandma was ill. I was lost without her but the chair gave me comfort and warmth.”
“I’m sorry, Grandpa.” John looked at Grandpa and said, “This is not just any old chair. You’ve gone through a lot together.”
That night, John told his mom this chair was like Grandpa’s {{8}} . They realized how much the chair meant to Grandpa. When they looked at the chair the next day, they found the room would be very dull(单调的) without this old chair.

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
From the time I was a child in New Jersey, I loved spending weekends with my grandparents. I felt {{1}} in Granny’s small kitchen. We always had peaceful conversations, and Granny always seemed to have some wisdom (智慧) with every dish she prepared.
I remember one Saturday morning. I was about 11 years old. After breakfast I asked Granny, “What kind of {{2}} are you making today?” “Vegetable beef,” she answered, “and you can help by cutting some carrots.” As I slowly cut the carrots. I said,“I’ve got to give a {{3}} next week and I’m scared. I don’t like standing in front of everybody. What if I forget what I’m going to say? Or what if somebody laughs?” “And what if you do just fine?” Granny asked. “Have you {{4}} notes?” “Well, no. That would be a lot of work.” “Hard work never hurts anyone,” Granny said, “you could try practicing in front of a mirror (镜子). It’s easy to find how well you are practicing.”
I pushed the pieces of carrots to the side of the cutting board and then complained about schoolwork, friends and family. Granny took it all in, listening {{5}} while I talked about so many pieces of grief (伤事) in my life. “Nancy,” she said, “there’s nothing wrong with a little trouble in your life. Well, you know, a lot of people don’t make homemade soup these days. They say it’s too much trouble. But I don’t {{6}} such a little trouble. It adds flavor (滋味) to my soup—and to my life. My soup will be pretty bland (平淡的) without the vegetables, and so will my life be if it doesn’t have the little ups and downs.” She smiled and then started washing the dishes. While I helped Granny clean up, I thought about what she had said. I still had a few days to practice my report.
That Saturday, Granny gave me food for thought as well as a bowl of her homemade soup. As I {{7}} the meal with my grandparents, my problems didn’t seem so big any more. Maybe I could {{8}} a little trouble into something as special as Granny’s homemade soup. I would have to work on them. Granny had said hard work paid off.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

It was Raj’s first day of school in a new country, and he was {{1}} . His family just moved to the United States from India.
The teacher, Mr. Washington came out of his office. He reached out his hand. Raj shook it as his father showed him. “Welcome!” Mr. Washington said. His first handshake in the United States was a success.
His mother told Mr. Washington that he earned high marks in English. Mr. Washington smiled and said, “I can tell that he is the apple of your eye.” Raj {{2}} what Mr. Washington meant. He has seen no apples in his mother’s eyes. “You are wonderful like a juicy, sweet apple!” his mother said to him. Raj felt a smile {{3}} slowly across his face.
“Sandeep, come here, please,” Mr. Washington said. A boy with a big smile walked over. “Raj, this is Sandeep. He will help you during the school day.” “Namaste,” Sandeep said. Then he placed his hands together. The {{4}} felt like a little bit of home. “It is nice to meet another person from India.”
Next, Mr. Washington {{5}} Raj in the class. The students smiled and called out, “Hello, Raj!” Raj was suddenly nervous again.
The morning passed quickly. A bell sounded loudly. “It’s time for lunch!” Sandeep said. “The early bird gets the worm(蠕虫)!” Mr. Washington said. “Are there other things to eat?” Raj asked Sandeep. “I don’t think I would like worms.” “It’s an idiom—a saying,” Sandeep explained. “He means that the first to arrive get the best {{6}} of food.” This new way of speaking English puzzled Raj. Then they went to the lunchroom. As they walked to the table, a boy dropped his milk on the floor. The milk flowed(流动) like a white river. Raj began to laugh {{7}} . “What’s so funny?” the boy asked. “You poured(倒出) away rivers of milk!” Raj said. “That makes no {{8}} ,” the boy said. “This is an Indian way of saying you are very giving,” Raj explained. “It’s an idiom.” “Oh,” the boy said. “I guess that is pretty funny!” “I’m Raj,” he said, suddenly feeling better. “Mike,” the boy said. They shook hands.

After dinner, my mum said sorry to my dad for burning the bread. And I never forget what he said, “I love burnt bread, dear. It doesn’t {{4}} at all.” Later that night, I went to kiss Dad good night. I asked him if he really liked his bread burnt. He held me in arms and {{5}} “Your mum worked very hard all day. She’s really tired. And you see a bit of burnt food never hurt anyone!”
Now I know life is not perfect. Nobody is perfect, either. As for me, I often forget birthdays or some other special days. But I’ve learned something {{6}} over these years. What we really need is the understanding of each other, whether between a husband and wife, a parent and {{7}} or just between two friends. This is the key to a happy life.
