blanks.why: 根据前文“Be kind to those around you”在教人生哲理, 可知是说这么做幸福生活就会离你更近, 故选C。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
“Whee!” I could hear kids cheering all around me. It was Nicky’s birthday party and we were all having fun in the bounce(弹跳) house. We were jumping up as high as we could, and falling down to let the soft ground catch us. I loved {{1}} in bounce houses! I wish I could have one in my backyard.
I looked up the {{2}} of a bounce house and found it was too expensive for me. Maybe if all of my friends and I put our money together, we could buy it! I found them playing outside and asked.
Jake said, “That would be great!” “Yeah, I’m in,” replied Kate. “Good idea!” said Janie. The next day, we all put our money together and found out we had enough! I talked to my parents about my idea. “That would be a lot of fun for you and your friends. We have space in our backyard, but there are some things that I don’t think you’ve considered(考虑) {{3}} . We would have to use our electricity to blow it up every time. That would cost more money, and it would cost money to {{4}} it if it ever got a hole(洞) in it or anything. Are you going to pay for the electricity and repairs(修理费) yourself?” Dad asked. “You’re right. I didn’t think about that…” I replied.
“Maybe something besides a bounce house would {{5}} better. What about a big trampoline(蹦床)?” Mom suggested. “That’s a great idea! We can buy a trampoline!” I said excitedly. “Great! Before we allow all your friends to use a trampoline, we need to make sure everyone will be {{6}} . We need to buy safety equipment(设备) for the trampoline, and we need to make some rules. Does that make sense?” Dad asked. “Yes,” I said. “I’ll talk to my friends tomorrow to make sure we all agree on the {{7}} .” “Perfect!” The next day, we all sat down and came up with rules. We decided that we should not push each other, we should not jump off the trampoline, and we should not land on our heads or necks. Our parents all looked over the rules, and wrote one more: we should have an adult to be outside with us. That seemed fair(公平的) to us, so we {{8}} our money together and got a trampoline!

blanks.mean: 我喜欢在弹跳屋里弹跳！
blanks.why: 根据上一句“We were jumping up as high as we could, and falling down to let the soft ground catch us.”可知, 我们尽可能地跳得高, 然后落下来, 让自己倒在松软的地面上。可知我喜欢在弹跳屋弹跳！故选C。

blanks.mean: 我查看了弹跳屋的价格, 发现那对我来说太贵了。
blanks.why: 根据下文“found it was too expensive for me.”可知, 我发现这对我来说太贵了, 可知是说我查了弹跳屋的价格。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我们的后院是有足够的空间, 但有些事情我认为你没有仔细考虑。
blanks.gloss: carefully认真地, 仔细地；directly直接地；quickly快速地；hopefully希望地。
blanks.why: 根据下一句“We would have to use our electricity to blow it up every time.”可知, 每次我们还得用电充气, 由此可知还没有仔细考虑到这个问题, 应用carefully来修饰动词consider。故选A。

blanks.mean: 那要花更多钱, 如果它里面有洞或其他任何东西的话, 也要花钱修理。
blanks.why: 根据下文“if it ever got a hole(洞) in it or anything”可知, 如果它有洞的话, 修理它要花钱。故选A。

blanks.mean: 也许除了弹跳屋以外还有其他的东西会产生更好的效果。
blanks.why: 根据下文“What about a big trampoline?”可知, 妈妈建议换一个大蹦床也不错, 动词短语work well表示“产生好的效果”。故选D。

blanks.mean: 在我们允许你的所有朋友使用蹦床之前, 我们需要确保每个人都安全。
blanks.gloss: relaxed放松的；safe安全的；active活动的；polite礼貌的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“We need to buy safety equipment(设备) for the trampoline”可知, 我们需要购买蹦床的安全设备, 由此可知我们需要确保每个人都安全。故选B。

blanks.mean: 明天我会和我的朋友们谈谈, 以确保我们都同意这些规则。
blanks.why: 根据上文“we need to make some rules.”可知, 我们需要制定一些规则。由此可知, 明天我会和我的朋友们谈谈, 确保大家都同意这些规则。故选C。

blanks.mean: 这看起来很公平, 所以我们把钱凑在一起买了一个蹦床！
blanks.why: 根据空格后的“our money together and got a trampoline!”可知此处表示我们凑齐钱买了一个蹦床！动词短语pool one’s money表示“集资”。故选B。

title: A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
text:
A Lesson Learned from a Grandparent
David sat alone on the school bus home. He didn’t want to talk to his friends. They were all talking about their class projects for the weekend. They were {{1}} but David wasn’t.
How could they understand his feelings when their parents would be them? Nobody would {{2}} David. His mum worked all the time and his dad never wanted to do anything with him.
“How was school today?” Grandpa asked when David got home.
“It was okay, I guess.”
“You don’t sound like that.”
David told Grandpa about the {{3}} . Each student needed to ask a grown-up for help, and together they would build something. The students needed to make a report to explain how their projects had gone.
“That sounds nice,” Grandpa said “Why does it make you {{4}} ?”
David felt his sadness rising inside him. “I don’t have anyone to help me.”
Grandpa raised his eyebrows. “Who am I?” he asked.
“You’d build a project with me, Grandpa?” David said in surprise.
“Sure, I would,” Grandpa said {{5}} .
David’s heart seemed so light that he thought it would fly away. Maybe this project wouldn’t be so bad.
They sat at the table and made a list of ideas. Finally, they {{6}} to build a robot from old boxes.
Two hours later, the robot was finished. The table was untidy, but David couldn’t stop {{7}} .
“I think it’s the best robot I have ever built. Now I’ll write my report.” David said.
He turned towards his room, but he stopped. He ran to Grandpa and hugged him. “Thank you for helping me, Grandpa. I had a lot of {{8}} .”
Grandpa patted his shoulders. “Me, too. Now, go and write your report. Maybe next time we can make a rocket.”
David smiled. He couldn’t wait any more.

blanks.mean: 他们很兴奋, 但大卫不是。
blanks.gloss: afraid害怕的；worried担心的；carefu小心的；excite兴奋的。
blanks.why: 根据“They were all talking about their class projects for the weekend”可知, 他们都在谈论周末的项目计划, 可见他们都很兴奋。故选D。

blanks.mean: 没有人会帮助大卫。
blanks.why: 根据下文“I don’t have anyone to help me”可知, 没有人帮助他。故选B。

blanks.mean: 大卫把这个项目告诉了爷爷。
blanks.why: 根据上文“They were all talking about their class projects for the weekend.”可知, 他们都在谈论周末的项目计划, 可见他告诉了爷爷这个项目。故选A。

blanks.mean: “听起来不错, ” 爷爷说, “为什么它会让你不开心呢？
blanks.gloss: ” bored无聊的；unhappy不开心的；sorry抱歉的；tired累的。
blanks.why: 根据“David felt his sadness rising inside him.”可知, 大卫感到内心的悲伤在上升, 可见老师的作业让大卫不开心了。故选B。

blanks.mean: “当然, 我会的。
blanks.why: 根据“Sure, I would”可知, 是自信地说。故选D。

blanks.mean: 最后, 他们决定用旧箱子造一个机器人。
blanks.why: 根据“to build a robot from old boxes”可知, 应该是决定建造一个机器人。故选C。

blanks.mean: 桌子很乱, 但大卫玩得停不下来 smiling微笑；cleaning打扫；playing玩；watching观看。
blanks.why: 根据“The table was untidy, but David couldn’t stop…”可知, 前后句表示转折, 桌子凌乱不堪, 但是大卫玩得停不下来。故选C。

blanks.mean: 谢谢你帮助我, 爷爷。
blanks.why: 根据“I had a lot of …”可知, 本题考查短语“玩得开心”have fun。故选C。

title: 从每题给出的A、B、C、D四个选项中
text:
从每题给出的A、B、C、D四个选项中, 选择最佳选项。
Caring for Rio
My brother Sam and I wanted a pet. “You are both in school, and I am at work all day. Pets like cats and dogs need lots of attention,” Mum suggested we think of other kinds of pets. We decided on a {{1}} .
The next weekend, we saw a small parrot at a pet shop. His name was Rio, and he knew how to talk. When he said “Hello there,” Sam and I knew Rio was a perfect {{2}} for us.
Mum agreed we could take Rio home if we {{3}} to take good care of him. As soon as we got home, Mum showed us how to line (铺) the bottom of Rio’s cage with newspaper. “You have to change the paper every other day,” she told us. “Rio should always have a {{4}} cage. You also have to give him fresh food and water every day.”
Rio was a very smart bird. We soon taught him to say our names.
Sam and I made a {{5}} . We each would care for Rio three days a week, and we would work together on Sundays. Later I got busy with football practice and visits with friends. Sometimes I {{6}} to change the newspaper. Sam noticed and began to do my job.
Soon Sam was caring for Rio seven days a week. I thought it was {{7}} until one day Sam and I came home and Rio said, “Hello, Sam. I love you, Sam.”
“Hey Rio, what about me?” I asked. I tried to get him to say hello to me, but he just looked at me.
“Maybe he does not like me any more,” I said to Mum.
“Maybe he knows Sam is taking care of him, and you are not,” Mum said. That night I {{8}} changed clean newspaper for Rio and gave him some food. The very next day I asked Sam if I could care for Rio for the next three weeks.

blanks.mean: 我们决定买一只鸟。
blanks.why: 根据下文“The next weekend, we saw a small parrot at a pet shop.”可知, 作者和哥哥打算买“鸟”作为宠物。故选C。

blanks.mean: 山姆和我知道Rio对我们来说是一个完美的选择。
blanks.why: 根据上文“My brother Sam and I wanted a pet.”及“When he said ‘Hello there’”可知, 作者和哥哥想要选择一种宠物, 小鹦鹉非常机灵, 这对他们来说是一个很好的选择。故选A。

blanks.mean: 妈妈同意我们可以带Rio回家, 只要我们答应好好照顾他。
blanks.why: 根据“Mum agreed we could take Rio home”可知, 作者和哥哥承诺照顾鹦鹉, 妈妈才同意将其带回家；promise to do sth.“承诺做某事”。故选D。

blanks.mean: Rio应该有一个干净的笼子。
blanks.gloss: strong强壮的；clean干净的；beautiful美丽的；safe安全的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“You have to change the paper every other day”可知, 每天都要给鹦鹉的笼子换报纸, 鹦鹉需要一个干净的笼子。故选B。

blanks.mean: 山姆和我制定了一个计划。
blanks.why: 根据下文“We each would care for Rio three days a week, and we would work together on Sundays.”可知, 此处是作者和哥哥制定的照顾鹦鹉的计划。故选A。

blanks.mean: 有时我忘了换报纸。
blanks.why: 根据上下文“Later I got busy with football practice and visits with friends…Sam noticed and began to do my job.”可知, 作者后来忙于自己的事情, 忘记换报纸, 所以哥哥做了作者的工作。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我以为一切都很好, 直到有一天山姆和我回到家。
blanks.gloss: crazy疯狂的；impossible不可能的；important重要的；fine好的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“Soon Sam was caring for Rio seven days a week.”可知, 哥哥独自照顾鹦鹉, 作者认为自己不用照顾是很好的, 直到发现鹦鹉不再和自己亲昵。故选D。

blanks.mean: 那天晚上, 我小心翼翼地给Rio换了干净的报纸。
blanks.gloss: easily容易地；secretly秘密地；carefully仔细地；bravely勇敢地。
blanks.why: 通读文章可知, 作者有一段时间没有照顾鹦鹉, 鹦鹉不再和作者亲昵, 作者决定重新照顾鹦鹉, 可推知作者怀着愧疚的心小心翼翼地照顾鹦鹉。故选C。

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship


Two friends, Ahmad and Ismail, were walking across the desert. The journey was long, and they were very tired from walking in the hot, hot sun. Ismail wanted to {{1}} , but Ahmad was not ready for it. “We have a long way to go,” he said, “We must walk a few more kilometres before we can stop.”
They began to argue (争吵). Ahmad became so angry that he hit Ismail. Ismail fell to his knees in the sand. He was {{2}} and angry. With his finger, he wrote in the {{3}} , “Here, my friend hit me.”
The friends went on their journey across the desert. Not a word was spoken between them. After a long time, they came to an oasis (绿洲) with palm trees and a pool of water. Excited, Ismail ran toward the cool water. But, as he came near the water, he {{4}} that he couldn’t run any more.
The sand was wet. He was pulled down into it, and he couldn’t climb out. He sank (下沉) further and further into the sand, and he became very {{5}} . He shouted to Ahmad, “Help me! Help me！”Ahmad ran forward and reached across the dangerous sand. He took his friend’s arm and pulled him to safety.
Then Ismail took out his {{6}} and on a stone near them, he carved (刻下) these words: “Here, my friend helped me.”
“But why,” said Ahmad, “did you write in the sand when I hit you? But when I helped you, you carved the words in the stone?” “Ah,” said Ismail, “When you hit me, I wrote it in the sand because soon the {{7}} will blow the words away and I won’t remember it any more. But when you helped me, I carved the words in the stone because I’ll never {{8}} that.”

blanks.mean: 伊斯梅尔想休息, 但艾哈迈德还没有准备休息。
blanks.why: 根据“‘We have a long way to go,’ he said, ‘We must walk a few more kilometres before we can stop.’”可知, 伊斯梅尔想休息, 但是艾哈迈德认为还要继续前行, 现在还不到停下的时候。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他又伤心又生气。
blanks.gloss: sad悲伤的；pleased高兴的；nervous紧张的；excited兴奋的。
blanks.why: 根据“Ahmad became so angry that he hit Ismail.”可知, 伊斯梅尔被朋友打了, 他是伤心和生气的。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他用手指在沙子上写道：“这里, 我的朋友打了我。
blanks.why: 根据“did you write in the sand when I hit you?”可知, 艾哈迈德打了伊斯梅尔之后, 伊斯梅尔把这件事写在了沙子上。故选D。

blanks.mean: 但是, 当他走近水边时, 他发现自己再也跑不动了。
blanks.why: 根据“that he couldn’t run any more.”可知, “再也跑不动”是伊斯梅尔自己发现的事。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他在沙子里越陷越深, 他变得非常害怕。
blanks.gloss: afraid害怕的；calm镇静的；brave勇敢的；unhappy不开心的。
blanks.why: 根据“He sank (下沉) further and further into the sand”及“Help me! Help me”可知, 伊斯梅尔在沙子中不断下沉, 变得非常害怕, 于是大声呼救。故选A。

blanks.mean: 然后伊斯梅尔拿出他的刀, 在他们旁边的一块石头上刻上了这些字：“在这里, 我的朋友帮助了我。
blanks.why: 根据“and on a stone near them, he carved (刻下) these words”可知, 用刀在石头上刻字。故选D。

blanks.mean: 当你打我时候, 我把它写在了沙子上, 因为风很快就会把这些字吹走, 我就不会再记得了。
blanks.why: 根据“blow the words away”可知, 风会把沙子上的字吹走。故选B。

blanks.mean: 但当你帮助我时, 我把这句话刻在了石头上, 因为我永远不会忘记。
blanks.why: 根据“But when you helped me, I carved the words in the stone”可知, 字刻在石头上不会消失, 就像记在心间永远不会忘记。故选C。 阅读理解 (共 32 分)

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship
Mark and Jarryd are good friends from Sydney. {{1}} of them enjoy playing Australian football.
A few years ago, when Mark was nine, he had a brain cancer（脑癌）. It made the boy lose his {{2}} and part of his hearing. As a result, Mark couldn’t play football any more. However, Jarryd still shared his love of Australian football with Mark. And they still {{3}} about the Sydney Swans, the team they like best, together.
One day I took my seat at Sydney Cricket Ground to {{4}} the Swans. The old stadium（体育馆）was crowded with football fans. Shortly into the second quarter（局）, I heard some great commentary（现场解说）from a {{5}} . This was Jarryd. He was sitting next to Mark.
Although Mark couldn’t see any more, he still loved the Swans very much. Usually, he went to the stadium and {{6}} to the commentary on the radio. However, in the second quarter of that match, the radio broke down. Just at that time I {{7}} watched the Swans and the team’s star player, Buddy. Instead, the voice between Jarryd and Mark came to my ears. “What’s happening now,” Mark asked. “Don’t worry, Mark（进球）! Buddy is on fire!” Mark listened carefully. He was {{8}} in the magic of Australian football brought to life by his friend.
Here, Jarryd and Mark moved me deeply with their great friendship.

blanks.mean: 他们俩都喜欢踢澳大利亚足球。
blanks.gloss: All三者或三者以上都；Both两者都；Some一些；None三者或三者以上都不。
blanks.why: 承接前句“Mark and Jarryd are good friends from Sydney.”和下文内容可知, 应是他们俩都喜欢踢足球, 故空处应是both。故选B。

blanks.mean: 几年前, Mark九岁时得了脑癌。
blanks.why: 根据“Although Mark couldn’t see any more”的提示可知, 应是脑癌使这个男孩失去了视力和部分听力。故选D。

blanks.mean: 他们仍然关心他们最喜欢的悉尼天鹅队。
blanks.why: 根据前句“However, Jarryd still shared his love of Australian football with Mark.”可推出, 应是他俩仍然关心着悉尼天鹅队。故选C。

blanks.mean: 有一天, 我坐在悉尼板球场观看天鹅队的比赛。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Shortly into the second quarter（局）, I heard some great commentary（现场解说）from a…. This was Jarryd. He was sitting next to Mark.”的语境可知, 应是在观看天鹅队的比赛。故选D。

blanks.mean: 第二局刚开始, 我就听到一个男孩的精彩解说。
blanks.why: 根据后句“This was Jarryd.”和上文“However, Jarryd still shared his love of Australian football with Mark.”可知, Jarryd是一个男孩。故选A。

blanks.mean: 通常, 他都会去体育场听无线电的解说。
blanks.why: 根据空后“on the radio”可知, 应是听现场解说。故选A。

blanks.mean: 就在那时, 我几乎看不到天鹅队和球队的明星球员, Buddy。
blanks.why: 根据后句“Instead, the voice between Jarryd and Mark came to my ears.”可推知, 应是几乎没看到天鹅队和球队的明星球员, 巴迪。故选C。

blanks.mean: 他沉浸在朋友带来的澳大利亚足球的魔力中。
blanks.gloss: sad悲伤的；lost迷失的；upset沮丧的；serious严肃的。
blanks.why: 根据前句“Mark listened carefully.”可推知, 应是Mark迷失在朋友带来的澳大利亚足球的魔力中。故选B。

title: On a snowy evening
text:
On a snowy evening, a rich woman was standing by the road. She was very worried. Her {{1}} had broken down. Just then a poor man named Robert came. He was on his way back home from work as usual.
The woman wondered, “Is the man going to {{2}} me? He looks very cold and hungry.” But to her surprise, he {{3}} and said with a smile, “Can I help you, madam?”
After forty minutes, the car was at last fixed (修理) by Robert. The woman wanted to pay him.
“No, that’s nothing, madam,” he said. “I was just helping someone in {{4}} . If you really want to pay me back, I hope whenever you see someone in need, you should give him a hand.”
A few minutes later, the woman saw a shabby (破旧的) house by the road. She {{5}} Robert’s words, so she stopped.
The hostess (女主人) was very happy to see her, {{6}} asked her in and went to the kitchen to make tea for her. The woman could see that was a poor family and that they needed help. When the hostess was making tea in the kitchen, the woman {{7}} 500 dollars on a table and went away quietly.
Robert came home later than before, thinking how {{8}} their life was. His wife was pregnant (怀孕) and the baby was to be born the next month, but there was not enough money.
His wife went up to him, gave him a kiss and said softly, “Don’t worry, dear! Everything is going to be all right. A stranger has helped us out.”
Let’s always be ready to help others because helping others is helping ourselves.

blanks.mean: 她的车坏了。
blanks.gloss: bike自行车；car汽车；boat船；bus公共汽车。
blanks.why: 根据“After forty minutes, the car was at last fixed (修理) by Robert”可知, 这位女士的小汽车坏掉了。故选B。

blanks.mean: 这个人会帮我吗？
blanks.gloss: help帮助；hit打, 击；drive开车；find找到。
blanks.why: 根据“But to her surprise, he...said with a smile, ‘Can I help you, madam?’”可知, 这位女士想知道这位男士会帮她吗。故选A。

blanks.mean: 但令她吃惊的是, 他停了下来, 微笑着说：“夫人, 我能为您效劳吗？
blanks.why: 根据“He was on his way back home from work as usual”和“...said with a smile, ‘Can I help you, madam?’”可知, 他停了下来。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我只是正在帮助有需要的人。
blanks.gloss: public公众的, 大众的；rain雨；danger危险；need需要, 需求。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
There would be an important exam at the end of this term, and all of my classmates were busy preparing for it. I went into a local library to find a quiet place for studying. But a girl kept singing behind me while I was reading my book. I turned around, knocked on her desk {{1}} and gave the girl a dirty look, “Please think about others in public. I’ve been unable to study because of your terrible singing.” Then the girl stopped singing and it was quiet again.
I still hate thinking of that moment. Let me tell you the rest of the story.
Two hours later, I found that I {{2}} my most important textbook in the library. What was worse, the library had already been closed. I almost wanted to cry. Just then, the phone rang. A soft voice {{3}} the speaker as Jenny and asked if I was Jane. After knowing that I was, she told me that she had noticed my {{4}} in the library. As my phone number was in it, she called and told me she didn’t live far away and could bring it to me.
I was so thankful and agreed to {{5}} her at the store down the road. You can guess who Jenny was. She was the girl I had warned about her singing. When I saw her in the store, I was filled with {{6}} and said sorry for what I had done. But Jenny just {{7}} and told me she was pleased that I had given her a dirty look in the library!
Can you believe we became best friends? I often think how {{8}} I am. She showed me forgiveness (原谅) even though she didn’t have to!

text:
A Family Lesson

Martha was born in a poor family in the countryside in Africa, and people need to pay much money for school. As a result, it was never {{1}} for her to have a life that she wanted. However, at the age of 14, she {{2}} to get an education(教育).
Martha believed that if she held her head high and had enough training, she would achieve the goal (实现目标) that other people only dreamed of. At the age of 15, she started looking for ways to make money for her education. Her father left his family, leaving his children with no other choices but to {{3}} out of school. Martha was ready to show the world that she would not be broken and nothing was going to stop her from being a respected(受人尊敬的) member of society. She found a way of {{4}} a hair product but there wasn’t much money she made. {{5}} , the little money she had would go a long way.
At the age of 16, Martha managed to put herself through high school. After high school, her uncle put her through college where she studied science for 2 years. At 22, she graduated and worked for the Red Cross and her life changed for the {{6}} . A few years later, one of the best companies in her country heard about her ability(能力) and graduate hard work and asked her to work for them.
Today, Martha is one of the most {{7}} women in her family. Martha has also changed the lives of her family members just as she planned. She never gave up and today she is able to walk with her {{8}} high and she is telling you that with an education and a clear goal, you can achieve anything.

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
When I was ten, the best part of the summer was the swimming pool. My friends and I were only interested in which one of us could hold breath underwater the longest. I never thought about how I {{1}} in a swimsuit.
Then one day, when I was swimming over to the ladder to make my way out of the pool, I saw a cute, thin girl standing at the top of the ladder. So I swam {{2}} , waiting patiently（耐心地）for her to move. Instead of moving, she stared （注视） at me for a while and said, “They don’t allow beached whales in this pool. “Then she laughed and walked away. Beached whales? It took me a minute and then it {{3}} me —I looked like those huge animals. From then on, I began to care about my {{4}} and many times I cried over clothes that didn’t fit me.
Things didn’t change much even after I had my baby girl Lucy. To keep her from being laughed at, I dressed her in beautiful things. But she wanted pants and T-shirts. She liked to be {{5}} . However, society wasn’t interested in comfort.
When Lucy was about ten. I showed her an old {{6}} . “That’s me!” she shouted. “No, it isn’t you. It’s me” I told her. We could have been twins. Lucy looked just like me, and I thought she was beautiful. That little girl in the picture seemed to remind me that I was a beautiful little girl with hopes and gifts. I often repeated the story of the little girl at the pool to my daughter, telling her that we should never let others’ words {{7}} our own life.
My daughter is now a teenager with healthy confidence. What society says is not {{8}} . She cares more about what brings her joy. She has taught me that life isn’t measured （衡量）by the size of my clothes, but by who I am.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
Tom loved cars more than anything else. This spring he thought of building a model car to enter for a competition. So he asked his dad for {{1}} .
“Well,” Dad said. “How about this: you do some research first and then come back to me with a design (设计).”
A week later, Tom brought his notes and drawings to Dad. Dad looked over his work, thinking. “Well, that’s interesting,” he said. “Try to {{2}} it as you’ve designed.”
Over three weekends of hard work, Tom turned his design into a real model car and {{3}} it light blue. Dad asked Tom to take it for a test drive. Tom agreed.
After a while, Tom came back to Dad. “Well,” he said. “Now I know {{4}} you wanted me to have a test drive. When I drove fast, there was a problem with it.”
“Very good!” Dad said.
“So, why didn’t you tell me about that {{5}} in the first place?” Sally asked.

Dad smiled. “Good. Sometimes, learning happens during the process.We learn how to do something right by doing it a few times first and making {{7}} along the way.”

title: The Reward of Helping Others
text:
Tobey had always liked zoos. It was great to see animals around his house such as cows, horses and all different kinds of birds. For Tobey, going to the zoo was a great and wonderful way to spend his weekend {{1}} about animals.
Today, he was trying to go to somewhere a little {{2}} . He’d learned that near his house there was an animal shelter (收容所). It wasn’t a common place to adopt (收养) dogs and cats, but a place with lions, tigers and bears.
As he arrived, he was {{3}} , because he heard lions even from the parking lot. The place was small, but clean. And the volunteers (志愿者) there were very helpful. Tobey and his family {{4}} the place at their own pace (节奏), looking at the cages and places the animals lived in.
Tobey {{5}} understood the differences between this place and a zoo. Zoos had beautiful habitats set up for each animal, but you could not get near the animals at all. At this shelter, he was almost {{6}} enough to reach out and touch the animals, even if there were two fences between him and the animals. There weren’t as many people, either, so it seemed like a more personal {{7}} . The paths were covered with trees and it made the animals feel more at home.
It was interesting to look into the eyes of a lion when you could almost reach out and touch it. It was {{8}} to watch the bears walking slowly in front of you. Then there were lions lying lazily in the midday heat and monkeys cleaning themselves. It was a very special experience.
The best part about the place was the stories. Each animal had a story posted on the side of their cage. People {{9}} them from abuse (虐待) or took them to the shelter when they were no longer wanted. These were hard luck stories with a happy ending.
When it was finally time to go, they all {{10}} the volunteers and made a donation. Shelters always needed money, food for animals, and help. It made them feel good to do something they could. It was a great place, and Tobey couldn’t wait to return.

title: A Memorable Journey
text:
Yesterday, 10-year-old Sam Williams returned from space. He is the first child to have made the exciting {{1}} . Will he be the first of many?
On 22nd June, 2016, Sam Williams with three other astronauts set off from Cape Canaveral to the International Space Station. Before that, they had a special {{2}} for their space experience.
Sam firstly entered a newspaper competition for this trip. He had such rich knowledge of space that the judges (裁判员) all {{3}} that he was the perfect child for the space trip.
It took Sam and the three astronauts just six hours to reach the International Space Station. Sam said that he was surprised at how {{4}} they got there. “I always thought that flying to space would take days, but actually it only takes the same number of hours as there are in one school day. Unbelievable!”
Sam was very {{5}} while he was on the Space Station. He helped with many of the science experiments. He also had to make sure that the Space Station was working {{6}} , so he had to clean, check equipment (设备) and make repairs. It was also important for Sam to stay healthy while he was on the Space Station, so he spent a few hours each day {{7}} , which kept his muscles and bones fit and healthy while he was on board.
The Space Station travels through space at 17,500 miles per hour at an altitude (海拔高度) of about 220 miles. While Sam was on board, he orbited (环绕轨道运行) the Earth about once every 90 minutes. During each orbit he was in daylight for about 45 minutes and darkness for about 45 minutes. Sam {{8}} that from Earth we are able to see the Space Station at a certain time.
Sam spent ten days on the Space Station and he is now even more {{9}} in the wonders (景观) of space than he was before his magical trip. He says that he is now 100% sure about what {{10}} he would like to do when he grows up. Can you guess what it is?

title: A Family Lesson
text:
On a sunny afternoon, my father and I were reading together in the living room. My father is an amateur (业余的) {{1}} . He likes writing short stories and some of them were published in the newspapers. I read the stories for a while and then looked at him and said, “Why not write a story myself like them? If you like it, give me a {{2}} !” He agreed happily.
Back to my room, I concentrated (集中精力)on writing. But when the hundredth draft (草稿) still hardly gave me satisfaction, hopelessness filled my heart. I looked out of the window, and listened to the bird purposelessly. How could I make my father {{3}} ? Then I went past the living room to the study {{4}} for help, where I found an interesting story. I was so excited that I took down everything I needed from the book without thinking. Then I took the story to my father. He finished reading, nodded and smiled, “It is excellent, Jay. I am quite sure you can get what you want.” Then he pointed at a line, “Writing really takes study and imagination. I can tell you’re a creative boy from this sentence. So there is nothing I can {{5}} .”
I listened to his praise, my heart beating fast and my hands sweating. What he said made me embarrassed (尴尬的). I didn’t feel like a {{6}} .Mark Twain should have won the prize, because he was the writer of the book.
I stepped back a bit and said, “Dad, I’m sorry. I {{7}} the story from a book, changing the setting and some words. I guessed you might not have read it, so...” My voice lowered, and the tears ran down the cheeks.
“Jay, I am glad that you can realize your mistake.” He patted my head and continued, “That’s because, I know, you want to show your passion (热爱). for writing to me and make me happy. But, my boy, no matter what you want to do, {{8}} always comes first. Remember?”
I nodded, trying to understand his words, which would be the most special prize for me in my life.

blanks.mean: 我父亲是个业余作家。
blanks.why: 根据下文“He likes writing short stories and some of them were published in the newspapers”他喜欢写短篇小说, 其中一些发表在报纸上；可知, 作者的父亲是一名业余作家。故选B。

blanks.mean: 为什么不自己写一个像他们一样的故事呢？
blanks.why: 根据文章最后“I nodded, trying to understand his words, which would be the most special prize for me in my life”……这将是我一生中最特别的奖励；可知, 此处指“作者要求父亲如果喜欢这个故事就要给作者奖励”。故选A。

blanks.mean: 我怎样才能让我父亲感到骄傲？
blanks.why: 根据上文“作者要求父亲, 如果喜欢作者写的这个故事就要给作者奖励”可知此处指“作者希望能写出让父亲引以为豪的作品”。故选D。

blanks.mean: 然后我偷偷地穿过客厅去书房寻求帮助, 在那里我发现了一个有趣的故事。
blanks.why: 根据下文“Then I took the story to my father”然后作者把抄好的故事拿给父亲；可知, 作者是秘密地到书房。故选A。

blanks.mean: 所以我没有什么可以改动的。
blanks.why: 根据下文父亲读完故事说的话“It is excellent, Jay…”可知此处指“父亲满意作者的作品, 没什么需要改动的”。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我觉得自己不是一个获胜者。
blanks.why: 根据“Mark Twain should have won the prize,because he was the writer of the book.” 马克·吐温是这本书的作者；可知, 此处指“作者不觉得自己是获胜者”。故选D。

blanks.mean: 我从一本书中抄袭了这个故事, 改了背景和一些单词。
blanks.why: 根据“Mark Twain should have won the prize, because he was the writer of the book.”可知, 作者抄袭马克·吐温写的一本书上的故事。故选B。

blanks.mean: 但是, 我的孩子, 无论你想做什么, 诚实总是第一位的。
blanks.why: 根据上文“作者抄袭马克·吐温的作品, 主动向父亲承认错误”可知此处指“父亲教育作者无论做什么事, 诚实都是第一的”。故选C。

title: Everybody
text:
“Everybody, it’s time for our group project. Let’s get to work!” says Ms White.

Amy considers telling Ms White about these problems, but she doesn’t want to get Ray in trouble. Instead, she decides to talk to him and find out what the {{2}} is. She says, “Everyone is working hard on our {{3}} . But so far, you haven’t done anything. Is there something wrong?”
Ray thinks {{4}} for a few seconds, and finally says, “It’s not that I don’t want to be in the {{5}} . Sometimes, I don’t really understand the things we’re learning. I know it’s not fair (公平的), but I don’t want to say something stupid, {{6}} I do nothing.
Now Amy understands. Ray isn’t lazy—he just needs help! “From now on,” she says, “I will try my best to {{7}} you to feel more confident (自信的). Then you can do your share, and it will be fair for everyone.”“Thank you! I’ll try hard to do my part.” says Ray.

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
Who Did Jeffery's Homework?

Jeffery loves outdoor games like hockey and basketball. He is a good sports player but he is not interested in studies. He never does homework. "Too boring," he says. His teachers tell him," Jeffery! Do your homework, or you can't learn a thing. "But what can he do? He {{1}} homework.
One day, he found his cat playing with a little doll and he took it away. When he looked at it closely, he found that it wasn't a doll at all but a man of the smallest size. It was a little elf（精灵）! The elf shouted, "Save me! Don't give me back to the cat. You can make a {{2}} if you save me. "
""How {{3}} I am!" Jeffery thought. Here was the answer to all of his problems. So he said, "Please do all my homework till the end of this term and make sure I can get A's. If you make my wish come true, I'll let you go then." The little elf agreed.
And true to his word, the little elf began to do Jeffery's homework. But there was one problem — the elf didn't always know how to do the homework and needed {{4}} . When doing reading, the elf asked Jeffery to {{5}} new words in the dictionary. When doing history, the elf needed Jeffery to go to the {{6}} to borrow books and read to him.
Jeffery was working harder than ever! He stayed up late at night and got up early in the morning. That little elf was driving him crazy! He never felt so {{7}} . Finally the last day of school arrived and the elf was free to go. As for homework, Jeffery didn't hate to do it anymore.
He got his A's. His classmates and teachers were all surprised. They {{8}} what had happened to Jeffery. Do you know who really helped Jeffery?

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

Lucy tried not to be nervous. It was her first day at a new school. She had no idea who to sit with. Then a girl with a big, bright smile waved Lucy over to her table. Lucy sat down beside her. “I’m Dinah. You look like an artist,” she said. “Hi, I’m Lucy. I like art,” Lucy said. “Me, too! Let’s {{1}} at your house this weekend. I’ll bring my markers (马克笔). You can make us cookies,” Dinah said. “OK,” Lucy said, {{2}} to have a new friend.
On Saturday, Dinah came to Lucy’s house. Lucy took out the strawberry cookie, fresh from the oven. “I like chocolate chip better. I told you that.” But in fact, Dinah had told her nothing of the kind. When she finished the cookies, she sat down on Lucy’s {{3}} and said, “Let’s draw here.” Lucy hesitated (犹豫). But she wanted Dinah to like her, so she {{4}} . While they were drawing, Dinah’s marker slipped and made a long, black line on Lucy’s bedspread (床罩). “It was a/an {{5}} !” Dinah said. But it seemed not.
That night at dinner, Lucy didn’t feel happy because Dinah confused her a lot. “What’s wrong, Lucy?” her dad asked. Lucy told her father what happened. “Friends make us feel {{6}} . Does Dinah make you feel like this?” “Sometimes, but sometimes I’m afraid of her,” Lucy answered. Lucy’s dad smiled. “To have a friend, you have to be a friend. Maybe Dinah hasn’t {{7}} that yet but you have.” “Dinah told me not to play with other kids,” Lucy said. “Dinah is in charge of (掌控) Dinah. You’re in charge of you,” dad said.
The next day at lunch, Dinah waved and asked Lucy to sit beside her. “Let’s sit with Ana,” Lucy said. “No, she is mean,” Dinah said. Then Ana smiled at Lucy, and it made Lucy feel a little {{8}} . “I’m going to sit with Ana. Come with me,” Lucy said. “Lucy, sit down!” Dinah said loudly but Lucy didn’t sit down. “If you want to be my friend, you need to be a friend to me. I hope you will.” Lucy said, turned and walked over to Ana. She sat down and looked at Ana. “How’s it going?” asked Ana. Lucy took a deep breath and said, “Better.”

title: 通读下面的短文, 掌握其大意
text:

When I was 13, my only purpose (目标) was to become the star on our football team. That meant beating Miller King, the best player at our school.
The football season started in September, and all summer long I {{1}} my football everywhere for practice. Just before September, Miller was knocked down by a car and lost his right arm. I went to see him after he came back from the hospital. He looked very {{2}} , but he didn’t cry.
That season, I {{3}} all of Miller’s records while he watched the home games from the chair. We went 10-1 and I was named the best player, {{4}} I often had crazy dreams in which I was to blame (负责) for Miller’s accident.
One afternoon, I saw Miller in great trouble when going over a short wall — which wasn’t hard to climb if he had both arms. I was sure I was the last person he wanted to accept {{5}} from. However, he agreed. To my surprise, he moved slowly over the wall with my help. When we were finally safe on the other side, he said to me, “You know, I didn’t tell you this during the season, but you did {{6}} . Thanks a lot!”
His words freed me from my bad {{7}} . Disabled but not defeated (被击败的), he was {{8}} the most excellent one. To me, he was more than a winner.

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship

Katy Sullivan is an actress, an athlete, and a person who doesn’t like to use the words “no” or “I can’t”.
She was born without the lower half of her legs and has worn prosthetic legs (假肢) all her life. {{1}} , her family has treated her the same way they would treat anyone else. She kept up with her brothers and sisters at the gym and in the swimming pool.
When a person is born without legs, there are lots of things that are {{2}} 
to do. But Sullivan believes she could do anything. She chose to do two things that are difficult even with both {{3}} .
As a teenager, she saw a movie that had a great influence on her. Before it was over, Sullivan had made her mind up to be an actress.
She {{4}} a degree in theater and then moved to Los Angeles, where she has played {{5}} in theater, television and movies. She has a positive view of life. She thinks that if you believe you can do something, you should go for it. So when Sullivan’s friend asked her whether she’d like to try {{6}} , she said “yes”. She was given a pair of running legs and {{7}} her new life.
Sullivan was the first person in the world with two prosthetic legs to take up running as a competitive sport. She made it to the 100-meter finals in the 2012 London Paralympics.
Sullivan’s family, friends and fans look up to her as a/an {{8}} of someone who has overcome difficulties and achieved her dreams.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

It was on a cold morning that my mother came into my bedroom with a red {{1}} . She said it was very cold outside and asked me to wear it to school. “I spent the whole night weaving (编织) the sweater.” She told me.
The sweater was so unfashionable and ugly that I didn’t like it at all. After mom went out to work, I {{2}} the ugly sweater to a corner. Although I would catch a cold, I didn’t wear the sweater. I thought my classmates would {{3}} at me. I put on a thin uniform and went to school.
Before I walked into the classroom, I heard Lana’s voice, “Look at my overcoat. My father bought it in Hong Kong.” Connie said, “My scarf is expensive, too.”
I looked through the window and was surprised to see all the girls in colorful winter clothes but I didn’t have. They {{4}} their clothes to each other and laughed happily. Suddenly, I felt inferior (低于他人的) to them. Why wasn’t my family as {{5}} as theirs? I wanted to wear beautiful clothes, too.
A strong cold wind blew and I sneezed. During class I didn’t feel very well. The school doctor said I had caught a cold. “You should wear warm clothes today.” she said. I suddenly thought of my mom. She said the same thing to me but I didn’t listen.
As soon as I got home, I fell asleep on the sofa. I {{6}} of a woman weaving. She was my mother! She spent the whole night making a sweater for me. But I didn’t thank her or wear the sweater, either.
When I opened my eyes, my mother was smiling at me. Her eyes were full of worry and {{7}} . I held her in my arms and said, “Sorry, mom, I should {{8}} complained (抱怨) about that sweater.”
Two days later, I wore the warm and comfortable sweater to school. Some of my classmates laughed at me. But I didn’t care. I know mom’s love is more important than money.

blanks.why: 根据“I spent the whole night weaving (编织) the sweater.”可知是花了一整晚织毛衣, 可推测出毛衣, 故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“I fell asleep on the sofa”可知是在沙发上睡着了, 可推测出梦到, 故选B。

blanks.why: 根据“full of worry”可知是担心, 可推测出关心, 故选A。

title: The Reward of Helping Others
text:
Mom was leaving home to volunteer in the food kitchen. She went there three times a week offering {{1}} for the poor people. Jason was tired of watching TV. His friends were away on vacation. “Mom, I’m {{2}} ,” said Jason. “There is nothing to do.” “Why don’t you come with me?” Mom asked. “I don’t know anything about working at a food kitchen,” said Jason. “It’s very easy,” said Mom.
Jason was excited to be in the food kitchen. He {{3}} his mom put some turkey on a plate and some mashed potatoes. She then passed the plate to the next lady, and she put some green beans and bread on the plate. “I can do that,” thought Jason. One of the volunteers {{4}} early, so Jason took over (接手) her work in the serving line. He helped 25 people that day. After the {{5}} closed, Jason and his Mom stayed to clean up.
Jason enjoyed his day at the food kitchen. He couldn’t {{6}} to tell his Dad about how much fun he had. “Not only did it give me something to do, but I felt so good doing it,” Jason told his Dad. Dad said, “Jason, that was a nice thing you did today.” “You helped many people who weren’t as {{7}} as you to have a hot meal,” Mom said, “We’re so proud of you Jason!”
Jason went to bed that night thinking about the food kitchen. “I am going to help out again,” he said to himself. Jason made some new friends, and he didn’t even {{8}} they lived so close to him in town! The best part was how good he felt inside.

blanks.why: 根据上文“Mom was leaving home to volunteer in the food kitchen.”可知, 妈妈做义工的地方是厨房, 所以她的工作应是给贫穷的人提供食物, 也就是提供午餐。故选B。

blanks.gloss: bored感到无聊的；angry生气的；happy快乐的；relaxed感到放松的。
blanks.why: 根据下文“There is nothing to do.”可知, Jason无事可做, 所以他会感到无聊。故选A。

blanks.why: 根据下文“…his mom put some turkey on a plate and some mashed potatoes. She then passed the plate to the next lady, and she put some green beans and bread on the plate. ‘I can do that,’ thought Jason.”可推知, 看完妈妈的一整套动作之后Jason才知道工作内容, 他才能判断出他能胜任这份工作, “watched”符合文意。故选D。

blanks.why: 结合“…so Jason took over her work…”和选项可知, 这名志愿者应是离开了这个岗位, Jason才能接手这个岗位的工作。故选A。

blanks.why: 根据上文“Mom was leaving home to volunteer in the food kitchen.”可知, Jason和妈妈是去厨房做义工, 所以他们会在厨房关门后留下来打扫卫生。故选C。

blanks.why: 结合“He couldn’t…to tell his dad…”和选项可知, 此处应用短语“can’t wait to do sth.”, 表达“迫不及待地想告诉他爸爸”的意思。故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
Jack was building a snowman in his front yard (院子). He needed to finish it before his father came home. His new neighbor, Tracy, was {{1}} Jack play at her window. She ran to Jack’s yard and asked if she could help him.
“Yes, please,” Jack said. “My father will be home very soon.”
“Okay. What can I do?” Tracy asked.
“I’ve built my snowman’s body with two snowballs I need another one for its head.”
“But snowmen only need one snowball for the body and one for the head,” Tracy explained.
“No, snowmen always have three snowballs. I don’t need your {{2}} now.” Jack said.
Jack {{3}} up some snow and made it into a snowball. He rolled the snowball away from Tracy to make it big enough for the head of his snowman. Tracy went back to her yard and began to build her own snowman.
“I don’t want to {{4}} Jack anyway,” she thought to herself. Tracy made the snowman with two big snowballs. She found some sticks and pine cones (松果) for her snowman’s eyes and mouth and arms.
Jack used buttons for his snowman’s eyes and mouth. Then, he used a carrot for the {{5}} . At that time, Jack’s father was driving up the street. Suddenly, the head fell off and crashed (坠落) to the ground!
“No!” Jack said {{6}} , “ My father is almost home!”
Tracy heard Jack’s cry and ran over to see what the problem was.
“I’ll help you,” Tracy said.
Together, they made a new snowball for the head and put the carrot and buttons on it.
“We made it!” Jack said. “Thank you.”
“You’re welcome. I think your snowman is {{7}} ,” Tracy said. “Mine doesn’t have a nose.”
Jack walked over to see Tracy’s snowman. He loved it, but he knew it wasn’t finished. Jack ran back to his snowman and {{8}} the carrot out. He broke it into two pieces and gave half to Tracy. She put it on her snowman and said, “I think our snowmen make good neighbors.”

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson
People always seemed to make me as the conversation topic in grade school. I was quiet and shy. I never got a chance of making friends.
“Teacher, Kimi is so strange. Why is she writing with her left hand?” One day I heard a little girl saying that again. That night I forced myself to write with my right hand. Mother {{1}} the pen away from me. She said I would be fine because there was nothing wrong with left-handed writing. I asked her to give it back and then I {{2}} . How I wanted to be like the other kids!
Another day, as I was going through the mall, I noticed the shoes with wheels. I saw the other kids trying them on and doing cool tricks. I asked my mother to buy a pair. Then she asked, “You do not usually want this sort of things. What changed your {{3}} ?” I told my mother about my school and how I still had no friends for five months. My mother hugged me and said, “I will buy you these shoes, but don’t let other people get into your head.”
I went to school with my new shoes, not wanting to show them. Then I realized the other students had the shoes like mine. I found {{4}} that I was able to talk to them, but as soon as I showed them my shoes, one said, “Huh? Where did you get them? From a cheap store?” The other girls laughed {{5}} . I didn’t think I was close to being their friends, but I was even further from them. That day I went home crying and told my mother it didn’t {{6}} . She comforted me. “Don’t worry. You still have us. If those friends care about you because you have cool items, they are not your true friends,” she added. “If you don’t have friends now, you will find one soon. Just give it some time, okay?”
Years after that, I began to understand my mother’s {{7}} . “Kimi, you’re so lucky. Myth says left-handed people are talented or smart.” Actually I’m neither talented nor smart, but I’m a left-handed writer. It was {{8}} throughout my childhood, but now I’m in high school with friends that I thought I would never have had.

blanks.why: take sth. away from sb.从某人那里拿走某物。故选D。

blanks.why: 根据“How I wanted to be like the other kids!”可知作者希望能和别的孩子们一样, 但却做不到, 应是难过地哭了。故选B。

blanks.why: 根据“You do not usually want this sort of things.”可知作者之前不想要的东西现在想要了, 应是改变主意, change one’s mind改变主意。故选A。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

I remember being really happy for my friend Avery when she won the championship, although I admit I was also a little bit envious (嫉妒的). When Avery and I tried out for Alice in Wonderland, however, things went the {{1}} way.
Avery really hoped to get picked to be Alice, but I didn’t {{2}} what part I would get as long as I was in it. A few days later, we raced over to the theater office to see the cast list.
“That can’t be right,” Avery said. “There must be some mistake!”
But I really and truly was given the {{3}} of Alice. Avery got the role of the March Hare.
“Do you want to come over to {{4}} our lines?” I asked.
“You mean your lines?” Avery said, not even looking at me. “No, thanks. I’m pretty busy this week.”
“OK,” I said. “How about some day next week?”
“Sorry,” she turned back. “I’m pretty sure I’m busy forever.”
That night at dinner, my parents congratulated me for getting the lead role. “Well, I’m really confused,” I said. “Avery was so {{5}} because I was picked to be Alice. She pretty much threw away our friendship.”
“Hmm,” said my mom, “sometimes when our friends do well, we feel envious and don’t know how to {{6}} . She just needs a little time and understanding.”
Over the next week, I did my best to give Avery some space. Then at rehearsal (排练) one day, I went up to her, “I know you didn’t exactly love the idea of being the March Hare, but you’re such a talented actor, and the way you say your lines is so awesome.” I smiled.
“Thanks,” said Avery.
“Well,” I said, “I’m still struggling with a few things about my character. I’d love your help if you have any free time.”
“I think I might be free on Thursday.” She {{7}} .
Our play ended up going great. Even though things were rough for a little while with Avery and me, they’re better than ever now! Avery even apologized (道歉) for the way she’d been acting at first.
People often have a hard time dealing with their feelings of envy and disappointment. If you happen to be the lucky one who’s doing amazingly well, give your teammate a little time and {{8}} , and he or she just might come around before too long. This might be the perfect time for you to be an extra-good friend.

blanks.mean: 当艾弗里和我参加《爱丽丝梦游仙境》的选拔时, 结果却适得其反。

blanks.why: 根据“But I really and truly was given the…of Alice”可知, 让作者饰演这个角色, 故选C。

blanks.mean: 你想过来练习我们的台词吗？

blanks.gloss: upset沮丧的；nervous紧张的；pleased满意的；surprised惊讶的。

blanks.why: 根据“don’t know how to”可知, 此处指不知道怎么做, 故选A。

blanks.why: 根据“I think I might be free on Thursday”可知, 作者邀请艾弗里帮忙, 艾弗里微笑地回答, 故选B。

title: A Family Lesson
text:

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
One day a teacher taught a group of students how to manage (支配) time. He gave such an interesting example that his {{1}} would never forget.
He put a wide jar on the table, {{2}} some rocks and carefully put them into the jar one at a time.
When he filled the jar to the top and no more rocks would fit inside, he asked, “Is this jar {{3}} ?” Everyone in his class shouted, “Yes.”
“Really?” he asked. “Let’s see.” He pulled out a bag of small stones and put some in. The {{4}} went down into the space between the big rocks. Again, he asked the same question, “Is this jar full?”
“Maybe not,” one of them {{5}} . “Very good!” he replied. He then brought out a box of sand. He started {{6}} the sand into the jar. One more he asked, “Is this jar full?”
“No!” the class shouted.
“Good!” he replied. Then he poured a cup of water into the jar until it was full.
Then he asked, “What is the point (重点) here?” One student put up his hand and said, “Try really hard, and you can always put more {{7}} in!”
“Well, you are right,” the teacher replied. “But that’s not the only point. Besides (除……之外) that, I hope you know more about it. Put the big rocks in {{8}} , or you can’t get others in. What are the ‘big rocks’ in your life? Time with your friends, your education, or your dreams. Remember to put these big rocks in first, or you can’t get them in at all.”

title: A Family Lesson
text:
“Mommy, look!” cried my daughter, Darla, pointing to a chicken hawk in the air. "Uh huh, "I answered, driving, lost in thought about the timetable of my day.
Disappointment {{1}} her face.
“What's the matter, sweetheart?” I asked.
“Nothing,” my seven-year-old daughter said. The moment was gone. Dinner, baths and phone calls filled the hours until bedtime.
" Come on, Darla, time for bed! "She raced past me up the stairs. Tired, I kissed her and hugged her.
“Mom, I forgot to give you something! "she said.
“Give it to me in the morning. "I said. My {{2}} was gone. I could hardly stay cool.
“You won't have time in the morning! "she talked back quickly.
"I’ll take time,” I answered. Sometimes no matter how hard I tried, time was never enough.
She wasn't ready to {{3}} up yet. "No, you won't! It will be just like today when I told you to look at the chicken hawk. You didn't {{4}} listen to what I said.”
I was too tired to argue, and she hit too close to the truth. "Good night!" I shut the door in anger.
Later though, her gray-blue eyes filled my vision as I thought about how little time we really had until she was grown and gone. My husband asked me about what was going on and I told him.
“Maybe she was not asleep yet. Why don' t you {{5}} ?"he said.
I followed his advice, {{6}} it was my own idea. I opened her door gently. In Darla's hand I could see her paper all crumpled up. She had torn into small pieces a big red heart with a poem she had written titled,"Why I Love My Mother?”
Why I Love My Mother
Although you're busy, and you work so hard
You always take time to play with me
I love you Mommy,
Because l am the biggest part of your busy day!
Tears filled my eyes. When I softly touched her face, she awakened from a dreamless sleep and asked, "Why are you {{7}} , Mommy?”
“You are the most important part of my busy day!”
She smiled and then went back to sleep, not really understanding how strongly I {{8}} what I said.

text:
A Family Lesson
The other day, I was sitting in the study and working on my website, a cup of tea on the table and old songs from my computer. It was a special pleasure to have such a {{1}} day after weeks of hiking, snowboarding and going crazy.
“Hi dad! Want some orange juice, graybeard?” Coyote yelled (叫喊) to me much louder than {{2}} “No, just bring me some chips!” I shouted back.
One time, when I misheard what he said three times in a row, he {{3}} that I had become too old and started to hear worse. Since then, yelling at me has become a kind of family joke.

text:
A Family Lesson
I stare at the broken vase on the floor. It was Mom’s favorite. Now it’s in a million pieces. It was silly to play {{1}} inside with Mom away. I wasn’t thinking about that, though. Saturday is my team’s final match. I just wanted to practice a little more. Now I’m in {{2}} !
Rusty thinks I am playing—not {{3}} up the vase He jumps up and down barking happily. This gives me an {{4}} .
Mum comes back. Rusty jumps up to greet Mom, his tail wagging.
“I’m sorry, Mom, but Rusty {{5}} your vase,” I lie, looking at my feet.
“Rusty, you bad boy!” she scolds. Rusty whines. A sick feeling rises in my heart. “You go outside,” says Mom. Rusty hangs his head in shame.
“Go to your doghouse, Rusty,” I say, holding the door open. Rusty slumps to his doghouse looking sad. I close the door and try to think about something else. Then it begins to rain hard. I can’t help but {{6}} out the window. Rusty shivers in his doghouse. That sick feeling in my heart grows.
Rusty peeks (偷看) out. Rain falls down his nose as if he is crying. What have I done? I ask myself. Rusty is in trouble because of my lie.
“Mom, I have something to tell you.” I say. “I was playing soccer in the house and I broke the vase.” I {{7}} explain.
“Blaming Rusty for your mistake was wrong,” Mom says. “Thank you for being {{8}} ,” she adds.
“Let Rusty back inside now,” she says. I open the door and Rusty runs back in. He jumps up and gives me a big lick. Suddenly, my heart feels warm.

“We brought her down to see what was happening,” said Don Chaffee, a Cruiser official. “At first, she said, ‘I can't do that.’ Then she realized, ‘I can do that. I'm going to do that.’”
Just over a year after her accident, Thompson was a good wheelchair athlete. Her {{4}} was track and field (田径).
Thompson also played basketball in her college. It wasn't {{5}} for her. She had never played basketball before her accident. Now she was learning the sport in a wheelchair. She tried out for the, U. S. Paralympic women’ s basketball team, and she {{6}} it.
Thompson is a role model for millions of people. She wanted to tell kids through her story. “Try,” she said. “Really try. If you want to do something, try your best to do it. If you really want to do something, you can find a {{7}} to do it.”

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
The Meaning of True Friendship
Jerry was a manager of a restaurant. He was always in a good mood(情绪)and always had something {{1}} to say. Sometimes when the waiters or cooks in the restaurant had a bad day, Jerry always came up with a smile, and helped them to look on the bright {{2}} .
One day a friend asked Jerry, "How can you be so positive all the time?" He replied,"Every morning I tell myself that I have two {{3}} to be in a good mood or in a bad one. I always choose the good one. When something {{4}} happens, I can be sad and angry or I can learn instead. I choose to learn life is all about choices. You can't stop bad things from happening, but you can {{5}} your own attitude."
One morning, Jerry left the restaurant's back door open and three robbers (抢劫犯)with guns broke in. When Jerry was asked to open the safe, he was so {{6}} that he couldn't get the password correct. The robbers shot him in anger and hurried off. Luckily, Jerry was found and taken to hospital in time. After many hours of operation, Jerry was {{7}} saved.
When he was asked what he was thinking during the accident, he said, "When lying on the floor, I {{8}} the two choices. To live or to die? I chose to live. When I was in the hospital, the nurse asked me if I was allergic (对……过敏) to anything, I replied 'Yes'. Then I took a deep breath and shouted, 'Bullets (子弹)'. They started laughing and I said, 'My choice is to live, so {{9}} me as I am alive, not dead.'"
Thanks to the skills of the doctors, now Jerry is as well as before. However, his amazing {{10}} played an even more important role.

blanks.mean: 他总是好情绪, 说一些鼓励的话。
blanks.why: 根据后文when the waiters or cooks in the restaurant had a bad day, Jerry always came up with a smile, and helped them to look on the bright当服务员或厨师不愉快时, 他总是面带微笑, 帮助他们看到阳光的一面, 可知说一些鼓励的话；故选D。

blanks.mean: 帮助他们看到阳光的一面。
blanks.why: 根据前文when the waiters or cooks in the restaurant had a bad day, Jerry always came up with a smile当服务员或厨师不愉快时, 他总是面带微笑；可知是“帮助他们看到阳光的一面”；故选A。

blanks.mean: 每天早晨我告诉自己有两个选择, 有一个好心情还是一个坏心情。
blanks.why: 根据be in a good mood or in a bad one有一个好心情还是一个坏心情 , I always choose the good one.我总是选择好的那一个, 可知是“两个选择”；故选B。

blanks.mean: 当事情出问题时, 我伤心、生气还是吸取教训。
blanks.why: 根据 I can be sad and angry or I can learn instead伤心、生气还是吸取教训, 可知是“错误的事情发生”；故选A。

blanks.mean: 但是你能决定你的态度。
blanks.why: 根据You can't stop bad things from happening你不能阻止坏的事情发生, “决定你的态度”符合题意；故选C。

blanks.mean: 他是如此的紧张以至于想不起密码。
blanks.why: 根据three robbers (抢劫犯)with guns broke in三个抢劫犯带着枪破门而入, 可知是紧张；故选C。

blanks.mean: 最后杰瑞被救了。
blanks.why: 根据after many hours of operation几个小时的手术后, 可知“最后被救了”；故选B。

blanks.mean: 当我躺在地板上时, 我记起了两个选择。
blanks.why: 根据 he was asked what he was thinking during the accident他被问到在事故发生期间想什么, 可知“记得, 想起”符合语境；故选A。

blanks.mean: 我的选择是活, 因此当我活着时治疗我, 而不是死的时候。
blanks.why: 根据上文可知这是对护士说的话, 可知是“治疗”, 符合语境；故选B。

blanks.mean: 他超赞（惊人）的态度起着更重要的作用。
blanks.why: 考查名词辨析。words话；purpose目的；actions行为；attitude态度； you can 5 your own attitude你可以决定你的态度, 可知杰瑞能够恢复健康, 除了医生的医术, 他的“态度”起到了更重要的作用；故选D。

title: A Family Lesson
text:
I still remember my father spent plenty of time teaching me how to pronounce a word, how to understand something that I saw for the first time and how to be polite to others. And I will never {{1}} one sentence my father used to say to me, "I love you, son. Say you love me, son." Naturally, I would scream, "I love you, Dad."
When I was growing up, I found that I had little in {{2}} with my father gradually. Sometimes we often argued about something sharply and then the argument changed into a quarrel (争吵). I knew there was a gap between us. I didn't {{3}} hearing the words "I love you" from my father the last time. To tell you the truth, I couldn't honestly remember when I had last said those words to him, either.
Now father was in hospital. The doctor said it was {{4}} and he needed an operation at once, {{5}} he wasn't sure whether my father was able to survive (幸免于, 经受得住) it. Everything in my childhood {{6}} in my mind. Then I called and said, "Dad, I love you!"
There was a {{7}} at the other end and he replied coldly, "Well, I love you, too!"
I cried and said, "Dad, I know you love me, and when you are {{8}} , I know you will say what you want to say."
Fifteen minutes later my mother called and nervously asked, "Paul, is everything OK?"
A few weeks later, I was working when I received my father's call, "Paul, I love you." I was so {{9}} that my tears rolled down my cheeks. Perhaps both of us {{10}} that this special moment had taken our relationship to a new level.
A short while after this special moment, my father finally narrowly escaped death following the heart operation. I can't {{11}} that if I did not take the first {{12}} and Dad did not survive the surgery, what kind of life I would lead now.

blanks.mean: “我”将从不会忘记父亲给“我”说的一句话。
blanks.why: 根据 “"I love you, son. Say you love me, son." Naturally, I would scream, "I love you, Dad." 可知, “我”将从不会忘记父亲给“我”说的一句话, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 当“我”长大时, “我”发现和父亲有很少的共同点。
blanks.why: 根据“Sometimes we often argued about something sharply and then the argument changed into a quarrel (争吵).”有时我们经常激烈地争论某件事, 然后争论就变成了争吵。可知, 当“我”长大时, “我”发现和父亲的共同点就少了。故选C。

blanks.mean: “我”不记得最后一次听到父亲说“我爱你”。
blanks.why: 根据“To tell you the truth, I couldn't honestly remember when I had last said those words to him, either.” 说实话, 我也记不清我上次对他说这些话是什么时候。可知, “我”不记得最后一次听到父亲说“我爱你”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 医生说父亲病的很严重。
blanks.why: 根据“he needed an operation at once”他需要马上动手术。可知, 父亲病的很严重。故选B。

blanks.mean: 但是他也不确定我的父亲能否活下来。
blanks.why: 考查连词辨析。but但是；because因为；so所以；and和。句子“he needed an operation at once”与句子“he wasn't sure whether my father was able to survive (幸免于, 经受得住) it.”之间存在着转折关系, 因此用but连接。故选A。

blanks.mean: 童年的每一件事都出现在“我”的脑海里。
blanks.why: 根据“Then I called and said, "Dad, I love you!"”然后我打电话说：“爸爸, 我爱你！”可知, 作者童年的每一件事都出现在脑海里, 故选A。

blanks.mean: 另一端有一个惊奇, 他冷冷地回答说：“好吧, 我也爱你！
blanks.why: 结合语境可知, 作者的父亲病的很重, 他们又好久没有说“我爱你”了, 这次听到父亲说“我也爱你！”, 作者感到很意外。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我哭着说：“爸爸, 我知道你爱我, 当你准备好了, 我知道你会说你想说的话。
blanks.why: 由的；ready准备好；happy高兴的；excited兴奋的。be ready：准备好。故选B。

blanks.mean: “我”如此地感动, 以至于眼泪流了下来。
blanks.why: 根据“my tears rolled down my cheeks.”眼泪流了下来。可知, 作者是很感动的。故选A。

blanks.mean: 也许我们两个都意识到这一特殊时刻使我们的关系达到了一个新的水平。
blanks.why: 根据“Perhaps both of us 10 that this special moment had taken our relationship to a new level.”也许我们两个都_______ 这一特殊时刻使我们的关系达到了一个新的水平。可知, 选择realized意识到；符合语境。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我无法想象, 如果我不迈出第一步, 爸爸也没有从手术中幸存下来, 我现在会过怎样的生活。
blanks.why: 根据“if I did not take the first 12 and Dad did not survive the surgery”如果我不迈出第一步, 爸爸也没有从手术中幸存下来。可知, 作者无法想象现在会过怎样的生活。故选C。 27题详解】 句意：我无法想象, 如果我不迈出第一步, 爸爸也没有从手术中幸存下来, 我现在会过怎样的生活。 考查名词辨析。advice建议；step步骤；word单词；world世界。句子“if I did not take the first____”可知, 这是虚拟语气, 语境是：如果“我”没有迈出第一步, 父亲能否活下来。故选B。

title: The Reward of Helping Others
text:
The Reward of Helping Others

It is not always easy to discover yourself. From a young age, I had a strong sense of who I would become-but an accident changed everything.
To me, skating was more important than anything else in the world. Nothing else filled my heart with so much {{1}} . I spent 24 hours a week developing my skills. I had no social life or interests other than {{2}} . But I was rewarded(回报)with first place medals in nearly every competition.
Unfortunately, during one competition, I fell and hurt my {{3}} badly. The doctor told me that I couldn't skate anymore. The pain in my back was hard to bear and even basic daily tasks became {{4}} .
My passion(激情) had been taken away. I lost heart and had no idea what I would become. After eight months of suffering, something had to {{5}} . Instead of sitting around and wasting my days, I began to work with local community service projects. By volunteering as a swimming teacher and summer reading assistant(助教)for kids, I got an idea of who I wanted to become. After a few months, I found a new interest. Little by little, I {{6}} out of the shadow and rebuilt my confidence.
Sometimes, challenges in life will get in our way. We can choose to stay {{7}} or try to get past these challenges. My accident was a challenge that failed to stop me from {{8}} success. Today, I'm a very confident and optimistic(乐观的) person.

blanks.mean: 没有什么比这更让我感到幸福了。
blanks.gloss: carelessness粗心；happiness幸福, 开心；sadness悲伤；hopefulness希望。
blanks.why: 根据后文“I had no social life or interests other than…”可知, 我没有别的社交和兴趣, 所以没有什么比这更让我开心、幸福了。故选B。

blanks.mean: 除了滑冰, 我没有其他的社交生活和兴趣。
blanks.why: 根据“To me, skating was more important than anything else in the world.”可知, 对我来说, 滑冰比世界上任何事情都重要。故选D。

blanks.mean: 不幸的是, 在一次比赛中, 我摔倒了, 背部严重受伤。
blanks.why: 根据后文“The pain in my back was hard to bear”可知, 我是背部受伤。故选A。

blanks.mean: 背部的疼痛难以忍受, 甚至连基本的日常工作都变得困难。
blanks.gloss: boring无聊的；interesting有趣的；difficult困难的；easy简单的。
blanks.why: 根据“The pain in my back was hard to bear”可知, 背部的疼痛难以忍受, 而且由于受伤, 所以连基本的日常工作都变得困难。故选C。

blanks.mean: 在八个月的痛苦之后, 有些事情必须改变。
blanks.why: 根据后文的“Instead of sitting around and wasting my days, I began to work with local community service projects.”可知, 我没有闲坐着浪费时间, 而是开始参与当地的社区服务项目, 所以应该是进行改变。故选A。

blanks.mean: 渐渐地, 我走出了阴影, 重建了信心。
blanks.why: 根据后半句“rebuilt my confidence”可知, 我重拾了信心, 所以是走出了之前的阴影,step out of “走出”。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们可以选择停滞不前, 也可以尝试着克服这些挑战。
blanks.why: 根据“Sometimes, challenges in life will get in our way.”和“or try to get past these challenges”可知, 有时生活中的挑战会阻碍我们, 我们可以选择克服这些挑战, 相反的就是停滞不前, 可用stay behind表示。故选B。

blanks.mean: 我的意外是一种挑战, 并没有阻止我获得成功。
blanks.why: 根据后句“Today, I'm a very confident and optimistic(乐观的) person.”可知, 我现在是一个自信乐观的人, 所以我的意外并没有阻止我获得成功。故选C。 阅读理解

title: The Meaning of True Friendship
text:
On my first day of the seventh grade. I noticed one little girl called Amy on the school bus. “Don’t talk to her,” Lauren said, who sat beside me. “Or they will make fun of you.”
Amy had many physical(身体的) differences - lots of {{1}} for other kids to make fun of her. Her eyes weren’t straight. Her glasses were an inch thick. And she had really ugly teeth.
Every day as we drove to and from school, kids would shout insults (侮辱) at Amy. “God, what a (n) {{2}} face! Stop looking at me!” “Mr. Rolland (the driver)! Amy took off her {{3}} and now her eyes are frightening me!”
For a while I shouted my share of insults, just so I’d would fit in, I didn’t want them to treat me the same way they treated Amy. But while I was insulting her, my heart {{4}} for the girl. I could see that the insults were making her look uglier, because she was so ashamed and alone. Then I wanted to stand up for her. I just didn’t know how to {{5}} my schoolmates until the night of our class roller-skating party.
Our whole class was there, including(包括) Amy. Amy didn’t know how to skate, but I could see how much she wanted to have fun like the rest of us. So I skated over to her and took her by the hand; we began the journey together around the skating rink (溜冰场). She just smiled, and sometimes she would laugh {{6}} .
On the school bus the next morning there was much news about Amy and me {{7}} together, but nobody insulted her or me. And they didn’t do that for the rest of the year.
After graduation, I never heard from Amy again. However, I never forget her and I’ve always {{8}} if I changed her life for the better. But I know for sure she changed my life. After becoming her friend, I no longer tried to impress (给……留下印象) people by trying to act like them. I became myself.

blanks.mean: 艾米有很多生理上的缺陷——这给了其他孩子取笑她的理由。
blanks.why: 根据“Her eyes weren’t straight. Her glasses were an inch thick. And she had really ugly teeth.”可知, 这些应该是孩子们取笑她的理由。故选A。 14题详解】 句意：天啊, 多可怕的一张脸！别再看我了！ pretty漂亮的；common普遍的；terrible可怕的；lovely美丽的。根据文章中的句子“Her eyes weren’t straight. Her glasses were an inch thick. And she had really ugly teeth.”她的眼睛斜视。她的眼镜片有一英

blanks.mean: 艾米摘下眼镜, 现在她的眼睛吓到我了！
blanks.why: 根据上文的句子“Her glasses were an inch thick.”她的眼镜有一英寸厚。以及句子“now her eyes are frightening me!” 现在她的眼睛吓到我了！可以推知我是在艾米摘下眼镜后被吓到的！故选D。

blanks.mean: 但当我侮辱她时, 我的心为那个女孩而痛。
blanks.why: 根据下文的句子“Then I wanted to stand up for her.”然后我想站出来支持她。可以推知, 作者在侮辱她时, 他的心是痛的, 因为她本不想侮辱艾米。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我只是不知道如何阻止我的同学, 直到我们班举行轮滑派对的晚上。
blanks.why: 根据“I could see that the insults were making her look uglier, because she was so ashamed and alone. Then I wanted to stand up for her.”我看得出来, 这些侮辱使她看起来更丑了, 因为她感到羞愧和孤独。然后我想站出来支持她。可以推知我是想阻止同学侮辱艾米。应该选择stop阻止；符合语境。故选B。

blanks.mean: 她只是微笑, 有时她会开心地笑。
blanks.gloss: happily快乐地；quietly安静地；quickly迅速地；secretly秘密地。
blanks.why: 结合句子“She just smiled.”她只是微笑。可以推知有时她会开心地笑。因此选择happily快乐地；符合语境。故选A。

blanks.mean: 第二天早上在校车上有很多关于艾米和我一起滑冰的消息, 但是没有人侮辱她或我。
blanks.why: 根据“So I skated over to her and took her by the hand; we began the journey together around the skating rink (溜冰场).” 于是我溜到她跟前, 拉着她的手, 在溜冰场里滑了起来。可知, 在校车上有很多关于艾米和我一起滑冰的消息。故选C。

blanks.mean: 然而, 我从未忘记她, 我一直想弄明白我是否更好地改变了她的生活。
blanks.why: 根据“However, I never forget her and I’ve always 8 if I changed her life for the better.”然而, 我从未忘记她, 我一直 _______ 我是否更好地改变了她的生活。可知, 应该选择wondered想弄明白；符合语境。故选C。 【点睛】完形填空题与单项选择题不同, 它给出的是一篇意思较为完整的短文。做该题型试题时, 首先应跳过空格通读全文, 以全文为背景, 联系句子的上下文进行推理和判断, 从4个选项中选出一项进行试填。考生可以从词义用法、固定搭配、逻辑推理和上下文的联系等方面去考虑。最后应再把全文通览一遍, 细心

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

Brenda Bongos was a happy, artistic girl. She had one big dream—to play the drums in a band. But one big problem lay in her way. To be good enough to play in a band, Brenda had to {{1}} a lot, but she lived next-door to a lot of old people. Many of them were sick. She knew that the sound of beating drums would really make them {{2}} . So, she had tried playing in the strangest places: a basement(地下室), a kitchen, and even in a shower. However, there was always someone it would annoy(打扰). To practice as much as she could, Brenda spent most of her time playing on books and boxes, and looking for new places to practice.
One day, while watching a science documentary on TV, she {{3}} that sound cannot travel in space, because there's no air. At that moment, Brenda Bongos decided to become a sort of musical astronaut.
With the help of a lot of time, books and work, Brenda {{4}} a space bubble. This was a big glass ball connected to a machine which sucked out(吸出)all the air inside. Only a set of drums and a chair would be {{5}} inside the bubble. Brenda also made herself a space suit. She put on the suit, entered the bubble, turned on the {{6}} , and played those drums like a wild child.
Soon Brenda Bongos became very famous. Many people came to see her play in her space bubble. Then she came out of the bubble and started giving concerts. As her fame(名气)spread {{7}} , the government suggested that she should be part of a special space journey.
Finally, Brenda was a real musical astronaut, and had gone far beyond her first dream of playing drums in a band.
Years later, when asked how she had achieved all this, she thought for a moment, and said: "If those old people next-door hadn't mattered so much to me, I wouldn't have found a(an) {{8}} , and none of this would have ever happened. "In the face of difficulties, Brenda showed her kindness, she worked hard and never stopped trying.

title: A Family Lesson
text:
A Family Lesson

"We have to let him try it, Lila," I said to my wife. "Can't you see that?"
"But how will he {{1}} on his own?"
"He'll make it."
"But he can't see he's blind!"
"I know it."
Of course I knew it. I'm Andy's father, aren't I? But I also knew how much it hurt Lila to say that. It was years before I heard her accept it. She knew it and had been told it over and over by all the {{2}} at the hospitals we had taken Andy to when we were still hoping during the early years.
"Lila," I tried again, "he's nineteen years old. He's clever. He's ambitious. He's {{3}} -he believes in himself. He wants to try things on his own. We've given him what we can. We have to let him go."
"But why does he have to {{4}} a college halfway across the country?"
"Because he wants to test his wings."
"That's all very well, " she continued to protest (抗议), "but he cannot see. How do we know he can fly on his own?"
"I think he can," I said softly. "And we have to let him {{5}} . He'll come back sometimes." We were both silent for a while.
"Remember Gertie, the bird we saved?" I asked.
"Yes," Lila nodded. "I remember Gertie."
"And we let her use her wings, didn't we?"
Lila {{6}} again.
"Even though she had broken her wing; even though you wanted to hold onto her; even though she was disabled too in a way, and we were {{7}} she might not make it, we still let her test her wings."
"Yes."
"And she did come back, didn't she? Not only that spring, but for several springs, and a couple of falls, too."
"But never to stay."
"No. Never to stay," I agreed. "And that's the {{8}} it is with children too, once they're grown and gone."
There were tears in Lila's eyes again, but her voice was firm (坚定的) as she stood up.
"Let's go find Andy. We'll tell him he can go and test his wings."

blanks.mean: 但他自己怎么能行呢？
blanks.why: 根据上文“We have to let him try it, Lila,” I said to my wife.可知, “我”对Lila说要让他去尝试, 而Lila比较担心, 怕他做不了。故选A。

blanks.mean: 他知道这一点, 早年我们还抱着希望的时候, 我们带Andy去的医院里, 所有的医生都一遍又一遍地告诉他。
blanks.why: 根据空后…at the hospitals可知, 这里指“医院里的医生告诉……”。故选B。

blanks.mean: 他很自信——他相信自己。
blanks.why: 根据空后 “he believes in himself”“他相信自己”可知, 他是自信的。故选B。

blanks.mean: 但是为什么他要选择一所横跨半个国家的大学呢？
blanks.why: 根据上下文语境 “He wants to try things on his own……. Because he wants to test his wings.”可知, Andy想要自己去尝试, 所以他“选择”了一所很远的大学。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们必须让他试一试。
blanks.why: 根据上文 “He wants to try things on his own. We've given him what we can. We have to let him go.”可知, Andy想要去尝试, “我”觉得必须让他去试一试。故选D。

blanks.mean: Lila再次点了点头。
blanks.why: 根据上文“Yes,” Lila nodded.“Lila点了点头”可知, 这里说Lila又点了点头。故选B。

blanks.mean: ……而且我们担心她做不到。
blanks.why: 根据上文“Even though it had broken her wing; even though you wanted to hold onto her; even though she was disabled too in a way”可知, 这只鸟翅膀折了, 所以我们担心她做不到。故选B。

blanks.mean: 一旦孩子们长大了, 离开了, 他们也会这样。
blanks.why: 根据文意可知, “我”用曾经救过鸟举例, 告诉Lila孩子长大了, 也会像那只鸟那样离开大人们。the way it is with…“……也是这样, 是同一个道理”。故选B。 【点睛】这是一篇记叙文, 短文中“我”和Lila在谈论如何处理失明的Andy选择去很远的地方上大学这件事。文章通过叙事给我们讲述道理, 内容贴近日常生活。本题考查学生们在具体语境中运用语言的能力, 综合性较强。做题时, 应先通读短文, 了解大意；然后根据上下文语境做题, 先易后难。注意空前后的固定搭配, 并仔细辨析选项中单词的意思和用法；最后将答案代入原文, 再读一遍, 检查答案是否正确。例如第7小题, 根据上文“Even

title: The Value of a First Painting
text:
Our community library decided to offer a painting class. I told my friend Ella, and we both signed up.

On the big day, our first {{1}} was to paint a white vase of cheerful yellow sunflowers against a blue background.
We were asked to paint our canvas (画布) {{2}} . It was easy to follow the instructor to move the brush. Although I had never painted before, I could tell I was a {{3}} . I started thinking about where I would hang my new masterpiece.
Immediately after that, however, I began to run into {{4}} . The first curved (弯曲的) line of my vase looked perfect, but when I painted the line on the opposite side, my hand slipped (打滑). I tried to {{5}} that white streak (条痕) with blue paint, but it didn’t work.
While I was busy fixing my messy painting, the instructor explained how to paint the sunflower leaves. Things went downhill fast after that. My leaves looked like fat, green caterpillars (毛毛虫). When I failed to clean my paintbrush, I accidentally made the sunflowers green. I felt {{6}} when I saw how good everyone else’s paintings looked.
Ella sweetly praised my sunflowers, perhaps feeling sorry for me. When I said that hers were much better, she looked surprised. “No, they’re not. I messed up in at least five places.” After a few seconds, she asked, “Want to {{7}} paintings?”
Until that moment I had felt only dislike for my painting. And yet for some reason, giving it away felt wrong. It wasn’t a perfect painting, but it was mine—the first one I had ever created. I knew Ella must have realized that she felt the same way when she suddenly shook her head and said. “Never mind.”
My sunflower painting still hangs directly above my bed. I often look at it. Every time I look at it. I {{8}} . It always brightens my day and brings warmth to my room. I really like it now.

blanks.mean: 在这个重要的日子里, 我们的第一个任务是在蓝色的背景上画一个白色的花瓶, 里面装着欢快的黄色向日葵。
blanks.why: 根据“to paint a white vase of cheerful yellow sunflowers against a blue background”可知这是个任务。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我们被要求把画布涂成蓝色。
blanks.gloss: white白色的；blue蓝色的；yellow黄色的；green绿色的。
blanks.why: 根据“against a blue background”可知背景用蓝色。故选B。

blanks.mean: 虽然我以前从未画过画, 但我看得出我是个天生的画家。
blanks.gloss: beginner初学者；performer表演者；failure失败；natural有天赋的人。
blanks.why: 根据“I started thinking about where I would hang my new masterpiece.”可知被告知是个有画画天赋的人。故选D。

blanks.mean: 然而, 在那之后不久, 我开始遇到问题。
blanks.why: 根据“The first curved (弯曲的) line of my vase looked perfect, but when I painted the line on the opposite side, my hand slipped (打滑).”可知开始出问题。故选C。

blanks.mean: 我试着用蓝颜料盖住那条白色的条纹, 但没有用。
blanks.why: 根据“but when I painted the line on the opposite side, my hand slipped (打滑).”可知没有画好, 试图用颜料把线覆盖了。故选A。

blanks.mean: 当我看到别人画得那么好时, 我感到很沮丧。
blanks.gloss: confused困惑的；afraid害怕的；bored无聊的；upset难过的。
blanks.why: 根据“When I failed to clean my paintbrush, I accidentally made the sunflowers green.”可知自己的画没画好, 看到别人画得好, 感到沮丧。故选D。
